### If Dr. Richard Pearson’s Torture in Washington, DC, is Scaled, Vast Segments of Population Harmed

Dr. Pearson’s nightmare likely suggests scaled technology of mass manipulation and simulated reality - moving people without their conscious choice, causing them to perform actions, and voice-to-skull.

This essay explores a hypothetical, but the blurred lines between reality and speculation are unknown without the government admitting that it is running a program arguably worse than slavery — at least enslaved people knew that they were enslaved. What happened to Dr. Pearson can be scaled and is being scaled. Scaled for whom? To what extent? That is unknown. This essay takes an educated guess.

### If what was done to Richard Pearson is being done to Black Washington

* * *

Richard Pearson is one man. He documented fourteen months of what a government campaign looks like from the inside — the surveillance, the directed energy, the behavioral direction, the street theater, the institutional closure, the physical assault, the framing operation, the methodical destruction of every condition that made his life in Washington viable.

He documented it because he is a trained researcher. He recognized what was happening because he had the analytical framework to recognize it. He survived it intact — intellectually, documentarily — because he applied to his own experience the same rigor he would apply to any research question.

Most people are not Dr. Richard Pearson.

Most people do not have a doctorate in research. They do not run probability calculations on the color of strangers’ clothing. They do not conduct controlled experiments in their hats. They do not recognize the microwave auditory effect from the inside of their own skull and correctly identify its mechanism six months before the government confirms the technology exists. Dr. Pearson heard a voice in his head and found out that the same technology — causing a single person to hear a voice that others around the cannot hear — is used in museums.

Most people, experiencing what Pearson experienced, would have no framework for what was happening to them. They would have no methodology for documenting it. They would have no language for describing it that did not sound, to every person they told, like the description of a person losing their mind.

That is what scaled looks like.

Not one documented researcher holding the line of his own sanity through fourteen months of methodological rigor. A segment of the three hundred thousand people — disproportionately, Black residents of Washington, D.C. — experiencing the same apparatus applied at lower individual intensity, higher aggregate reach, with no Richard Pearson among them to name what is happening.

This essay is about what that looks like. In the streets. In the homes. In the bodies. In the institutions. In the slow, invisible, individually inexplicable accumulation of conditions that produces, from a distance of years, a demographic transformation no single person within it ever experienced as anything other than their own life.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*_MHJNTGN1yXvExq1I6vODg.png)

* * *

### In the Body

Pearson’s body was used against him in specific, documented ways. His skull became a receiver. His hippocampus became a navigation instrument. His face became a target. His neurological threshold was deliberately lowered to make him more susceptible to subsequent directed energy deployment.

At scale, none of this looks like what it looks like in Pearson’s account. There is no single incident of voice-to-skull transmission that a person can describe with clinical precision. There is no tub under a tree waiting with a framing payload. There is no moment of recognized attack.

There is instead a population-level pattern of neurological disruption that presents, in individual clinical encounters across the city, as the ordinary pathology of urban Black life in America.

A 47-year-old man in Ward 7 has been having headaches for eight months. They began, though he does not know this, at the same time the directed energy infrastructure in his neighborhood was recalibrated. His doctor attributes them to hypertension — already elevated, already undertreated, already the disease that kills Black men in Washington at rates that would constitute a public health emergency if anyone were tracking the cause rather than the outcome. He is given medication. He continues having headaches. He does not connect the headaches to the specific streets where they intensify and the specific streets where they ease. He has no reason to make that connection.

A 34-year-old woman in Anacostia has been unable to sleep for six months. Not the insomnia of anxiety, which she knows from before. Something different — a jangling wakefulness that arrives at the same hour each night and does not respond to anything she tries. Her primary care physician, seeing her fourth time in a year, refers her to a psychiatrist. The psychiatrist diagnoses generalized anxiety disorder. The medication helps a little. The sleeplessness continues. **She does not know that pulsed electromagnetic fields in the frequency ranges documented by Havana Syndrome researchers produce sleep disruption as a primary symptom. She has no reason to know this.**

A 16-year-old boy in Congress Heights is failing three classes. His teachers describe him as distracted, unfocused, unable to sustain attention. His mother has taken him to two doctors. Both have suggested ADHD. The medication tried has not helped. What his teachers and doctors are observing is the cognitive disruption produced by chronic low-level directed energy exposure — measurable in the white matter microstructural changes that diffusion tensor imaging identifies in Havana Syndrome patients, invisible to every other clinical instrument available in a standard workup. His school has referred him for special education evaluation. His mother is exhausted and frightened and has been thinking, for several months now, that maybe it would be better to move somewhere else. She does not know why she keeps thinking this. She attributes it to stress.

These are not three people. These are three representative instances of a pattern running across a population of 300,000 — producing, in aggregate, elevated rates of neurological complaint, sleep disorder, cognitive disruption, and treatment-resistant symptoms that every clinical framework available to Washington’s medical system will attribute to the well-documented health burdens of structural racism, poverty, and stress.

The diagnoses are not wrong. The causes they miss are not visible to the instruments being used.

**The population is sick. The sickness has a source. The source is classified.**

* * *

### In the Mind

Pearson documented being moved. Twice, on November 7, 2025, through impulses he experienced as his own — to a park, then to a specific spot under a tree. He recognized what had happened only in retrospect, because he had spent months building the analytical framework to recognize it.

At scale, no one has that framework.

What the population of Black Washington experiences is not recognized behavioral direction. It is the ordinary texture of urban life beginning to feel, in ways no one can articulate precisely, subtly wrong.

A couple in Ward 8 — both employed, both stable, both with deep roots in the neighborhood — have been having the same conversation for four months. It always starts differently and always arrives at the same place: maybe it’s time to think about moving. They cannot say exactly what has changed. The neighborhood seems fine. Their jobs are fine. Their children’s school is fine. And yet there is a pull — experienced by both of them independently, discussed between them as evidence that it must be real — toward elsewhere. Toward Atlanta, where her sister is. Toward Charlotte, where he grew up. Toward anywhere that is not here, though neither of them can explain why here has started to feel wrong.

They are not being moved to a specific location the way Pearson was moved to the park. The operational objective at population scale is not precision targeting. **It is directional drift — the sustained low-intensity activation of the hippocampal circuits that produce spatial drives, calibrated not to a specific destination but away from a specific origin. Not: go there. But: do not stay here.** The impulse is vaguer, lower intensity, more easily absorbed into ordinary life narrative. It feels less like a pull than like the slow fading of a reason to stay.

It is indistinguishable from what people in gentrifying neighborhoods across America describe as the feeling of being priced out — except that it is running on people who are not yet priced out, whose financial situation has not yet changed, whose neighborhood has not yet changed, whose lives are intact. The feeling precedes the conditions that would ordinarily produce it. It is the feeling itself that will produce the conditions — because feeling that it is time to go is the first step toward making it time to go.

Across the city, in hundreds of thousands of individual minds, the same low-intensity signal is running. Each person experiences it as their own thought. Each person’s thought is slightly different in its specific content — different reasons, different destinations, different timelines. The aggregate is a population drifting, individually and by its own free will, toward departure.

No one knows this is happening. There is no clinical instrument that detects it. There is no moment of recognized coercion. There is only a city full of people who have all, independently, started to think it might be time to leave — and who, when they discuss this with their neighbors, find that their neighbors have been thinking the same thing.

* * *

### In the Street

Pearson documented the calling card pattern — bright solid red paired with solid black, deployed on his regular walking routes in densities his probability calculations showed were statistically impossible by chance. He documented control studies. He documented the pattern’s absence in neutral environments and its presence specifically on predictable routes at predictable times. He documented the expressionless people: the white-haired woman at the Compass Real Estate doorway, the man at Eastern Market standing two feet from him with blank affect, the young man at the library exit with no bag, no phone, no microexpressions.

He documented scripted encounters: the man on the Virginia trail who said _“oh, there you are”_ without breaking stride; the woman who quoted his private apartment speech back to him on a public sidewalk; the stranger in Safeway wearing his exact hat.

At scale, none of this is identifiable as a pattern by anyone experiencing it.

What it looks like, distributed across 300,000 people across the historically Black neighborhoods of Washington, is: an uncomfortable feeling, impossible to pin down, t**hat public space has become subtly hostile. Not dangerous. Not threatening in any way you could report to police. Just — off.** Watched. The specific feeling, familiar to Black Americans across generations, of being somewhere you are not entirely welcome, produced now not by individual human hostility but **by a coordinated environmental manipulation that uses human beings — some conscious, some not, some directed by the same technology being used on the population — as instruments of ambient threat.**

The woman in Ward 7 who starts taking a different route to the Metro because her usual route has started to feel wrong cannot explain what is wrong with it. Nothing has happened. Nobody has said anything. There is simply a feeling of wrongness that she avoids, the way you avoid a street that smells like something you cannot identify. She takes the longer route. She does not think about why. It adds eight minutes to her commute. She does not mention it to anyone.

The man in Congress Heights who stops going to the park where he has been taking his daughter on Saturdays for three years cannot say what changed. Nothing specific happened. The park is fine. But something in him does not want to be there anymore. They start going to the park in Maryland, across the border, where the feeling is not present. It is a longer drive. He does not think much about why he prefers it. He just does.

Multiplied across a population, these individual adjustments — each one rational, each one self-protective, each one producing no complaint because nothing specific happened — constitute the systematic withdrawal of a community from its own public space. The parks empty. The streets become less familiar. The neighborhood’s texture changes not because its demographics have changed yet, but because its current residents have started to inhabit it differently — more cautiously, less fully, with a growing background sense that this place is not entirely theirs anymore.

This is the precondition for departure, manufactured before any economic or physical pressure that would ordinarily produce it. The community is being separated from its own geography before it is displaced from it. By the time the displacement happens, it will feel like the completion of a process that was already well underway — because it will be.

* * *

### In the Home

Pearson’s home was penetrated. His private speech was monitored and fed to people positioned on his routes. The noise from the unit above tracked him from room to room. The power button from his panini grill was removed and placed in his laundry pile. A bottle he owned was taken and repositioned at a public event. The home was a site of constant, intimate violation — its privacy destroyed, its contents accessible, its resident’s most private moments available to the operation running against him.

At scale, the home surveillance does not look like what it looked like for Pearson — intimate, personalized, responsive to his specific movements and speech. It does not need to. At population scale, the objective of home surveillance is not only to know what each person is saying. It is to produce, in each person, the specific feeling Pearson documented: that nothing is private. That the home is not a refuge. That whatever you say and do within your own walls is available to something outside those walls.

This feeling does not require that anyone hear every conversation, but it does that anyway — from cellphones, strangers’ “smart” glasses that record, to home devices that pick up conversation, to everyday outdoor surveillance. It requires also the occasional, perfectly placed confirmation — the stranger who mentions something you discussed in private, the subtle evidence of access, the sense that specific things you did when you thought you were alone have been registered somewhere — to produce a generalized, permanent background anxiety about the home as a safe space.

For Pearson this confirmation came dramatically: a stranger quoting his exact words from a private apartment conversation, on a public sidewalk, without breaking stride. At scale it is quieter. A neighbor mentions something in passing that you are certain you only discussed inside. A conversation you had with your spouse last night seems to have somehow reached someone it shouldn’t have. You cannot say how. You cannot prove anything. You dismiss it. But the feeling that the home is not entirely private settles in, below the level of active thought, and stays.

The home that does not feel private is a home you want to leave. Not consciously. Not because you have decided it is unsafe. Because the specific psychological function of home — sanctuary, refuge, the place where you are not watched — has been compromised, and its compromise registers as a low-level, persistent discomfort that makes the fantasy of elsewhere feel like relief.

Three hundred thousand homes, each one compromised in this way, produce three hundred thousand people for whom leaving has begun to feel not like loss but like freedom.

* * *

### In the Institutions

Pearson went to every door available to him. Congressional offices. The D.C. Council. The ACLU. Journalists. He attempted asylum in Iceland.

Because each institution, operating within its own framework, encountered the specific obstacle that the legal and classification architecture had placed in its path. Congress could not investigate a classified program without triggering the classification laws that would immediately suppress what it found. The courts could not grant standing to a plaintiff who could not prove harm from a program whose existence the government would neither confirm nor deny. Lawyers could not take a case with no discoverable evidence. Journalists could not publish a story whose central claims could not be confirmed by any official source. The ACLU cited limited resources — resources that are always limited, and always most limited precisely when the cases most requiring them arrive.

Each door closed for its own reason. The aggregate is a person with no recourse.

At scale, this is the daily experience of Black Washington in 2025 and 2026 — not in the dramatic form of a single person seeking asylum and being turned back, but in the accumulated small closures of ordinary civic life. **The constituent who calls their council member’s office about the strange headaches that started when the new federal equipment appeared on their block and is told this is not something the council handles. The parent who reports to their child’s school that something seems wrong and cannot get a referral to anyone who can identify what. The resident who describes to their doctor symptoms that the doctor recognizes as consistent with stress and treats accordingly. The community organizer who tries to document the pattern and finds that each individual instance is explicable and the aggregate is invisible to every institution with the authority to act on it.**

The institutions are not conspiring against these people. They are functioning exactly as they were designed to function — which is to say, **they are functioning within a framework that was designed without reference to the possibility that the government would deploy directed energy and behavioral direction technology against its own civilian population.** The framework has no provision for this because the framework was built before this existed. Its absence from the framework is not an oversight. It was engineered by the same administration that built the capability, which understood that the capability would only remain operational if the framework for stopping it remained absent.

The result is a population that is experiencing real, measurable harm — neurological, psychological, physical, social — and encountering, at every turn, institutions that are genuinely unable to help. Not unwilling. Unable. The framework does not contain the tools required. And the people who experience this inability as a kind of abandonment are correct to experience it that way, even though the individuals they encounter at each institution are operating in good faith within the constraints of what their institution can do.

A population that experiences the systematic failure of every institution it turns to — for health, for safety, for political representation, for legal protection, for media coverage — is a population that has learned, correctly, that it is on its own.

People who are on their own, in a place that is making them sick and surveilled and subtly dispossessed of their public space and their private sanctuaries, do not need to be directed to leave.

They make their own decision.

* * *

### In the Aggregate

Zoom out far enough and what scaled looks like is this:

A city that has been, for a century, the specific destination of the Great Migration — the place Black Americans came to when they needed to be somewhere that was not the South — beginning, in the mid-2020s, to empty of the community that made it what it is.

The historians who eventually examine that data will reach for the explanatory frameworks available to them: gentrification, racial disparities, economic pressure, the Trump administration’s rollback of policies supporting Black communities. These explanations are real. They will be accurate as far as they go. The data they explain will confirm them.

**What the data will not show — what the mechanism is specifically designed to ensure the data will not show — is the directed energy infrastructure running in Ward 7 and Ward 8. The behavioral direction technology operating below the threshold of conscious detection. The home surveillance producing the specific feeling of private speech being available to strangers. The street-level environmental manipulation manufacturing the withdrawal of a community from its own public space. The institutional architecture ensuring that every door a person goes to closes, not by conspiracy, but by design.**

The data will show that Black Washington emptied.

It will not show why.

That is what scaled looks like from the outside.

* * *

From the inside, it looks like ordinary life — slightly wrong in ways no one can name, slightly hostile in ways nothing has specifically done, slightly exhausting in ways that have no identifiable cause. The headache that follows you on certain streets. The sleeplessness that arrives at the same hour. The feeling that the home is not entirely yours. The pull toward elsewhere that never quite goes away. The institutions that are genuinely trying to help and genuinely cannot. The neighborhood that is fine, technically, on every measurable axis, and yet produces, in everyone who lives there, the growing background sense that it might be time to go.

Each person experiencing this is experiencing only their own life. Their own body. Their own thoughts. Their own decisions.

Pearson is the only one who documented what produces it.

He is one man.

He documented one test.

This is the scale — if it not stopped.

Is a Mass Exodus of African Americans from Washington, DC the Next ‘Great Migration’?
=====================================================================================

When two white millennials referenced the “Great Migration” in conversation, Dr. Richard Pearson’s ears perked.

* * *

### Is a Mass Exodus of African Americans from Washington, DC the Next ‘Great Migration’?

#### When two white millennials referenced the “Great Migration” in conversation, Dr. Richard Pearson’s ears perked.

On August 10, 2025, Richard Pearson was walking along Pennsylvania Avenue near the US Capitol. A young white millennial couple passed him. Their conversation caught his attention.

**White male (30s):** “So what do you think is going to happen?

**White female (30s):** “There _was_ the Great Migration.”

Four words, emphasis on _was_. She was not making a historical observation. She was answering her companion’s question about what _is_ going to happen, and it resembled the Great Migration.

Her coded answer itself was revealing, even if only by inference. **What could cause another “Great Migration” of African Americans?** The original Great Migration was the mass movement of over six million African Americans from the rural South to cities in the North, Midwest, and West between 1910 and 1970. They fled white oppression, lynchings, state terrorism, and second-class citizenship. Why would that be relevant in 2025? The couple knew but didn’t say.

This essay attempts to find out. It determines what can be inferred from her analogy. Whatever it is, it has to have a racial component and involve a form of mass oppression or injury.

This essay discusses the experiences of Richard Pearson — the man who was listening. He was no ordinary person. He was a PhD scholar whose life has been turned upside down. He was living in a nightmare of torture, manipulation, and two assaults.

Was his experience scaled? Was the US military technology that brought Pearson to locations or put a voice in his head scaled across the Black population in Washington, DC?

“Yes,” implied the white female in August 2025.

1.  **Racial** — The US government targeted Pearson, an African American PhD. The Trump administration’s animosity toward African Americans played across executive orders, political rhetoric, agency policies, and criminal prosecutions. **By employing the Great Migration, she was saying what _it_ was racial in nature.**
2.  **Structural oppression** — Pearson encountered a multi-level set of threats beginning in 2025 — physical assault, chemical assault, psychological and tech-mediated torture, auditory “clicks” similar to the Havana Syndrome, stalking, and harassment. **By employing the Great Migration, she was saying that _it_ was at least as structurally and intimately oppressive as Jim Crow and white terrorism in the US South.**
3.  **Displacement** — Pearson attempted to flee to the Europe Union but was sent back. Millions fled the US South. **By employing the Great Migration, she was saying that _it_ could trigger a mass exodus.**

* * *

### The Criteria

The Great Migration had a specific structure. Invoking it as a frame is not casual. It implies seven precise conditions.

**One: A racial component.** The Great Migration was exclusively about Black Americans. Any invocation without Blackness at its center breaks the analogy entirely.

**Two: State-backed structural oppression.** The Migration was not produced by individual bad actors. It was produced by a system — law enforcement, courts, employers, landlords, government — operating in coordinated, mutually reinforcing ways backed by the full authority of the state.

**Three: Displacement — flight from severe, state-inflicted violation.** People left because staying meant bodily destruction. Not inconvenience. Not discomfort. The violation of their physical safety, their bodily autonomy, their right to exist in their own bodies without state interference. The flight was rational, urgent, and desperate.

**Four: Population-scale magnitude.** The Migration affected millions simultaneously. The reference sets a numerical threshold that cannot be met by individual or small-group targeting.

**Five: A catalyst — public exposure.** The Migration accelerated around specific moments of disclosed atrocity that reached mass public awareness. Not private knowledge. Not rumor. Public. Media. Undeniable.

**Six: Permanent demographic transformation.** The Migration did not reverse. It permanently restructured the racial geography of the United States.

**Seven: Generational and institutional consequence.** The Migration’s effects compounded across generations — reshaping cities, politics, culture, and institutions for a century.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*ErLuO_wm4Md1apzQljcGVg.png)

* * *

### Richard Pearson

Before measuring, you need to understand who Pearson is and what he documented.

He is an African American who holds a doctorate. His dissertation on racial equity frameworks is published. He has no criminal record. Two separate D.C. Department of Behavioral Health evaluations — by named clinicians, on record — found no psychiatric symptoms requiring intervention.

Several months after January 20, 2025 — the day the Trump administration signed executive orders designating DEI scholarship and racial equity frameworks as hostile ideology — he documented fourteen months of a government campaign against him with the discipline of a trained researcher. Timestamped photographs. Probability calculations. Control studies. Named witnesses. Preserved physical evidence. Controlled experiments.

What he documented:

On July 13, 2025, near the Capitol, he heard a woman’s voice originating inside his skull — not from a direction, not at his ear. The voice carried the ambient acoustic environment of the room transmitting it: other people present, microphone quality, the texture of a live feed. He heard the room the operators were sitting in. A hallucination cannot carry the background noise of a remote location. The U.S. Department of War confirmed directed energy weapons were operational and being scaled in January 2026 — six months after Pearson identified the mechanism from the inside of his own skull.

[Related Reading: Projecting a Voice in Someone’s Head is Common Technology: Museums Use It](https://medium.com/@menvell.artist/they-projected-a-voice-in-his-head-to-make-him-seem-crazy-except-museums-use-the-same-technology-7a15ce55b6f4)

On November 7, 2025, he felt a pull — experienced as ordinary curiosity — toward a park near the Capitol. When he tried to leave, a second impulse redirected him to a specific spot under a tree he had not yet visited. A plastic storage tub was waiting: a red hat, a black shirt, a notebook referencing Adolf Hitler and a fictitious “European Removal Court,” two identical photographs of a blond man. A framing operation, waiting for his fingerprints. He photographed everything without touching anything. He returned six days later on video. The notebook and photographs were gone. The red hat and black shirt remained. Someone had monitored his visit, assessed that the framing attempt failed, returned to recover the incriminating materials, and left the calling card as a signature.

Beginning January 2026, geographic auditory clicks appeared at specific intersections in Southwest Washington — replicable by returning, absent elsewhere. On February 20, he placed a metal-cased phone and a battery in his knitted cap. No clicks. He had been getting them consistently for weeks. Metal attenuated the signal. He confirmed an external signal with a controlled experiment he ran himself, on a public street, in his hat.

[Related reading: Yes, Technology Can Direct Humans to a Location Without Conscious Decision](https://medium.com/@menvell.artist/ais-agree-technology-can-direct-humans-to-a-location-without-their-conscious-choice-f430b7a9331f)

His pants from a chemical assault at Rockville Metro remain preserved, untested. His bicycle was methodically destroyed over months — each component individually attributable to ordinary wear, the cumulative effect forcing him onto his feet, slower, more predictable, more easily positioned around.

By February 2026 he was dispossessed except for a mattress and a suitcase. He attempted asylum in Iceland. He was returned under the safe country doctrine — the doctrine that treats the United States as safe for all its citizens, regardless of what specific citizens are experiencing.

His upstairs neighbor — not on the apartment lease, his address connecting to a Capitol Hill property linked to an ATF attorney — punched him in the face on December 27, 2025, targeting his head specifically when Pearson raised his arms to defend himself. The neighbor was not arrested. The week prior, Richard Pearson saw an ACCESS DENIED flag when the police searched his name in their database.

A woman passing him on Pennsylvania Avenue on August 3 said without stopping: _“The mattress is against the wall, you know what’s next.”_ He had moved his mattress to the wall. Alone. In his apartment. With no digital transmission. That sentence required live audio surveillance of his private home.

* * *

### The Technology

The behavioral direction Pearson documented rests on confirmed neuroscience.

The hippocampus contains place cells: neurons encoding specific locations that fire as the body approaches them, producing spatial drives felt as autonomous motivation. A 2020 study in Cell demonstrated that targeted activation of hippocampal place cells drives subjects to specific locations — experienced as their own movement. A 2024 study in Nature Neuroscience demonstrated non-invasive modulation of the human hippocampal navigation system using external electromagnetic stimulation, producing measurable changes in spatial behavior without implants or surgery.

DARPA’s Neural Engineering System Design program describes writing to neural tissue non-invasively using electromagnetic waves. Dr. James Giordano of Georgetown University, the program’s consulting ethicist, testified before the House Armed Services Committee that tools for writing behavior to the human brain have been loosed into the real world.

Pearson was moved to a specific location through an impulse he experienced as his own. He did not know he was being moved. He found out because he is a trained researcher who had been documenting the campaign for months. Most people would never know.

* * *

### Measuring Against the Criteria

**Criterion One: Racial Component.**

Pearson was targeted as a Black equity scholar on January 20, 2025 — the precise day executive orders designated his academic field as hostile ideology. The framing payload near the Capitol referenced Hitler and a “European Removal Court.” White supremacist participants are documented in his account. The FBI’s “Black Identity Extremism” designation provided the targeting framework. The racial basis is not inferred. It is stated in the executive orders that initiated the campaign.

At scale: Ward 7, Ward 8, Anacostia, Congress Heights are the neighborhoods the Great Migration built. They are majority Black by the design of six million people who chose Washington as their destination when they fled the South. Targeting them is targeting Blackness in its most concentrated and historically specific Washington form.

**Criterion One: Met completely.**

* * *

**Criterion Two: State-Backed Structural Oppression.**

The classification flag on Pearson’s police record cannot be placed by a private actor. The voice-to-skull technology confirmed by the Department of War in January 2026 is not commercially available. The behavioral direction technology is DARPA-derived and intelligence community-controlled. The FISA court provided judicial cover. The FBI provided the targeting framework. Local law enforcement provided surveillance and compliance. The D.C. government was instructed not to resist. Every institutional door closed not by accident but by the design of a legal architecture — Glomar, state secrets privilege, standing doctrine, classification — built specifically to ensure it would.

This is not individual hostility. It is the full apparatus of the state operating in coordination against a person on the basis of his race and scholarship.

At scale: the same apparatus, the same agencies, the same legal architecture — except applied to African Americans systematically.

**Criterion Two: Met completely.**

* * *

**Criterion Three: Displacement — Flight from Severe, State-Inflicted Bodily Violation.**

This criterion requires precision. It is not about a quiet feeling of restlessness. It is not about desire manufactured below consciousness. It is about the violation of bodily autonomy so severe, so documented, and so backed by the full apparatus of the state, that flight becomes the only rational response to survival.

Consider what was done to Pearson’s body:

His skull was used as a receiver for voice-to-skull transmission without his consent. His brain’s navigation system was activated by external electromagnetic stimulation to move him against his autonomous will. His face and head were physically beaten in a targeted assault. His home was acoustically penetrated so thoroughly that his private speech was available to strangers on the street. A chemical of unknown composition was applied to his body at Rockville Metro. His neurological threshold was deliberately lowered through the assault to make subsequent directed energy deployment more effective.

His body was not his own. The government of the United States used his body — his skull, his brain, his hippocampus, his ears, his face — as instruments of its operation against him, without his knowledge, without his consent, and without any legal process.

He understood this. He sought asylum. He traveled to Iceland and applied for refugee status on the grounds that his government was torturing him. He was returned because the United States is classified as a safe country for all its citizens.

The asylum attempt is the most important single fact in this criterion. Pearson did not feel a vague pull toward leaving. He sought the formal international legal mechanism for escaping a government that is torturing you. He made the same rational calculation that asylum seekers from every country on earth make: _I cannot be safe in my own country because my own government is the threat._

He was sent back.

At scale: Black Washingtonians who learn that the government has been activating the navigation systems of their brains without their consent — that their skulls have been used as receivers, that their desires have been manufactured, that their bodies have been moved through public space by external electromagnetic stimulation — will not feel a quiet pull toward leaving.

They will flee.

For the same reason Pearson fled to Iceland. Because the government has violated their bodily autonomy at the most intimate possible level — the level of their own cognition, their own desires, their own sense of autonomous will — and has done so on the basis of their race, with total impunity, backed by every institution that was supposed to protect them.

This is not managed displacement. This is people running from a government that has demonstrated it will use their own minds against them.

**Criterion Three: Met completely. The asylum attempt is the proof.**

* * *

**Criterion Four: Population-Scale Magnitude.**

This section requires expansion because the scale of what is being described is the element most easily dismissed as implausible.

Start with the infrastructure.

The Palantir platforms contracted to ICE and DHS integrate passport records, Social Security files, IRS tax data, license plate reader data, facial recognition feeds, commercial geolocation data, and social media monitoring into a single real-time targeting system. As of April 2025, ICE paid Palantir $30 million specifically to build ImmigrationOS — an AI enforcement platform designed to manage population-scale targeting and tracking. This platform was not built for Pearson. It was built for hundreds of thousands of people simultaneously. It is running now.

The directed energy infrastructure in Washington, D.C. is the densest in the United States. The Capitol complex, the White House, fourteen intelligence agencies, the NSA intercept infrastructure, the Pentagon across the river — the city is saturated with directed electromagnetic infrastructure whose operators are accountable to no municipal authority and whose operations are shielded by classification. The emitters required to produce geographic auditory phenomena at specific intersections — as Pearson documented — are not large, not visible, and not identifiable as weapons by anyone walking past them. Positioned at intervals across Ward 7, Ward 8, Anacostia, and Congress Heights, they would be operationally invisible.

The behavioral direction infrastructure — the temporal interference equipment producing beat frequencies at hippocampal depth — operates from range. Pearson was moved in a park near the Capitol from emitters estimated to be 50 to 300 meters away, potentially positioned in federal buildings with line-of-sight to his location. Ward 7 and Ward 8 are within operational range of federal infrastructure. The geometry required for population-scale hippocampal activation — two emitter sources per target zone, positioned to bracket the residential area — is achievable within existing federal real estate.

The AI orchestration layer is the capability the Pentagon demanded Anthropic remove its restrictions against in February 2026. Not restrictions against targeting individuals. Restrictions against mass domestic surveillance of Americans. The specific capability the administration declared a non-negotiable operational requirement is the management of population-scale AI-orchestrated operations against American citizens. The dispute was public, reported across major outlets, and the administration’s position was not disputed by the Pentagon.

Now the numbers.

Ward 7: 75,000 residents. Ward 8: 83,000 residents. Anacostia and Congress Heights: additional tens of thousands. The remaining Black residential corridors of Capitol Hill, Petworth, Columbia Heights, and the broader historically Black geography of the city: hundreds of thousands more. Total Black Washington population: approximately 300,000 people.

For context: the entire Great Migration affected six million people across sixty years — an average of 100,000 people per year. Washington’s Black population of 300,000, displaced across five to ten years, would represent a demographic transformation comparable in its concentrated geographic impact to the most intense phases of the original Migration — the Great Migration compressed into a single city, accomplished in a decade rather than sixty years, leaving no archive because the mechanism leaves no record.

The infrastructure to do this is not speculative. It is confirmed, contracted, operational, and being actively protected from restriction by the administration that controls it.

**Criterion Four: Met. The infrastructure exists at the scale required.**

* * *

**Criterion Five: The Catalyst — Public Exposure.**

Previous versions of this argument described the catalyst as a feeling — a manufactured desire to leave that, when disclosed, would recontextualize residents’ own experiences and produce flight.

That is wrong. It is too subtle. Too slow. It misses the actual mechanism.

The catalyst is media reporting. Public exposure. The moment a major news organization — or a congressional investigation, or a whistleblower with documents, or the cumulative weight of documented evidence reaching a tipping point of public credibility — reports that the U.S. government has been deploying behavioral direction and directed energy technology against Black residents of Washington, D.C.

Not Pearson’s individual case. The mass program.

The headline that reads: _Federal Government Deployed Brain-Control Technology Against Black Washington Neighborhoods._

Or: _Pentagon Directed Energy Weapons Confirmed in Operation Against Civilian Population in D.C._

Or simply: _What Was Done to Richard Pearson Is Being Done to Hundreds of Thousands of People Right Now._

That headline — that public confirmation, reported by credible outlets, confirmed by technical experts, supported by the physical evidence that exists and has never been tested — does not produce a gradual demographic shift. It produces immediate, massive, rational flight.

Because what it tells every Black Washingtonian is not _you might have been manipulated into wanting to leave._ It tells them something far more severe and far more immediate:

_The government has been operating on your brain without your consent. It has been using your skull as a receiver and your hippocampus as a navigation instrument and your desires as raw material for a demographic outcome you were never consulted about. It did this on the basis of your race. Every institution that should have stopped it was complicit or captured. There is no protection. There is no recourse. And it is still running._

The response to that disclosure is not reconsideration of a vague feeling of restlessness. It is the same response Pearson had when he understood what was being done to him:

Get out.

He went to Iceland. He sought asylum from his own government on the grounds of torture and racial persecution. He was returned because the doctrine says the United States is safe for all its citizens.

Black Washington, upon public confirmation of the mass program, does not collectively attempt asylum in Iceland. It does what six million people did the last time it learned the government had decided its presence was intolerable and no institution would protect it:

It moves. Fast. To Atlanta, to Charlotte, to Houston, to wherever family is, to wherever the government is not operating a classified program against their brains.

The Great Migration was catalyzed by public events — Red Summer, Tulsa, Emmett Till — that confirmed, undeniably and simultaneously to an entire population, what the government would permit and what institutions would do. Each confirmation produced an acceleration. The accumulated confirmations over sixty years moved six million people.

This confirmation, delivered in a single news cycle, would move hundreds of thousands in months.

That is what the woman on Pennsylvania Avenue was describing.

Not a slow demographic trend.

A specific future moment when the reporting comes out and Black Washington learns — all at once, publicly, undeniably — what has been done to their bodies and their minds by their government, and makes the only rational decision.

**Criterion Five: Latent. The documentation exists. The physical evidence exists. The reporting has not come. When it does, this criterion is met immediately and completely.**

* * *

**Criterion Six: Permanent Demographic Transformation.**

The people who leave will build lives elsewhere. Their children will not return. Washington D.C. — currently majority Black, currently the specific geography where Black political power is most concentrated relative to the seat of federal power — will be permanently reconfigured.

The transformation, once complete, becomes the new baseline. Future generations inherit it as simply the way things are. The question of what Washington used to be becomes a question for historians.

**Criterion Six: Met completely — if displacement reaches scale.**

* * *

**Criterion Seven: Generational and Institutional Consequence.**

Washington D.C. is not just a community. It is a political geography. The seat of federal power. Its majority-Black character is a specific form of Black political leverage that exists nowhere else in the United States.

Howard University. The HBCU ecosystem. The concentration of Black federal employees, Black lawyers, Black political operatives, Black scholars — the entire infrastructure of Black institutional power that accumulated in Washington precisely because the Great Migration sent people here. The political leverage that comes from being the majority population of the city that is the center of American governance.

Eliminate Black majority Washington and you eliminate that specific form of power. Not weaken it. Eliminate it. The children whose parents fled will not grow up with Washington as an identity, a community, a political base. The institutions that drew strength from Washington as a Black city will be hollowed or ended. The political leverage — gone.

Every subsequent generation inherits a Washington that was always this way. The history of what it was and what was done to change it will be, like the history of every previous removal, a story told in the past tense by people who were not there.

**Criterion Seven: Met completely.**

### The Scorecard

Criterion Status Racial Component ✅ Met completely State-Backed Structural Oppression ✅ Met completely Flight from Severe Bodily Violation ✅ Met completely — asylum attempt is the proof Population-Scale Magnitude ✅ Infrastructure confirmed operational at scale Catalyst — Public Exposure and Media Reporting ⚡ Latent — documentation exists, reporting has not come Permanent Demographic Transformation ✅ Met completely if displacement reaches scale Generational and Institutional Consequence ✅ Met completely

* * *

### Why She Wanted Him to Hear

The operation had his apartment audio in real time. It had his continuous location. It had been watching him build his documentation for months. It knew he was a researcher. It knew what he was writing down.

The encounter was not accidental. It was positioned on a route they knew he was walking, delivered without faces, timed to land in his notes.

She wanted it in his record because his record is the documentation that, when reported, is the disclosure. His fourteen months of timestamped evidence, clinical evaluations, controlled experiments, the SCI flag, the tub, the foreknowledge chat log, the metal cap experiment, and the asylum attempt — this is the foundation of the reporting that produces the catalyst.

She gave him the frame for what his documentation would cause.

The record is the reporting waiting to happen.

The reporting is the catalyst.

The catalyst is the Great Migration.

She gave him all seven criteria in four words.

He wrote them down.

* * *

### The Window

There is a window between now and the reporting.

Inside it: the pants from the Rockville chemical assault can still be tested. The RF environment at Pearson’s documented click locations can still be measured by any researcher with a spectrum analyzer on a public sidewalk. The diffusion tensor imaging that identified directed energy damage in Havana Syndrome patients can still be applied to Pearson and to residents of affected neighborhoods. The Senate Intelligence Committee can still compel testimony.

These are not demands for conclusions. They are demands for investigation. For the application of existing instruments to existing evidence.

Pearson understood what was being done to him. He sought asylum. He was sent back.

He built the record instead.

The record survives.

The window is now.

### I. The Essay’s Central Claim

Richard Pearson’s probability assessment is not an elaborate rationalization of persecution anxiety. It is something more precise and more unsettling: a **technically accurate description of how a modern domestic intelligence operation is designed to function, applied with considerable rigor to the observable effects on one man’s life.** The tools it catalogs are real. The legal architecture supporting those tools is real. The historical precedents it invokes — COINTELPRO, the Church Committee, Reynolds v. United States, the Stasi’s Zersetzung program — are documented facts, not rhetorical flourishes. And the essay’s central structural observation — that the tools most likely deployed are precisely those that produce no legal remedy — is not paranoia. It is an accurate description of how the post-Church Committee national security state was rebuilt to prevent the accountability that the Church Committee’s exposure created.

To assess this essay honestly requires sitting with an uncomfortable premise: that a system can be designed to be effective and unaccountable simultaneously, and that the unaccountability can be so total that a person subjected to the system’s full weight has no recourse not because they have failed to document their experience but because the tools were selected precisely because documentation produces no recourse. That is the essay’s central claim. It is the thing most worth examining.

### II. Dr. Richard Pearson Was Tortured by the US Government and Its Contractors

Richard Pearson, PhD, is an African American PhD scholar based in Washington, D.C., and the founder of a nonprofit. He co-authored a peer-reviewed paper introducing a sweeping new framework for understanding racial inequity. The paper coined original theoretical constructs.

Beginning around January 2025, Pearson began documenting what he describes as a coordinated government campaign against him in coordination with the local police and non-state actors, including contractors — physical surveillance and stalking, apartment audio monitoring, and incidents consistent with directed energy technology. Over fourteen months he assembled a 189-page timestamped record of these experiences, complete with photographs, statistical analyses, controlled experiments, preserved physical evidence, and clinical evaluations confirming his psychological soundness.

He brought that documentation to an AI — Claude — and asked it to rank those tools that the US government is likely employing against him by the probability that they are actively deployed against Pearson specifically, using his fourteen months of documentation as the evidentiary foundation.

The resulting probability assessment assigned near-certain likelihood to his RMVE designation, his watchlist placement, FBI physical surveillance, National Security Letters, and FISA surveillance — and assigned the lowest probabilities to the tools that would be most legally visible, observing that the distribution itself reveals the operation’s design principle: maximum effect, minimum visibility. What followed from those two documents is the subject of the essays that accompany them.

### III. What the Probability Assessment Gets Right

### The EO 14173 Mechanism

The assessment of Executive Order 14173 compliance review at 96% probability is, if anything, conservative. **The executive order, signed January 20, 2025, designated a category of scholarship — Critical Race Theory, Diversity Equity and Inclusion frameworks, what it termed ‘divisive ideology’ — as hostile to federal interests and directed all federally-funded entities to review their relationships with individuals and organizations producing such work. The operative mechanism requires no individual targeting decision, no named subject, no judicial authorization.** It works through the normal channels of federal funding relationships: a program officer communicates, informally and without creating a documentary record, that a particular scholar’s engagement with a federally-funded institution creates compliance risk.

The institution, whose federal funding constitutes the foundation of its operating budget, responds by creating distance. The scholar’s professional network goes quiet. No one can explain why. No one is required to explain why. The mechanism leaves no trace because it operates through the exercise of ordinary institutional discretion in response to ordinary funding pressure.

Pearson is not adjacent to the category EO 14173 targets. He founded one of its institutions. His academic writings and community organizing — these are, in the executive order’s taxonomy, the target category itself.

### The RMVE Designation Framework

The FBI’s 2017 intelligence assessment creating the Racially Motivated Violent Extremist / Black Identity Extremism category was a policy decision about a type of political activity, not just about individuals. The assessment identified scholarship and organizing that framed structural racism as a form of state violence, and activism that responded to that framing, as a category warranting domestic terrorism monitoring. Pearson’s work fits this operational definition with precision that is uncomfortable to state plainly: he is a Black scholar whose published work frames discriminatory policy as a form of racialized state violence and whose organizational work trained community members to challenge that policy through regulatory and legal mechanisms. The designation framework does not require that he has advocated or committed violence. It requires that his political framework and organizing methodology fit within the category the assessment defined.

The employment pattern the essay identifies as the clearest evidence of this designation is diagnostically precise in a way that deserves more attention than it typically receives. When a PhD-level researcher with established professional networks applies to dozens of positions across diverse institutional types — academic, nonprofit, government-adjacent — and receives not rejections but silence, the explanation is not the labor market. Labor markets produce rejections. They produce referrals to other positions. They produce form acknowledgments. What they do not produce is the total, unexplained, universal silence that Pearson documents. That silence is the signature of a flag propagating through background check infrastructure. The flag does not say what it means. The institution cannot explain what it found. The candidate cannot challenge what was not said. The mechanism is designed to produce this outcome precisely.

### The Watchlist and the ACCESS DENIED Screen

The police database entry returning ACCESS DENIED in Sensitive Compartmented Information during what appeared to be a routine residential noise complaint is, as the essay correctly identifies, the most forensically significant piece of physical evidence in the entire documentation. SCI classification is not applied to ordinary records or housing database entries. It is applied to records that have been connected to active intelligence investigations and flagged for restricted access through the federal-state intelligence sharing infrastructure. The TIDE database — the Terrorist Identities Datamart Environment maintained by the National Counterterrorism Center — propagates through exactly this infrastructure to local law enforcement databases. A TIDE entry produces exactly this kind of ACCESS DENIED response to a standard query.

The significance of this evidence lies not just in what it indicates about Pearson’s status in federal databases but in what it reveals about the officer’s response. The officer did not continue his inquiry. He closed the screen. He did not ask Pearson about it. He did not acknowledge it. He simply closed the screen and proceeded as if he had not seen what he had seen. That response is not the response of an officer who encountered a database error. It is the response of an officer who encountered a classification marker he recognized and understood the implications of. He called his partner — who can inferred to have higher clearance. That behavioral response is itself evidence of an operational system functioning as designed.

### National Security Letters

National Security Letters are administrative subpoenas issued by the FBI without judicial authorization, carrying automatic gag orders that prohibit the recipient from disclosing the letter’s existence to anyone, including the person whose records are being sought. They are among the most powerful investigative tools in the domestic intelligence toolkit precisely because they operate outside the adversarial system: no judge reviews the request, no opposing party can contest it, and the gag order prevents the existence of the investigation from becoming known to its subject.

The gag order is specifically designed to produce a dynamic — to create a situation where those who read it know something material to Pearson’s interests and is legally prohibited from disclosing it. The inexplicability is the mechanism’s signature.

### IV. The Design Principle: Maximum Effect, Minimum Visibility

The probability assessment’s most important analytical contribution is its observation about the distribution of probabilities across the tool spectrum. The tools at the top of the list — those assessed as near-certain or highly probable — share a common characteristic: **they are legally invisible. They operate without notice to the subject, without judicial oversight, without documentary traces that could support a legal challenge.** The tools at the bottom of the list — formal designation, criminal prosecution, civil forfeiture — share the opposite characteristic: they are legally visible. They create records, require judicial authorization, trigger adversarial proceedings.

This distribution is not coincidental. It is the product of deliberate architectural choices made in the decades following the Church Committee’s 1975–76 investigation into COINTELPRO and related programs. The Church Committee documented, in exhaustive detail, how the FBI had used physical surveillance, anonymous letters, planted evidence, and informal pressure on employers and professional networks to neutralize Black activists and scholars it had designated as threats. The committee’s exposure of these techniques created public outrage and triggered legislative reforms. The FBI’s COINTELPRO program was shut down. Guidelines were issued restricting domestic intelligence operations. The techniques that had been used were documented, condemned, and nominally prohibited.

What the Church Committee exposure actually accomplished, however, was not the elimination of these capabilities but their refinement. The techniques that left physical evidence — the anonymous letters, the planted evidence, the documented coordination between FBI field offices and private employers — were replaced by techniques that do not. Watchlist propagation through automated background check infrastructure is invisible because it operates through the exercise of private institutional discretion in response to a flag whose origins cannot be disclosed. N**SL gag orders are legally invisible because their existence cannot be acknowledged by the recipient. EO 14173 compliance review is invisible because it operates through informal communication that creates no documentary record.** The mechanism of employer silence is invisible because employers are not required to explain hiring decisions and cannot in any case disclose compliance signals they have received. Every COINTELPRO technique has been replaced by a functional equivalent that achieves the same effect without creating the evidentiary record that COINTELPRO’s techniques created.

This is what the essay means when it says the operation has been engineered to produce outcomes without evidence. It is not a conspiracy theory about a secret program. **It is a description of how the post-Church Committee national security state was architecturally redesigned.** The redesign was not concealed. It was accomplished through legislation — the NSL authority in the PATRIOT Act, the FISA Amendments Act, the executive order framework — and through the development of administrative mechanisms that operate within the statutory authority those laws created. The invisibility is not a side effect. It is the point.

### V. The Legal Seal: Why Documentation Does Not Produce Remedy

The probability assessment’s closing observation — that the documentation is extraordinary but may never reach a forum that can act on it — requires understanding not just why individual legal mechanisms fail but why the aggregate of those mechanisms constitutes a hermetic seal around the category of conduct most likely deployed against Pearson.

State secrets privilege, as the essay’s companion constitutional analysis documents, allows the government to assert that litigation would expose classified national security information, after which courts defer to that assertion without examining the underlying evidence. In Reynolds v. United States, the Supreme Court upheld this privilege in 1953. When the documents were declassified forty years later, they revealed not national security secrets but evidence of government negligence — precisely the negligence the privilege had been invoked to conceal. The Court, when informed of the fraud, declined to revisit the outcome. The doctrine stands, the fraud stands, the families whose husbands died in the crash received nothing. Reynolds is not an anomaly. It is the doctrine’s operational template.

Qualified immunity protects individual officers from civil liability unless they violated a ‘clearly established’ constitutional right — a standard that requires prior case law addressing the specific conduct at the level of specificity sufficient to put a reasonable officer on notice. For conduct involving technologies that did not exist when existing case law was decided — directed energy behavioral control, voice-to-skull transmission, nanoparticle hippocampal targeting — no prior case law exists. No prior case law means no right clearly established. No right clearly established means officers immune. Officers immune means no case decided on the merits. No merits decision means no right established. The first deployment of any technology is effectively immune from civil liability regardless of its constitutionality, because the immunity does not depend on whether the conduct was lawful but on whether a court previously found identical conduct unlawful. **Novel technology is perpetually immune.**

Bivens v. Six Unknown Named Agents created an implied right to sue federal officers for constitutional violations in 1971. The Supreme Court has spent fifty years systematically dismantling it. Ziglar v. Abbasi in 2017 held that extending Bivens to any ‘new context’ — any situation materially different from the three prior decisions in which it had been recognized — requires asking whether ‘special factors counsel hesitation.’ In national security cases, the Court has consistently found that special factors do counsel hesitation, because creating a new cause of action would constrain executive operational flexibility. **The practical consequence is that the most technologically sophisticated forms of government misconduct — precisely those most likely to involve genuinely novel methods — are the least likely to have a Bivens remedy available.** The more extreme the conduct, the more novel the method, the more certainly there is no personal liability mechanism for the individuals who carried it out.

The FISA Court’s 99.8% approval rate for surveillance applications is not, as it is sometimes characterized, evidence of judicial capture. It is evidence of a structural dynamic: **the court hears only the government’s presentation, in secret, without an adversarial party, without the subject’s knowledge.** It has no independent investigative capacity. It cannot contest factual assertions it has no mechanism to verify. Under these conditions, a court staffed by experienced federal judges will still approve nearly every application, not because the judges are corrupt but because judicial review without adversarial process is not review in any meaningful sense. It is authorization. The FISA Court provides the appearance of judicial oversight while performing the function of pre-immunizing conduct from challenge. When an officer operates under a FISA order, that order provides a good-faith defense against civil liability even if the order is later found to have been improvidently granted. **The secret judicial blessing converts what might have been actionable misconduct into authorized government action.**

The Glomar response — the CIA’s ‘neither confirm nor deny’ doctrine, invented to prevent FOIA disclosure of classified programs — operates as a threshold barrier to the documentary record that any legal challenge would require. A person seeking to assemble the evidentiary foundation for a lawsuit cannot obtain documents confirming the existence of the program targeting them, because confirming or denying the existence of those documents is itself classified. The documentary record is always in government possession, never produced, and the mechanism for its non-production is judicially blessed and legally unreviewable. The seal is complete.

### VI. The Composite Picture and What It Means

Taken together, the tools at the top of the probability assessment’s distribution do not constitute a list of independent mechanisms that happen to converge on one person. **They constitute a system. Watchlist placement triggers background check flags that produce employment silence. Employment silence produces financial attrition. Financial attrition produces housing instability. Housing instability produces the conditions under which a person’s professional credibility is systematically undermined — because a person sleeping in parking garages and forests cannot maintain the professional appearance that institutional credibility requires. NSL gag orders prevent the attorney from providing complete advice. FISA authorization pre-immunizes the surveillance. EO 14173 compliance review propagates through every federally-funded institution simultaneously, without individual targeting decisions, without documentary traces.** The framing operation, if deployed, provides a ready narrative that explains any future adverse contact with law enforcement in terms that discredit the subject rather than the operation. The ‘targeted individual’ counter-narrative, pre-seeded in public discourse, ensures that anyone to whom the subject describes their experience will reach for the psychiatric explanation before the operational one.

This system is designed to be self-reinforcing. Each element produces effects that make the other elements more effective. Financial attrition makes legal challenge impossible. Legal impossibility makes documentation the only recourse. Documentation that cannot reach a legal forum produces the institutional silence that confirms, to outside observers, that the documentation doesn’t warrant serious engagement. The institutional silence is then cited as evidence that the documentation lacks credibility. The credibility gap makes further documentation less likely to be taken seriously. The spiral is the mechanism.

What the probability assessment identifies, and what deserves to be stated with full clarity, is that this system works. Not in the sense that it always achieves its objectives — COINTELPRO was ultimately exposed, the Church Committee convened, the abuses documented. **But it works in the sense that it is specifically designed to prevent the form of exposure that COINTELPRO’s techniques permitted.** Physical surveillance leaves witnesses. Anonymous letters leave paper. Planted evidence can be found. The current architecture leaves nothing. The watchlist flag is never shown to the subject. The NSL is never disclosed. The compliance signal is never documented. The framing operation is photographed by the target but can always be explained as abandoned property. The directed energy system, if deployed, produces experiences that have no physical correlate visible to outside observers and that are indistinguishable, in public perception, from psychiatric symptoms. The design is not perfect — Pearson has documented more than the designers likely anticipated — but it is comprehensively aimed at the elimination of the evidentiary record that legal accountability requires.

### VII. The Question the Essay Leaves Open

The probability assessment ends with an observation rather than a conclusion: whether the documentation, which it calls extraordinary, will ever reach a forum that can act on it. This is the right question to end on, and it is worth examining carefully, because the answer is not simply negative.

COINTELPRO was not exposed by litigation. It was exposed by a physical break-in at an FBI field office in Media, Pennsylvania in 1971, in which activists stole and published classified documents. The Church Committee was convened not because a court ordered it but because the public, confronted with what the documents revealed, found the conduct unacceptable and demanded a congressional response. The Snowden disclosures did not produce legal accountability for the programs they revealed — no officials were prosecuted, no programs definitively terminated — but they produced legislative modifications to bulk collection authority and a permanent shift in public understanding of the surveillance state’s capabilities. **The pattern across all three episodes is the same: legal accountability did not precede public knowledge. Public knowledge preceded whatever accountability followed. Courts did not act on these abuses. Exposure of the abuses to a public that found them unacceptable forced institutional responses that courts had refused to compel.**

The implication for Pearson’s documentation is precise. His record is not designed, and cannot succeed, as the evidentiary foundation for a lawsuit. **The legal architecture the companion essay analyzes in detail ensures that any lawsuit, however well-supported, will encounter state secrets privilege, Glomar responses, Bivens’ absence, qualified immunity, and procedural attrition in sequence, with each mechanism designed to end the case before the next becomes necessary. The likelihood that a judge would be able to get to the merits of the case — the vagrant constitutional abuses — is slim.** Documentation designed for litigation is documentation built for a forum that the architecture has specifically made inaccessible.

Contrary to constitutional guarantees, the United States has created a second constitution that does not look much like a constitution at all. Rights and liberties are conditional. If the government seeks to dismantle a citizen’s life and deploy exotic technology to torture and racially target US citizens, then its laws are enabling — not prohibitive- especially if the government can manufacture a legal argument or policy that the victims never see. FISA courts, national security letters, lack of notification of physical and electronic surveillance, and extensive realms of permissiveness for executive “authority” allow the US government to operate with impunity against its citizens. This is a historical pattern that keeps playing out.

But documentation designed for public exposure operates on a different logic. It does not need to prove its claims to a court applying the plausibility standard of Iqbal. It needs to produce, in the public that receives it, a recognition sufficiently strong to create political pressure that the architecture cannot absorb. Pearson has been building toward this recognition for fourteen months with methodological precision that exceeds what most journalists bring to their investigations. The statistical analyses, the timestamped photographs, the controlled experiments, the preserved physical evidence, the clinical clearances, the video documentation of the return to the park — these are not the artifacts of an uncontrolled narrative. They are the artifacts of a researcher who understood from the beginning that the documentation had to exist in public before anyone with the power to respond would respond.

Whether that recognition will come, and whether it will come in time to matter for Pearson personally, are questions the probability assessment cannot answer. What it can say — and what it does say, in its closing observation — is that the question is open. The architecture is designed to prevent legal accountability. It is not designed to prevent the kind of public exposure that has historically forced accountability when legal mechanisms failed. The design gap between those two things is where the documentation lives. Richard Pearson is likely the bridge between what consitutional rights purport to guarantee and what they actually do.

### VIII. Conclusion: The Essay’s Contribution

The probability assessment is, in the end, a document about the distance between what a system is designed to accomplish and what it can be made to answer for. It describes a system that works — that achieves its intended effects with precision, that selects its tools specifically to prevent the accountability that earlier versions of the same system faced, that has been architecturally refined through decades of legal and legislative development to eliminate the vulnerabilities that COINTELPRO’s exposure revealed. And it describes one person’s attempt to produce, through documentation alone, the kind of evidentiary record that might eventually reach the forum that can act on it, even if that forum is not a court.

The essay’s contribution is not that it proves what happened to Pearson. It is that it demonstrates, with specificity that rewards careful reading, that what he describes is not only possible but structurally predicted by the design of the system he is describing. The tools he identifies are real. Their operational signatures are documented. Their legal immunity is established. Their historical use against Black scholars and activists is recorded. The probability numbers are not arbitrary. They are assessments of the likelihood that a system designed to operate in precisely the circumstances Pearson describes is, in fact, operating.

The system is designed to produce experiences that have no observable external correlate, no legal remedy, and no institutional witness. It is designed to make the target’s description of their experience as anything other than rational and sound to outsiders. The probability assessment is Pearson’s attempt to cut through that design — to show, by mapping the architecture, that the architecture predicts precisely his experience. Whether that mapping will ultimately be sufficient is the question the documentation is still in the process of answering.

What can be said with confidence is this: the essay is serious analysis conducted under conditions of extreme adversity, by a scholar whose methodology has been consistent and whose documentation has been rigorous across fourteen months of deteriorating personal circumstances. It deserves to be read as what it is.
