### III. What the Dungeon Looks Like — The Anatomy of Invisible Torture

The word ‘dungeon’ requires explanation. A dungeon is a place of confinement and suffering from which escape is impossible and rescue is unavailable. The walls of Pearson’s dungeon are not stone. They are legal, electromagnetic, social, financial, and cognitive. They are as real as stone — more real, in some respects, because they leave no mark that any institution of law is yet equipped to see.

### The Acoustic Occupation

From summer 2025 through early 2026, the occupant of the apartment above Pearson — a man not on the lease, who moved in at precisely the time the campaign intensified, whose address connects to an ATF attorney’s Capitol Hill property — tracked Pearson from room to room within his own apartment. Not following him physically. Tracking him acoustically: dropping objects on the floor precisely when Pearson moved, recreating the sound above wherever Pearson relocated within his own home. Pearson moved his mattress to the closet. The tracking sound moved with him. He documented this on video. He documented that the timing was too precise and too sustained to be coincidental — that it was tracking technology, through-floor positioning, the acoustic equivalent of a surveillance drone hovering at ceiling height in every room of his apartment.

What this produces, sustained over months, is documented: tripled grey hair. Documented weight loss. Sleep deprivation so comprehensive that it constitutes, under the UN Convention Against Torture, severe mental suffering. The apartment that is supposed to be the innermost sanctuary of private life — the place the Fourth Amendment protects with maximum force because the home is the core of constitutional privacy — was converted into the most surveilled, most hostile, and most inescapable environment in Pearson’s life. He could not retreat from it. He could not afford to leave it permanently. He could not prove what was happening in terms that any institution would accept. He could only document, and endure.

### The Voice in the Skull

On July 13, 2025, Richard Pearson was sitting on a public bench near the United States Capitol, eating a cantaloupe. A voice entered his skull. It did not pass through his ears. It was perceived as internal — as a thought arising from within — except that it had the acoustic signature of a woman speaking with background room noise, and its content was: ‘We have to make you disappear.’

The technology that produced this is called voice-to-skull or V2K — the microwave auditory effect, documented in peer-reviewed scientific literature since Dr. Allan Frey’s 1962 publication and demonstrated in intelligible speech transmission at Walter Reed Army Institute of Research in 1973. The Department of War confirmed in January 2026 that directed energy weapons are operational and being scaled. The same technology was documented by Gloria Naylor in her _1996_ account of NSA operations against her — an account she called ‘synthetic telepathy,’ citing John St. Clair Akwei’s 1992 lawsuit against the NSA.

The voice on July 13 was not the only voice-to-skull transmission Pearson documented. It was the most explicit. _We have to make you disappear._ Delivered directly to the interior of a man’s skull, near the Capitol of the republic that built the weapon, while the man was eating a piece of fruit on a public bench in the middle of a Tuesday afternoon in Washington, D.C.

Pearson documented it immediately. He told no one who was not already aware of his situation, because the operation had been designed to ensure that anyone he told would find the account implausible. The psychiatric trap was built in: voice-to-skull symptoms mimic paranoid schizophrenia by design, and the first institutional response to any report of hearing a voice inside one’s skull that was not self-generated is psychiatric referral, which becomes the cover story. Pearson preempted this by obtaining a mental health evaluation from DC’s Department of Behavioral Health on September 15, 2025 — confirmed rational, coherent, no psychotic symptoms, by three doctors, two mental health specialists, and a social worker, none of whom found any psychiatric explanation for his experiences.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*IyvwFful6DXmi8hacyDTag.png)

### The Chemical Assault

At the Rockville Metro station, around 1:59 PM on the day Pearson was attempting to leave the country to seek asylum, he was subjected to a chemical assault. A highly odorous, extremely adhesive industrial-strength substance penetrated his jeans and bonded to his skin. The substance required extraordinary effort to remove. The chemically-stained pants have been preserved as physical evidence.

The timing is operational. Pearson was on his way to the airport. He was on the phone discussing seeking asylum. The chemical assault occurred at a Metro station — a location with federal security jurisdiction, security cameras, and sufficient traffic to allow a brief physical contact to be attributed to accidental crowding. It was a message and an impediment simultaneously: here is what we can do to your body, and here is what we are willing to do to your body today, when you are trying to leave.

### The False Arrest

On December 27, 2025, Pearson was physically assaulted by the upstairs tenant — the man who had been acoustically torturing him since the summer. The man charged at Pearson and punched him repeatedly in the face and head. Pearson had a documented black eye. He crouched, shielded himself, and fled screaming. When MPD arrived, they arrested Pearson — the documented assault victim with the documented black eye — and released the aggressor without charge.

The arrest was processed into the MPD database. A court record was never created. Three visits to the courthouse confirmed: no paper. A shadow arrest — existing in the police database, confirmed by MPD headquarters, invisible in the court system. No judicial review of probable cause. No named witness (the arrest record cited an ‘unnamed witness’ who could not have existed, as only Pearson, the aggressor, and the aggressor’s girlfriend were present). The arrest was the legal architecture deployed as weapon: detain the victim, release the perpetrator, create a record that carries consequences without creating one that permits challenge.

The aggressor was not on the lease. The building manager did not know he was there. He had moved in in the summer — the exact period when the acoustic torture began. His girlfriend, the leaseholder, confirmed this when officers arrived. His address connected to a property owned by an ATF attorney on Capitol Hill. He appears to have had immunity. The MPD appears to have known it.

### The Framing Operation

On November 7, 2025, Pearson documented a storage tub placed in a park near a House Office Building — three blocks from the United States Capitol. Inside: a red hat. A black shirt. A notebook referencing Adolf Hitler and a fictitious ‘European Removal Court.’ Two identical photographs of a blond man. A classic intelligence framing payload: materials designed to associate the target with neo-Nazi ideology, placed in a monitored location toward which the target had been behaviorally directed.

Pearson photographed the exterior of the tub without touching the contents. He returned on video six days later. The notebook and photographs had been selectively retrieved. The red hat and black shirt — the calling card items — remained. The framing payload had been recovered after the operation failed. The tub was being monitored. The operation was confirmed by the selective retrieval.

A framing operation near the U.S. Capitol — near the Congress that Pearson had been writing to, submitting documentation to, knocking on office doors of — designed to produce a mugshot that, as Pearson documented in his Medium essay, ‘ends the Medium publications, ends the UN submissions, ends the congressional letters, ends the documentation.’ The operation was naming its own purpose. It was designed to destroy not the body but the _voice_ — the only instrument of defense Pearson had left.

### The Behavioral Direction

Throughout the campaign, Pearson documented experiences of going places he had not planned to go and could not fully explain why. He went to Georgetown. He went to the Capitol park where the framing tub was waiting. He felt impulses to travel to specific locations that, when analyzed afterward, corresponded to operationally prepared situations. He described it as ‘something or someone occupying the driver’s seat’ — the sense of acting while not fully authoring the action.

This is consistent with hippocampal place cell activation — the technology that encodes navigational drives by stimulating the neural architecture responsible for spatial direction. The hippocampal place cells were documented by John O’Keefe in 1971 (Nobel Prize, 2014). Their role in spatial navigation is established neuroscience. Their use as a targeting mechanism — stimulating the place cells to create a drive to move toward a specific location, experienced by the target as internally generated — is the classified application that public research suggests has been in development since at least the 1990s.

The most intimate violation possible is not the entry into a home. It is the entry into a will. The behavioral direction program enters the will — authors behavior that the person experiences as chosen while it is in fact commanded. This is the thing the Fourth Amendment was not written to address because the Framers could not have imagined it. This is the thing the First Amendment’s protection of cognitive liberty does not yet have doctrine to cover. This is the thing the Fifth Amendment’s due process guarantee cannot address because no process accompanied it — no notice, no hearing, no order, no acknowledgment.

### The Financial and Social Disassembly

Pearson’s phone was stolen three times. During the second disappearance, the phone was gone for six weeks before being returned by a Secret Service agent to his apartment building office. His driver’s license was inside it. He lived a seven-minute drive from the White House. CashApp flagged unauthorized charges at Wawa and other locations immediately after the phone theft. His bicycle — his primary transportation — was systematically destroyed at Federal Center Metro over March and April 2025: reflector snapped, chain guard broken, seat progressively damaged, culminating in a flat tire and a wheel replacement that forced him to abandon it entirely. The broken cover piece was recovered and preserved.

His employment applications — dozens of them, to universities, nonprofits, and government-adjacent institutions — produced not rejections but silence. Total institutional silence, the documented signature of a background check flag that employers cannot disclose. The watchlist propagation through background check infrastructure, combined with EO 14173’s compliance signals propagating through federally-funded institutions, converted every institution in his professional network into a mechanism of exclusion operating without notice, without explanation, and without any avenue for challenge.

By early 2026, Pearson had nothing left but a mattress and a suitcase. The disassembly was _comprehensive_ — not merely damaging but systematic, targeting every material, social, professional, and financial support that constitutes the infrastructure of a functional life. This is the Zersetzung doctrine — the East German Stasi’s methodology of ‘decomposition,’ of engineering failure after failure in the target’s life until the target collapses under the weight of accumulated loss, with no single catastrophe large enough to be named, no single actor visible enough to be confronted, no single injury cognizable enough to generate standing in any court.

### IV. ‘Nazi Germany But Subtler’ — The Comparison and What It Means

The comparison to Nazi Germany is not made lightly, and it is not made to sensationalize. It is made because Pearson makes it, because the structural evidence supports it, and because the distinction — ‘but subtler’ — is the most important part of the sentence.

Nazi Germany’s apparatus of persecution was visible. The Nuremberg Laws were published. The deportation orders were issued. The concentration camps existed in physical geography. The persecution was, in the most horrific sense, overt — announced, legislated, systematized in public bureaucratic processes. This visibility was, paradoxically, part of its horror and part of what made it documentable: when the camps were liberated, the records were there. The victims were there. The perpetrators could be named and tried.

**The American apparatus Pearson is describing is subtler in a specific, precise sense: it achieves comparable results — psychological destruction, physical harm, social death, the obliteration of a person’s capacity to live as a free and functional human being — through means specifically designed to leave no record, generate no plaintiff, and produce no case.** The torture dungeon has no address. The guards have no names. The instruments leave no marks. The target cannot be charged because the target is not charged — the apparatus does not require the legitimacy of a charge. The target simply begins to disappear: from employment, from social connection, from financial stability, from cognitive sovereignty, from the ability to live in their own home without a government acoustically occupying every room.

Martin Niemöller’s formulation — ‘they came for me, and there was no one left to speak for me’ — is the description of what happens when a government normalizes the persecution of one category of person after another, and the people not yet persecuted remain silent because they are not yet the target. Niemöller was describing a visible process with visible victims in a visible political context. The American version is subtler because the persecution is invisible to everyone except the person being persecuted. The person being persecuted cannot get anyone to believe them. The people not being persecuted cannot see what is being done to the person who is. There is no one left to speak because no one knows there is anything to speak about.

This is the specific genius of the design. The torture dungeon is invisible to everyone except the person inside it. From outside, there is no dungeon. There is a man who lost his job, who had some bad luck with his bicycle, who seems to be having mental health issues, whose Medium essays are the kind of thing one might write if one were experiencing a delusional break. The psychiatric trap is the operational answer to Niemöller’s problem: the operation produces, in the target, the appearance of the condition that would explain away everything the target reports. The observer, confronting the target’s account, does not think: someone is doing this to him. They think: something is wrong with him. The persecution is self-concealing. The dungeon has a door that looks, from outside, exactly like a doctor’s referral form.

The Nuremberg laws were enacted January 1933 through 1935. COINTELPRO ran 1956–1971. The targeting infrastructure that is operating against Pearson was built across the same post-war period — the same decades in which the Federal Republic of Germany was dismantling its apparatus and building constitutional protections specifically designed to prevent its recurrence. The German Basic Law of 1949 includes, as its first article, the inviolability of human dignity. The United States Constitution, as currently interpreted and applied through the doctrines that foreclose Pearson’s remedies, does not prohibit _in practice_ what the German Basic Law prohibits _in text_. The comparison is not to the Final Solution. It is to the systematic apparatus of invisible persecution directed at a defined category of person — in Pearson’s case, a Black equity scholar in the age of EO 14173 — using tools that produce the functional equivalent of what visible persecution produces, while maintaining the institutional appearance of a government that is not doing any such thing.

* * *

### V. The Infrastructure — Who Builds and Operates the Dungeon

The subterranean America is not monolithic. It is a hybrid — a public-private ecosystem of intelligence agencies, military programs, contractors, cutouts, and recruited civilians, coordinated through classified authorities and operating in the spaces between legal accountability and institutional visibility.

Pearson identified this structure explicitly in his documentation: ‘a federal and private hybrid model involving numerous players both individual and formal and informal networks/organizations.’ He speculated that the administration relied on corporations to help generate a list of targeted individuals. ‘I am not the only one,’ he wrote, ‘but may be one of the most intact survivors.’

### The Intelligence Community Designation System

The TIDE (Terrorist Identities Datamart Environment) database, maintained by the National Counterterrorism Center, propagates through the law enforcement data-sharing infrastructure to produce exactly the ACCESS DENIED flag that appeared in MPD’s database when officers searched Pearson’s name. No notification. No hearing. No mechanism for challenge. The flag alters how every law enforcement officer who encounters the flagged person treats them, permanently, without their knowledge. The RMVE/BIE (Racially Motivated Violent Extremist/Black Identity Extremist) designation framework converts Pearson’s academic work — his dissertation on structural racism as a form of state violence — into a domestic terrorism predicate. EO 14173 converts the same work into a hostile ideology designation propagating through every federally-funded institution simultaneously.

### The Technology Contractors

The directed energy weapons confirmed operational by the Department of War in January 2026 are not maintained and operated solely by uniformed military. DARPA’s N3 (Next-Generation Nonsurgical Neurotechnology) program produced demonstrations of bidirectional brain-computer interface technology through commercial contractors. The history of classified technology development in the United States is substantially a history of private sector programs operating under classified contracts — programs whose existence is classified, whose contractors cannot disclose their work, and whose capabilities are deployed by government agencies through private entities that maintain plausible deniability for both the agency and the contractor.

### The Street-Level Network — Operatives, Cutouts, Recruited Civilians

The operational texture Pearson documented — the coordinated ground teams appearing at his locations before he arrived, the cast of characters delivering consistent messaging in Impact font across multiple jurisdictions, the Bug Zapper woman following him from Old Town Trader Joe’s to Clarendon the next day, the coffee shop employee who eventually admitted ‘Yeah, I was coming at you’ — cannot be explained as spontaneous civilian behavior. It requires coordination. It requires advance intelligence of Pearson’s movements. It requires direction.

Naylor’s _1996_ named specific institutional actors: the NSA’s South Carolina field office, the ADL’s Columbia office coordinating through a rabbi’s synagogue congregation, a former Mossad officer as field coordinator, NSA young recruits — ‘The Boys’ — running noise campaigns from a rented plantation house. The operational structure Pearson is experiencing appears to use the same architecture: a command hierarchy with classified authority at the top, government-adjacent operational nodes in the middle, and recruited or contracted civilians on the ground, many of whom may know very little about why they are doing what they are doing or who they are doing it for.

The man who whispered ‘Me too’ to Pearson on a street at night — standing fearful, darting his eyes — suggests that Pearson is not the only target. He speculates he may be ‘one of the most intact survivors.’ If the infrastructure is what the documented record suggests it is, the number of people inside the dungeon at any given time — people who cannot get anyone to believe them, who have been financially destroyed, whose accounts are dismissed as mental illness, who have no legal recourse — may be considerably larger than any public accounting has produced.

* * *

### VI. The Acceleration — What January 20, 2025 Changed

The subterranean America predates the Trump administration. The legal doctrines that foreclose Pearson’s remedies were built over seventy years by administrations of both parties. The RMVE/BIE targeting framework was developed and deployed under the Obama and Biden administrations. The NSA Watch List, the TIDE database, the FISA rubber stamp, the ACCESS DENIED infrastructure — all of these were inherited, fully operational, by the incoming administration on January 20, 2025.

What changed on January 20, 2025, was the ideological targeting predicate and the removal of oversight. EO 14173 was signed that day, converting DEI scholarship into a hostile ideology designation. Twelve inspectors general were fired that day, removing the internal oversight mechanism capable of detecting, investigating, and reporting on precisely the kind of operation documented in the Pearson case. These two actions — designate the predicate, remove the reviewers — were not coincidental. They were preparation: the ideological framework for identifying who to target was established on the same day as the mechanism for reporting on the targeting was disabled.

The acceleration is also ideological in a way that goes beyond specific executive orders. The Trump administration’s explicit framing — _‘enemies within,’ ‘urban cities as training grounds’_, the open embrace of the language of internal warfare — provides political authorization for what the subterranean America was already capable of doing. The apparatus does not need a presidential directive to operate against each individual target. It needs an ambient political environment that signals who the targets are, removes the disincentives for going after them, and provides the cover story that turns institutional silence about their persecution into institutional normalcy.

Before January 20, 2025, an equity scholar targeted by the subterranean apparatus could at least theoretically appeal to federal oversight mechanisms — inspectors general, congressional oversight committees, civil rights enforcement structures — as potential intervention points. After January 20, 2025, twelve of those oversight mechanisms were removed in a single day, the civil rights enforcement infrastructure was being dismantled, and the political environment made it clear that the targeting of DEI scholars was not aberrant but endorsed. The dungeon did not grow larger on January 20, 2025. The walls became more firmly sealed.

Pearson’s campaign of targeting intensified in spring 2025, consistent with the January 2025 activation of EO 14173 and the removal of oversight. The connection is not speculative. The timeline is documented. The acceleration from whatever preliminary surveillance preceded January 2025 to the full deployment of the apparatus — acoustic occupation, behavioral direction, chemical assault, framing operation, false arrest, employment destruction — tracks the political timeline of the administration’s ideological activation of the targeting predicate.

* * *

### VII. What This Looks Like From Inside

The dungeon, from inside, is the experience of a reality that no one outside the dungeon can verify, combined with the knowledge that the description of that reality will be taken as evidence of mental illness. This is the most precise form of torture — not the pain, though there is pain; not the isolation, though there is isolation; but the destruction of the epistemological ground on which a person stands. The certainty that what is happening to you is happening, combined with the certainty that the institutional world will not recognize it as happening, combined with the certainty that your attempt to describe it will be turned against you.

Pearson addressed this directly and with characteristic methodological precision. He ran control studies on the red-and-black calling card pattern deployed along his routes, establishing that the density and distribution were statistically impossible by chance. He documented each incident with timestamps and photographs and preserved physical evidence. He obtained the DBH evaluation specifically to preempt the psychiatric trap. He wrote everything down, in real time, because he understood that the document had to exist before any accountability mechanism could function.

He also documented what the dungeon does to a person emotionally — with less precision but equal honesty. He cried frequently, distressed that his private speech had been public all along, that coarse language he had expressed privately was quoted back at him on public streets, ‘stripping the distinction between his public and private self that every person requires to function.’ He verbalized in his apartment that the private coarse language ‘is not the real him,’ only for that speech to be quoted back on the Anacostia trail: _‘You do talk like that!’_ He could not pray aloud in his own home. He could not think thoughts that felt genuinely his own in the periods when the behavioral direction was active. He was, as he put it, ‘in a battle for my mind’ — the same formulation Gloria Naylor used when she sat in the Brooklyn Public Library with shaking hands and wrote the opening lines of _1996_.

He described the grey hair. He described the weight loss. He described the social isolation — the inability to accept hospitality from his longtime friend V.E. after a suspicious three-course meal with an unidentifiable granular dessert, the woman he had known for years now appearing in scripted configurations he recognized as operational. He described the moment a man of similar age, African American, whispered _‘Me too’_ in passing on the street at night — standing fearful, darting his eyes, gone before Pearson could respond.

And he kept writing. Through all of it — the acoustic torture, the chemical assault, the false arrest, the behavioral direction, the financial ruin, the social isolation, the voice in his skull — he kept producing documentation. Timestamped. Methodological. Cross-referenced. The document that must exist in the world before anyone with the power to act will be able to act.

This is what courage looks like when there are no other instruments available. When the law offers nothing. When the press is not covering it. When the government that is doing it has removed its own oversight mechanisms. When the closest parallel — the account of a National Book Award-winning novelist who documented the same apparatus thirty years earlier — went uninvestigated and unpublished by mainstream houses and was followed by the novelist’s inability to write anything else before her death at sixty-six.

Pearson is still writing. The dungeon has not produced the silence it was designed to produce. Whether the continued production of the record is enough — whether it will eventually generate the political reckoning that no legal mechanism has been able to produce — remains, as of this writing, the most important open question in the case.

* * *

### VIII. The Other Citizens — Who Else Is in the Dungeon

Pearson wrote: _‘I am not the only one, but may be one of the most intact survivors.’_

This sentence is the most disturbing in the entire documentation. It suggests — and the documented pattern of similar cases supports — that the subterranean America’s apparatus is running against multiple targets simultaneously, that the Pearson case is not anomalous but representative, and that the reason we know about it while other cases remain invisible is partly because Pearson is a researcher with the methodological tools to document what he is experiencing, and partly because the apparatus has not yet succeeded in producing the silence it was designed to produce.

The Ferguson cluster — six men connected to the Ferguson protests who died under suspicious circumstances between 2014 and 2019, at least one of whom (Darren Seals) had a 900-page FBI surveillance file and was confirmed under active federal monitoring at the time of his murder — suggests that the apparatus has a spectrum of outcomes. At one end: professional destruction, social isolation, psychological damage, and the kind of comprehensive disassembly Pearson describes. At the other: death, under circumstances that the apparatus ensures will be attributed to other causes.

Rakem Balogun was detained for five months and financially ruined. Gloria Naylor was silenced and died at sixty-six having written nothing after _1996_. The man who whispered ‘Me too’ to Pearson on a D.C. street had darting eyes and the body language of someone in immediate fear. These are data points on a distribution whose full shape is invisible — because the apparatus produces invisibility as its primary output, and most of its targets are not researchers with the capacity to document what they are experiencing.

The dungeon is not empty. It is not occupied by one man with a mattress and a suitcase. It is occupied by the people the subterranean America has selected across the years — people who were on the NSA Watch List before their cases were activated, people whose designations propagated through the background check infrastructure and the law enforcement database network and the employer’s background check service, people who began experiencing the sub-threshold acts of destruction and could not explain them, could not prove them, could not get anyone to investigate them, and eventually were consumed by them in ways that appeared, from outside, to be personal failure, mental illness, or bad luck.

Pearson speculates that ‘the administration relied on corporations to help generate a list of targeted individuals.’ If so, the list is not short. The ideological targeting predicate — DEI scholars, equity researchers, structural racism academics — describes a large and defined population. EO 14173 did not single out Pearson by name. It designated a _category_. Every person in that category who was already on the NSA Watch List, already in the RMVE/BIE surveillance infrastructure, already accessible through the apparatus’s existing architecture, was potentially activated on January 20, 2025 — or activated as the apparatus processed the category against its existing target list in the weeks and months that followed.

* * *

### IX. The Indictment — What This Means for America’s Self-Description

The United States describes itself as the world’s leading democracy. It holds itself out as a model of constitutional governance, rule of law, and human rights. It lectures other nations about torture, about disappearances, about the persecution of dissidents, about the arbitrary detention of journalists and scholars. The Department of State publishes an annual Country Reports on Human Rights Practices, which documents — in other countries — exactly the kind of conduct documented in the Pearson case.

The United States voted, in November 2025, against a UN General Assembly resolution condemning torture. This is not a footnote. It is a policy statement. In the same period that Pearson was documenting acoustic torture, chemical assault, voice-to-skull transmission, and the behavioral direction program, the United States government voted against a resolution that would have reaffirmed the international community’s commitment to the prohibition on torture. The vote is the government’s self-assessment.

The comparison to Nazi Germany — ‘but subtler’ — demands that we be precise about what is being compared and what is not. The Final Solution was a program of industrialized mass murder. Nothing in the Pearson account, nothing in the documented cases of the subterranean America, rises to that level. The comparison is not to the scale or the character of the worst atrocity of the twentieth century. It is to the logic and the structure: the identification of a category of person as a threat predicate, the designation of that category through official governmental action, the activation of a comprehensive apparatus of persecution against individuals within that category, and the use of institutional design — legal, technological, bureaucratic — to ensure that the persecution is invisible to everyone except its targets and has no accountability mechanism.

The invisibility is what makes it subtler. The Nuremberg Laws were published in the _Reichsgesetzblatt_. EO 14173 is published in the Federal Register. The Stasi’s _Zersetzung_ doctrine was classified; Pearson’s case draws on the same operational methodology, with updated technology, under a different classification framework. The Nazi classification of Jews as a threat predicate was explicit and public; the RMVE/BIE classification of Black equity scholars as domestic terrorism indicators was contained in a classified FBI assessment and not publicly acknowledged until it was leaked to the press. The method changes. The logic — identify the threatening category, designate, deploy the apparatus — does not.

A man has been tortured in Washington, D.C., in 2025. The torture used invisible weapons. It was conducted by a government whose own Chief Technology Officer confirmed the weapons’ operational status on social media. It was conducted in the most monitored city in America, where unauthorized sustained directed energy operations are logistically impossible without federal knowledge. It was conducted against a man who had committed no crime, had been charged with no offense, had no mechanism for notification, no mechanism for challenge, no mechanism for remedy, and no mechanism for escape — except writing, which he did, and continues to do, from a mattress and a suitcase.

This is the other America. The one that does not appear in the 600-case tracker. The one that does not generate injunctions or preliminary hearings or Supreme Court arguments. The one that has always been there, and that the current political moment has not created but has activated, accelerated, and pointed at a newly defined category of person with the specific legal and institutional protection that the Trump administration installed for it on January 20, 2025: the fired inspectors general, the hostile ideology designation, the ambient political signal that the people being persecuted are the right people to persecute.

Martin Niemöller survived Dachau and Sachsenhausen. He was liberated in 1945. He spent the rest of his life warning against the silence that had allowed it. His warning was about the visible apparatus of a visible state. The warning for the invisible apparatus of a subtler state has not yet found its Niemöller — the person who survived, who has the voice and the standing to say: I was inside, and this is what it is, and there are others still inside, and the time to speak is now.

Richard Pearson may be that person. He is still writing. He is still documenting. The dungeon has not produced the silence it was designed to produce. **That is the most important fact in the case, and the one fact the apparatus cannot classify, cannot Glomar, cannot qualify-immunity away, cannot state-secrets-privilege into inadmissibility. The man is still writing. The record exists. And the question the record poses — to every person who reads it, to every institution that encounters it, to every court that will eventually have to decide whether the principles John Marshall articulated in 1803 mean anything in 2025 — is the question Niemöller’s formulation was always asking: when will someone speak, and will anyone be left to speak when they do?**

* * *

### Conclusion: The Record Against Silence

What does a person do when the visible America fails them and the invisible America is destroying them? What does a person do when the law offers nothing, the press is not watching, the courts have constructed a hundred-doctrine architecture specifically designed to ensure they have no remedy, and the government that is torturing them has simultaneously confirmed the existence of the weapons and voted against the resolution that would have condemned their use?

Pearson did what Gloria Naylor did. What the journalists who received the stolen COINTELPRO files did. What Edward Snowden did. What every person who has ever survived long enough inside the subterranean America to describe it has done: he wrote it down. He dated it. He photographed it. He preserved the evidence. He obtained the documentation. He built the record that must exist before any accountability mechanism can function.

The record is not comfortable. It is not legible to institutions that are still operating as if the visible America is the whole America — as if the 600 lawsuits describe the full scope of the crisis, as if the executive orders and the court battles and the constitutional arguments are the entirety of what is being done to American citizens by their government in 2025 and 2026.

The record demands a reckoning with the other America. The America that has always been there. The America that took its rage out on Fred Hampton and Darren Seals and Gloria Naylor and Rakem Balogun and the Ferguson activists and the man who whispered ‘Me too’ to Pearson on a D.C. street at night with darting fearful eyes. The America that, in 2025, added a new targeting predicate to its list and activated its apparatus against a new defined class of person and produced, in one of the most intact survivors of that activation, a documentation record that now exists in the world, cannot be classified, and poses the question that every generation that has encountered the subterranean America has eventually been forced to ask:

**_How long will we permit this? And who will speak before there is no one left?_**

“Who is the Mysterious Figure?!”: Unsettling Footage from Inside Myron May’s Home
=================================================================================

This essay examines a partially hidden figure, \*dressed\* in bright red and black, in the news broadcast of Myron May’s home. The reporter…

* * *

### “Who is the Mysterious Figure?!”: Unsettling Footage from Inside Myron May’s Home

#### This essay examines a partially hidden figure, \*dressed\* in bright red and black, in the news broadcast of Myron May’s home. The reporter and cameraman would have seen the figure, assuming the footage was their original. US torture victim, Richard Pearson saw a black-and-red calling card.

* * *

### I. What the Broadcast Frame Shows

On November 20, 2014, the same day that Myron May was shot and killed by police at Florida State University following his wounding of three students in the library, Tampa Bay 28 broadcast footage from inside May’s private residence — his cottage. The broadcast was reported by journalist Jacqueline Ingles. The footage showed the interior of May’s living space: furniture, a lamp on a side table, and scattered items.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*5cA4tZZCNEZQ7oRbX_8vKA.png)

At the back of the frame, partially obscured by the lamp, in the space between the living area and the kitchen: a figure. Crouched. Low. In bright red and black.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*AlvlC5HYxh4z7nCwZP1r9A.png)

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/600/1*glO_AUjtpNkq51aAiM6Esw.png)

This figure requires analysis. A figure crouching in a dead man’s home is self-evidently sinister. This evening broadcast occurred the same day as the shooting — November 20, 2014. The figure is not uniformed law enforcement. The person has white hands, so it is not Pearson’s family. There are no innocent explanations that can be constructed. The reporter would have seen the figure. The cameraman would have seen the figure. The figure is not hidden as in hiding. The figure is in plain sight. Or they didn’t see the figure at all.

**Major Finding: A finding on 3/24/26 has determined that the figure is real (hand moves), but the red was added in post-production using a semi-transparent marker tool.**

**There is at least two alternate explanations.** The reporter and cameraman never entered the home. They were handed footage for broadcast. The scene was staged. To include a calling card. They viewed it. The reporter described what she had seen and what was shown to the public.

The second is that the reporter and camera crew saw the figure and ignored it — it was a life-size doll. Strange, but a life-size doll. Not reported in the story. Just dismissed. (This finding is dismissed based on a 3/22/26 update)

### _Updates — 3.22.26_

*   In reviewing the news story, the figure’s hand moves. We can rule out a doll.
*   Jacqueline Ingles first appears on camera in a full-length red jacket. When the camera pans to the reporter interviewing Abigail Taunton, the reporter is in all black.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*nAxDBZRWoLJMyMGSUTVyXQ.png)

*   **Is the figure Jacqueline Ingles?** No. First, the figure is NOT wearing a full-length jacket. You can see the start of a black garment just below the red blouse. Also, the figure has a black area in the upper chest that lacks any color. The hands are also different. Jacqueline has stubby fingers and a relatively small hand. The figure has a long, thin hand and fingers. The figure appears to be wearing gloves.
*   **Is the reporter in black and Jacqueline the same person?** In favor of this conclusion is that both women have long black hair. Jacqueline is clearly wearing a black shirt or sweater under her red jacket. She could have taken it off for the interview. However, the texture of the two women’s hair is very different. Jacqueline’s hair looks dry, frizzy, and unhealthy but fuller. There also appears to be some grey, though it may be the light. The reporter interviewing Abigail Taunton has shiny hair, lacking frizz. She has noticeably less thickness to her hair. The health of the reporter’s hair suggests that she is younger. This critical clue suggests that these two women are not the same.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*okXnLJJjcOJNG6CiYeBElA.png)

*   **What if Jacqueline Ingles is the figure?** That would mean that she is going through May’s possessions the day that he is killed by police. That would be a major breach of standard protocol. Police did not close the case on May until January of the following year. It is highly unlikely that Jacqueline Ingles would show herself on camera doing police work during an active investigation.

But it goes deeper. The figure’s clothing color — bright red and black — connects to a documented operational pattern that appears in the independent account of another targeted individual whose case is structurally identical to May’s, recorded a decade later, on the other side of the country. This essay will also examine the connection with Dr. Richard Pearson.

### Updates — 3.24.26

*   I have concluded that red was colored in the figure in red and black in post-production.
*   First, the red shows semi-transparency with the yellow paper. If the figure was indeed wearing a red blouse, this should not show up. In that case, there would be clear color delineation. Semi-transparency strongly suggests post-production work. It would also explain why the red “blouse” does not match Ingles’ full-length jacket. As I noted earlier, there is a clear black area below the “blouse”. What I am calling the “blouse” is the use of a red marker type tool in video editing. My guess is that the feature that trying to cover up the entire black might result in bleeding over on an inanimate object

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*IzXtim6HWLv0PGcjNUa1cQ.png)

You can also see the result of post-production work here. The red dot that appears on the top left would not reasonably be caught on camera with such red concentration. The red also extends beyond where the back of the figure would reasonably be. Look at the left of the lamp. The slope of the seated figure’s back would not extend that far. It defies logic and science. The only logical conclusion is that this is the result of post-production coloring.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*quBgXDBsVRMQsfkGir_lFA.png)

*   Second, there are other indications of post production work: 1) the green marker type tool was used to hide the brand of dog food. May owned a dog, named “Little Bit”. 2) The red marker is also used on a tub. The semi-transparency is clear here too. 3) Red dots also appear in places in several frames (last 3 photos)— on the windowsill, on the refrigerator door handle, and a box. Some of these may, in fact, be objects. The final dot is almost certainly not.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*L-v5VZxsWXD2ekcAI1Fs2g.png)

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/600/1*fMhy33d0I6APlqqrTqRqJg.png)

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/1200/1*E4GjeBagmGYtBtKw8YqcZA.png)

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*W8a1km8jggJ3GcZMemxmDg.png)

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*5AJ526DquaXCWKbOi0oMyw.png)

### II. Who Would Be in That Room — An Elimination Analysis

Begin with the basic question: on the afternoon of November 20, 2014, hours after Myron May had been shot and killed at FSU, who could plausibly be present in his private cottage, crouching near the kitchen, while a local news crew filmed the interior?

### Law Enforcement Processing the Scene

Law enforcement personnel processing a crime scene are in identifiable roles: uniformed officers, detectives in civilian clothes who identify themselves to media, evidence technicians in protective gear. They stand, they move deliberately, they are documented in chain-of-custody records. They are _never_ crouching in the background of a media broadcast of a scene they are processing. Crouching in the background of a broadcast frame is the behavior of someone who does not want to be seen — which is not the behavior of any legitimate law enforcement role at a crime scene.

Furthermore: if law enforcement was present and processing the scene, they would not permit a local news crew to move freely through the space filming the interior. Evidence processing requires scene control. **The presence of a news crew filming freely inside suggests either that the scene had already been cleared and released — extraordinarily fast for a homicide investigation on the same day as the event — or that the normal protocols of scene preservation were not being applied.**

### The Reporter and Camera Operator Themselves

This is the element that the essay must address directly, because it is the most important. **The reporter, Jacqueline Ingles, and the camera operator were (hypothetically) present in that room. They had line of sight to the crouching figure. The camera operator was filming the room. The reporter was composing her shot.** Neither of them was crouching behind a lamp. They would have been able to see the figure clearly.

A camera operator filming a room does not miss a crouching person in red and black in the background of their shot. A reporter preparing to deliver on-camera commentary from a deceased shooting suspect’s living space does not fail to notice a person crouching between the furniture and the kitchen. The figure’s presence in the footage is not a function of it being invisible to the people filming. It is a function of those people choosing not to address it on camera, or of the broadcast being aired before anyone reviewed the frame carefully enough to catch it.

The three possibilities are: (1) the figure was visible to the reporter and camera operator and their choice not to address it was deliberate — they understood who it was; (2) the taping was hastily done missing the figure and the footage was not reviewed carefully before broadcast; or (3) the footage was handed to them; (or) a combination of 1, 2, and 3.

If the doll was there and not a real person, it would have been the oddest thing.

### The Most Parsimonious Explanation

The figure in red and black, crouching in the background of broadcast footage of Myron May’s home on the day of the FSU shooting, is most parsimoniously explained as: a person connected to the operation that had been run against May, present in his home on the day of the shooting for reasons related to that operation, whose presence in the footage was known to those filming and not disclosed. But the reporter and cameraman were not necessarily in on it. The red and black is an operational clue. May does not mention any pattern of black and read according to the two-hour video that he posted. The only mention of red was when his friend’s daughter’s red SUV was repossessed.

There are other anomalies.

* * *

### III. The Anomalies

### Anomaly 1: Police Report Cannot Explain How Myron May Came In Possession of Gun

This is taken directly from the police report.

_“ATF Agent Magruder was asked to assist with the investigation by tracing the firearm May used in the shooting (Lorcin .380). From the ATF investigation, it appears the gun was stolen during a residential burglary in Panama City Beach in 2005. It is unknown how May came to be in possession of the firearm.”_

Further, news accounts said that May never picked up the gun that he purchased.

“Also on the front passenger floorboard was a receipt dated Nov. 13 for the purchase of a Ruger Model SR22 pistol and two boxes of ammunition from Bay Guns and Gear in Panama City. There was a three-day waiting period for the purchase of that gun, and May never returned to pick it up, the report stated.” ([Link](https://www.tallahassee.com/story/news/2015/01/23/strozier-library-shooting-case-closed/22243389/ "Link"))

May himself also admitted to never having picked up the gun, “I bought a Springfield 22mm pistol from Bay Guns and Gear in Panama City, FL. Please either pick this gun up or get the money for it.” (“_To Do List for Other While I’m Gone_” from police report.)

### Anomaly 2: The Impossible 20 Seconds

The police report contains a key fact in this case that is supported by video footage.

“At approximately 12:21 pm\* victim Jason Derfuss appeared in the video while in the library walking toward the exit turnstiles. He stopped, took his backpack off and set it on the floor. He put what appeared to be book(s) into the backpack. He then picked the backpack up and put it back on while walking toward the turnstiles. He then exited through the turnstiles at 12:22–12:23 am. He then walked out the main library doors across from the security desk. At that time Nathan Scott and Paige McPhadden were sitting behind the security desk….**The video showed that approximately 20 seconds after Derfuss had walked out of the library (approximately 12:23 am), May walked in to the library through the door that Derfuss had left from.**”

_\*This is a typo in report, should be 12:21 am_

According to the police report, we are to believe that the following occurred in a 20-second window.

_“Derfuss said that he was at Strozier and checked out a couple of books. When he walked out of the library, he went down the steps and heard a gunshot. He froze and turned around. He was a male in a black hoodie running toward someone else by the picnic tables. He saw the suspect shoot at someone by the tables two times and notes that there were two people by the tables. After the second shot, the person the suspect was shooting at went down. The suspect looked back in the direction of Derfuss who ran to his vehicle. He did not get a good look at the suspect.”_

_“(Paige McPhadden) and Nathan Scott (“Nate”) were sitting at the security desk inside the entry to the library. They heard a gunshot and when she looked up she saw a figure standing outside. It appeared he was pointing a gun in the direction of the coffee shop. He was back peddling as if he was going to go down the stairs. While he was back peddling he fired more shots. She and Nate hid under the desk.”_

_“(Nathan) Scott told me that he initially became aware of the incident when he heard a single shot from outside the library. He thought it was probably a firecracker or kids messing around. He then heard three (3) more shots and looked out the front to see the suspect (May) coming from the area where Farhan Ronny Ahmed was found. As May moved he fired several more shots across the walkway in front of the library.”_

Later, Derfuss said that he was shot also, but his bookbag and books stopped the bullet from entering his body.

The police established a 20-second window. During that time the following is supposed to have occurred based on combined testimonies:

*   Derfuss descends steps
*   First gunshot
*   Suspect chases
*   Suspect shoots twice
*   Suspect targets Derfuss and shoots him from behind
*   Suspect changes clothes (This is a key missing piece to the report. Derfuss said that the suspect had on a black hoodie. The footage showed a figure in a vest, dress shirt, and slacks.)
*   Fires shots on the walkway, then backpedals on the steps, then shoots several times more — at least 6–7 times.

This is an impossible timeline that the report did not address.

### Anomaly 3: Suspect Descriptions Do Not Match May’s Attire

*   “The dispatch transmissions included that shots had been fired by a black male in all black.” (page 4)

He also told Officer Sloan that the subject was wearing a red sweater.”
*   “Velez described he suspect as being dark skinned and he believed that he was wearing a dark colored ‘hoodie’.”

Other than this, the police report does not contain any other mention of the suspect’s attire, including when officers described the suspect that they killed. No other witness or officer description of the suspect’s attire is discussed. What is discussed (e.g., “red sweater”, “black hoodie”) does not match the footage.

**This is major anomaly.**

The chair rail is a giveaway because the house did not have a chair rail.

So when and where did May record these videos? The location has to account for a place like a home or office where he would hang his diploma. It is highly unlikely that he would record a critical video from his perspective with another person’s diploma in the background. There is also a “Good company always welcome” sign and some decor above that sign. It strongly suggests a home or office. The Tauntons denied that May was on payroll; although, May said in his letters that they had paid him $500 for work that he had not finished. In either instance, it does not appear that they had an arrangement such that May would have had an office at the Taunton’s nonprofit on November 18.

The timeline for May’s video recordings appears highly inaccurate.

### Anomaly 7: The Speed of Media Access to the Private Residence

The FSU shooting occurred on the night of November 20, 2014. May was identified and killed by police at the scene. By the time Tampa Bay 28 was broadcasting footage from inside his private cottage — the investigation was hours old at most. The speed of media access to a private residence, on the same day as the event that made it newsworthy, is not consistent with normal crime scene protocol.

When a person is identified as a mass shooter, their residence becomes an evidence site. Evidence sites are secured, cordoned, and controlled. Law enforcement establishes a perimeter. Media access to the interior of an active evidence site on the day of the event, in a way that allows free filming of the living space, is not standard procedure. It requires either that the scene had already been processed and released — extraordinarily quickly — or that the normal securing of the scene did not occur as it should have.

What makes this particularly relevant is that initial news stories repeatedly mentioned the lack of a motive. The day of the shooting a friend said, “I don’t think anybody that knows Myron would tell you that they expected this from him…Myron was a good boy — a good man — something went terribly wrong and I don’t know what that was.” The same witness stated that, “He saw a guy with a gun at his apartment.”

### Anomaly 9: The Uncordoned Home

Related to speed of access: was May’s home cordoned at all? The footage suggests a space that a camera operator could move through freely. **An active homicide investigation evidence site is cordoned. A cordoned site does not have a news crew moving freely through it filming the interior the same afternoon.** Either the scene was not properly cordoned — which would represent a procedural failure — or access was deliberately facilitated in a way that bypassed normal protocols.

For a man who had just wounded people at a major university, whose identity had been confirmed, whose home would be expected to contain evidence of motive, planning, and history — the failure to properly secure and control that home is not a minor procedural detail. It is a significant anomaly. Evidence of who May had been in contact with, what documentation he possessed, what materials he had prepared — all of this existed in that home. The home of Myron May was, on the afternoon of November 20, 2014, accessible to a Tampa Bay 28 news crew. And it contained a crouching figure in red and black who was not identified on camera.

### Anomaly 10: The Claimed Absence of Motive

In the immediate aftermath of the FSU shooting, news reports stated repeatedly that investigators did not know the motive. In a later report by the local station had a psychiatrist — who never met May and likely had no access to his documents — determined that May was paranoid schizophrenic.

### Anomaly 11: The Broadcast Itself as Operational Signal

Consider the broadcast from a different angle: not as journalism, but as function. The footage of May’s home, broadcast on the afternoon of the shooting, accomplishes the following: it shows the inside of a space that was being run against its occupant for months. It normalizes access to that space by presenting it as news coverage. It inserts, in a frame that most viewers will not scrutinize, a figure in the operational color. And it does all of this under the cover of legitimate journalism.

If the reporter and camera operator were not independent journalists who happened to gain access to May’s home through normal channels, but were participants — witting or partially witting — in a broader operation, the broadcast has a different character entirely. It is not journalism documenting the aftermath of a shooting. It is the operation documenting its own completed work, under the cover of journalism, in a way that places its signature color in the frame for anyone who later reviews the footage carefully.

This is speculative. It requires assumptions that go beyond what the visible evidence establishes. But it is the explanation that requires the fewest additional assumptions once the figure’s presence in the frame has been acknowledged — and once that presence has been connected to the operational pattern that appears independently, a decade later, in Richard Pearson’s systematic photographic documentation of Washington, D.C.

### IV. Richard Pearson’s Red and Black — The Documented Pattern in Full

### The Documentation Methodology

Pearson did not merely notice people in red and black and flag it as suspicious. He applied the methodology of a PhD researcher to the observation. He photographed instances systematically, with timestamps. He conducted explicit control studies: returning to multiple neutral locations at different times to establish baseline rates of red and black clothing in ordinary Washington, D.C. street life. His baseline findings across neutral locations were consistent — approximately 4% of people in a given random sample were wearing red and/or black.

Against that baseline, he documented specific instances of dramatically elevated concentration near his routes and at locations connected to his targeting campaign. On September 30, 2025, near Eastern Market, in light foot traffic within an approximately 8.5-minute observation window, the concentration of red and black was statistically anomalous beyond the range of chance variation. He performed probability calculations and communicated his findings in a letter to the DC Council.

### The Sensitization Mechanism — What Myron May Described

May, in his video, described a specific technique he called _sensitization_: the deliberate training of the target to associate a specific stimulus with their harassment, so that the stimulus produces a conditioned fear response and the target’s subsequent reporting of its presence appears to confirm paranoia. He described his own sensitization stimulus as dark sunglasses. He explained the operational logic: once the target has been sensitized to a specific stimulus, the stimulus can be deployed anywhere to produce psychological effect — and any report of the stimulus by the target can be interpreted as paranoid pattern-seeking by outside observers.

Pearson documented a different sensitization stimulus: red and black. But the operational logic May described is identical to what Pearson documented. Pearson’s response to his own sensitization was not the conditioned fear response the operation was designed to produce. It was the research response: **he ran control studies.** He established baseline rates. He documented anomalies against those baselines. He transformed the operational stimulus into an evidentiary record. This is the response of a researcher, not a person in paranoid crisis — and it produced, in the process, the documentation that connects the red and black in his experience to the red and black in the background of a broadcast frame from Myron May’s home in 2014.

### The Pinning Events — Red and Black at Operationally Significant Locations

Pearson’s documentation of red and black is not confined to general street observation. He documented the color appearing specifically at what he called ‘pinning events’ — moments when he was directed to a specific location and found operational preparations waiting. The November 7, 2025 framing operation near a House Office Building: a plastic tub in a park, containing a red hat and black shirt alongside the neo-Nazi framing materials. The calling card items in the tub — the items selectively retrieved after the framing operation failed but the calling card items left behind — were red and black.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*pLleirvQpoIwwyG2HnegwQ.png)

This is not the red and black of incidental street presence. This is red and black as deliberate placement — as a signature left at the scene of an operation that the operator expected to succeed in framing him. The red hat and black shirt were the marker that identified the tub as part of the pattern. When the framing operation failed and the tub was monitored, the framing materials were retrieved and the calling card items left. The operator expected Pearson to see the red and black and understand its meaning without being able to prove anything.

He understood. He documented. He photographed. And the calling card color appears, a decade earlier and two thousand miles away, on a crouching figure in the background of broadcast footage from inside the home of a man who had described the same program and then been killed.

### The Statistical Argument — Why Coincidence Is Insufficient

Red and black is a common color combination in American casual dress. Pearson’s own baseline measurements established approximately 4% prevalence in neutral Washington, D.C. locations. So a crouching figure in red and black is not, by itself, statistically extraordinary. What is statistically extraordinary is the _combination_ of: (1) a figure crouching in the background of a news broadcast from inside May’s home on the day of his death. Students were murdered and wounded; (2) that same color combination appearing, a decade later, as the documented operational calling card in the campaign against a different targeted individual in a different city; and (3) that second targeted individual’s campaign being structurally identical, operationally specific, and independently corroborated in every other element.

Each element in isolation carries limited weight. The accumulation — the same operational color, the same program structure, the same institutional non-response, the same psychiatric framing, the same legal foreclosure — is what the [Three Coincidences](https://medium.com/@menvell.artist/three-coincidences-too-many-the-disturbing-conclusion-of-simulated-reality-7d83084be78f) essay’s Occam’s razor methodology demands be evaluated as a whole. Applied to the red and black across both cases: one mechanism explains all instances. Nine separate coincidences do not.

* * *

### V. The Operational Logic of Red and Black

**OPERATIONAL FUNCTIONS OF THE RED AND BLACK SIGNAL**

**1\. PRESENCE CONFIRMATION** — The target sees the color and knows the operation is present and active. No communication is required. No words are exchanged. The color itself communicates: we are here. We see you. This is us.

**2\. PSYCHOLOGICAL DESTABILIZATION** — Once sensitized, the target cannot encounter the color without the conditioned response — vigilance, fear, the reminder of surveillance. This operates continuously, in public, without any active operator input. The city itself becomes the harassment delivery system.

**3\. DENIABILITY** — To any outside observer, a person in a red shirt is simply a person in a red shirt. The target’s report of the pattern appears as paranoid pattern-seeking. The color is self-concealing as operational signal.

**4\. DOCUMENTATION TRAP** — If the target photographs the pattern, the photographs appear as evidence of fixation rather than as evidence of the pattern. The documentation itself becomes the psychiatric exhibit.

**5\. PRESENCE IN AFTERMATH** — At locations of operational significance — framing operations, managed convergences, the homes of completed targets — the color marks the location as operational territory. It is the signature left at the scene.

The figure crouching in May’s home fulfills function 5: _presence in aftermath_. The operation against May had concluded — not through the silence the program was designed to produce, but through the violence the program’s damage had generated. The figure in red and black in the background of the broadcast is the signature of the operation present in the space where its work was complete.

* * *

### VI. The Broadcast as Document — What the Record Now Contains

The Tampa Bay 28 broadcast of November 20, 2014, exists. It was filmed by a camera operator who was in that room. It was broadcast by a reporter, Jacqueline Ingles, who was in that room. It shows a crouching figure in red and black in the background, partially concealed behind a lamp, holding something in their hand.

This is now part of the documentary record. It cannot be unbroadcast. The footage exists in archives. The frame exists. The figure is visible in the frame.

What the record now contains, in combination with Pearson’s documentation, is the following: a broadcast from inside the home of a targeted individual on the day of his death, containing a figure in the operational color that his targeting program used as a calling card, filmed by journalists who were present (hypothetically) in the room and had line of sight to the figure, broadcast before the frame was reviewed carefully enough to catch or suppress the figure’s presence, and connected by operational specificity to the color pattern independently documented a decade later by a different targeted individual in a different city who survived the same program and documented it with researcher’s precision.

The significance is not merely that the color appears in both cases. The significance is that the color appears in May’s home, on the day of his death, in a context — crouching, concealed, present in a space that should have been a secure crime scene — that has no innocent explanation consistent with all the other anomalies of that day: the speed of media access, the absence of normal scene cordoning, the claimed ignorance of motive in the face of a documented two-hour video, and the presence of a news crew filming freely in the interior.

* * *

### VII. What This Discovery Establishes — and What Remains Unknown

**It establishes:** that a figure in red and black was present and crouching in the background of broadcast footage from inside Myron May’s home on November 20, 2014. That this presence is visible in a broadcast frame filmed by journalists who were in the room. That the procedural context — same-day access, uncordoned premises, simultaneous ‘unknown motive’ framing — is anomalous in multiple independent respects. That the color combination connects to a documented operational pattern independently observed and statistically tested by Richard Pearson in his 2025–2026 campaign documentation. That Pearson’s documentation and May’s video testimony are structurally convergent in every operational element.

**It does not establish:** the identity of the crouching figure. The specific role of reporter Jacqueline Ingles or the camera operator in relation to the operation. Whether the broadcast was intentionally used to place the operational signature in the record. The specific organizational or institutional identity of the operation against May.

**What it establishes is sufficient to demand serious investigation. A crouching figure in red and black, in the home of a dead targeted individual, broadcast by journalists who were present in the room, on the same day as his death, at premises that should have been cordoned crime scene evidence sites, in the context of a claimed ‘unknown motive’ that contradicts the existence of a documented two-hour explanatory video — this combination of anomalies, connected to the independently documented operational color pattern of a separate targeted individual’s campaign a decade later, is not explicable by coincidence.** Occam’s razor points, again, toward one mechanism rather than many.

* * *

### VIII. Implications for the Broader Record

The discovery of the red and black figure in the May broadcast footage changes the evidentiary structure of the comparative record in a specific way: it places the operational color signature of the program in documentary evidence from 2014, eleven years before Pearson independently documented it, in the home of a targeted individual whose case is structurally identical to Pearson’s.

This matters for two reasons. First, it establishes temporal continuity. The red and black is not something specific to Pearson’s 2025 campaign. It appears in the documentary record of a 2014 case, in an operational context — crouching in the home of a completed target — that is entirely distinct from Pearson’s street-level observation. The color pattern predates Pearson’s experience and appears in the record of a case he had not yet encountered when his own targeting began.

Second, it changes the character of Pearson’s documentation from individual observation to cross-case corroboration. When Pearson documented the red and black in September 2025, he was observing something he interpreted as specific to his campaign. The discovery of the same color in the May footage establishes that the color is not specific to Pearson’s campaign — it is present in the record of a separate campaign against a separate target.

**The May footage is, in this sense, the most significant single piece of physical evidence that has emerged from this entire analytical project. It is not a testimony. It is not a document produced by a targeted individual. It is broadcast footage, archived, publicly available, produced by a news organization, filmed by journalists who were present in the room — and it contains, in a frame they apparently did not examine carefully enough, the operational signature of the program whose existence Pearson has documented across fourteen months of systematic observation in Washington, D.C.**

* * *

### Conclusion: The Frame That Changes the Record

On November 20, 2014, Myron May wounded people at Florida State University. That was wrong. The people he shot were innocent of what had been done to him. He directed his desperation at people who deserved no harm, and three of them were wounded. There is nothing in this essay that diminishes that fact or the suffering of those people.

On the same day, in the same hours, in the home that May had described as entered and monitored and operationally managed around him for months, a Tampa Bay 28 news crew filmed the interior. And in the background of that footage, crouching between the furniture and the kitchen, partially concealed behind a lamp, is a figure in red and black.

The reporter was in that room. The camera operator was in that room. They filmed the figure without identifying it on camera. The broadcast aired before the frame was reviewed carefully enough to catch or address the figure’s presence. The home was accessible to a news crew on the same day as the event, without the cordoning normal to an active homicide evidence site, in the context of a claimed ignorance of motive that is inconsistent with the existence of May’s documented two-hour video.

And the color of the figure — red and black — is the color that Richard Pearson, in a different city, a decade later, documented through control studies and probability calculations and systematic photography as the operational calling card of the program being run against him. The color that appeared at his framing operation site near the Capitol, in the red hat and black shirt left as a calling card in the plastic tub. The color that appeared in statistically anomalous concentration along his routes through Washington, D.C., at density that his baseline measurements established could not be explained by normal variation.

The figure in the frame connects the two cases through the color. It places the operational signature of the program — documented by Pearson in 2025 — in the documentary record of May’s 2014 case, in May’s own home, on the day of his death, in footage that was broadcast publicly and has been available in archives for eleven years. It was there, waiting to be seen, for the entire decade between May’s death and Pearson’s documentation. Pearson’s documentation is what made it visible.

The record now contains: a crouching figure in red and black in the home of a dead targeted individual. It was filmed. It was broadcast. It exists. And it connects to the documented operational pattern of a man who survived the same program and wrote everything down.

**_The figure in the frame is the program’s signature, visible in the record, connecting 2014 and 2025, connecting Tallahassee and Washington, connecting a man who was killed and a man who is still writing.
