### “I Can’t Pray Aloud”: US Torture Victim’s Surveillance Violates Religious Rights

#### Richard Pearson, US torture victim, explains loss of essential religious liberties during Trump Administration and why the conservative majority of the US Supreme Court has made it harder for victims like him to challenge government violations of their religious rights.

#### Richard Pearson is a torture victim in the United States. He has been physically assaulted resulting in a black eye and lacerations, with industrial chemicals, and with electrocution. His personal computer has also been hacked. He has been sleep deprived and harassed with noise.

His home is not off limits either. It’s being surveilled. A complete stranger told him so in 2025, “They are listening to you.” Weeks later, police responded directly to Pearson’s private remarks in his home to himself, confirming both the suspected surveillance and the government’s role.

Pearson, who holds a PhD, has written extensively about torture in Washington, DC through 2025–2026 during the second Trump administration. He has enumerated countless laws that were violated — a feature of being in America’s “Torture Dungeon” — a subterranean form of totalitarian government where no liberty or right is inviolable. His basic, fundamental rights guaranteed in the US Constitution — due process, First Amendment rights, equal protection, cognitive liberty, to be free of cruel and unusual punishment — weren’t just violated. Erased. As if no legal or constitutional authority existed at all.

*   First Amendment — cognitive liberty, compelled speech, academic freedom
*   Fourth Amendment — search and seizure, curtilage, new technology doctrine
*   Fifth Amendment — due process, self-incrimination
*   Eighth Amendment — cruel and unusual punishment
*   Fourteenth Amendment — equal protection
*   Fourth Amendment standing doctrine
*   Emerging constitutional doctrine on cognitive sovereignty

But there is one liberty that Pearson has yet to fully describe— right to religious freedom. Because Pearson is under surveillance, he cannot pray aloud in private. Pearson exclaims, “Can you imagine this in America? On top of being tortured, you have no way to pray in private without someone eavesdropping on your prayers. America is meaner, uglier, and far more racist that I ever thought possible. That says a lot because I have read extensively about US and world history. I would have left the US decades ago, even if that meant selling coconuts in a beach resort without ever having to be tortured in my lifetime. US constitutional democracy is a joke. It really is. Besides, US law has made it awfully hard for me to even bring my case. [A detained immigrant accused of gang membership or drug smuggling has more rights that I do as a US citizen facing covert, state-sponsored torture.](https://medium.com/@menvell.artist/when-detained-non-citizens-have-more-rights-than-us-citizens-inversion-in-the-us-legal-system-12a431a99be4) I have had no due process.”

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*KBaaXqCwP8YdOQ6ZJANy9g.png)

That is a problem, of course. It questions US guarantees of constitutional rights in the US, but it also questions the Trump administration — ostensible appeals to religion and faith. Most recently in April 2026, Trump read from the Bible in the White House in a taped message after Trump posted images of himself as Jesus on social media, which was widely condemned. The irony of the selected passage was not lost on Pearson, “_If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways, then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.”_ (2 Chronicles 7:11–22).

#### _“I guess they have done all of the torture and terror that they want to do. Very befitting, isn’t it?” Pearson said flatly of the President’s scripture reading. “_But it doesn’t work quite like that. You don’t get to defy God, then hide behind the Bible. They will see the Almighty’s hand of justice.”

Pearson’s experience also raises profound questions the US Supreme Court’s commitment to religious rights, consistently ruling in favor of religious freedom and against government influence in matters of faith while making it more difficult for US citizens to bring claims of religious rights violations against the government. If the government violated those rights but operates within a federal secret program, secret program trumps rights. In fact, the US Supreme Court has made it, more or less, legal doctrine upon critical examination of competing legal precedents.

Pearson’s experience also exposes a specific hypocrisy in the administration conducting the surveillance — an administration that has made religious freedom one of its most prominent rhetorical commitments, that has appointed judges on the strength of their religious freedom credentials, and that is simultaneously operating a surveillance program that makes private prayer impossible for one of its targets. The US Supreme Court’s recent jurisprudence on religious freedom creates a theoretical framework for Pearson’s claim that is simultaneously more protective than any prior court and — through the same doctrinal mechanisms that foreclose his other claims — practically inaccessible to him as a plaintiff.

### I. The Surveillance — What Is Known and How It Was Confirmed

Pearson’s home surveillance is not a suspicion. It is a documented conclusion resting on two independent confirmations.

The first confirmation came from a stranger in 2025, who approached him and said: ‘They are listening to you.” A person Pearson had never met, in an unplanned encounter, delivered a statement that described exactly what Pearson had been documenting as part of the campaign against him. The stranger’s motivation — whether the statement was a warning from someone with knowledge of the operation, an inadvertent disclosure by someone with operational awareness, or an act of conscience by a peripheral participant — is unknown. What is documented is what was said. The surveillance is visible enough to produce a civilian disclosure from someone outside Pearson’s social network.

The second confirmation is more specific and more legally significant. Weeks after the stranger’s warning, police responded directly to remarks Pearson had made privately in his own home — to himself, aloud, in his private space, not transmitted digitally, not spoken to anyone present. The police response was not coincidental to the remarks in content or timing. It corresponded directly to what Pearson had said in private. There is only one explanation consistent with that correspondence: the remarks were heard by someone with access to Pearson’s home audio environment, and that person — or the system they were operating — communicated the content to law enforcement.

The police response is the government’s role confirmed. Private citizens with listening devices do not produce police responses keyed to the content of a specific person’s private remarks. Police responses of this kind require: a system capable of capturing private audio in a private home; operators with access to that system and the ability to act on its content; and a connection between those operators and law enforcement sufficient to produce a calibrated response. That infrastructure — the warrantless home audio surveillance, the operator monitoring, the law enforcement coordination — is the infrastructure of a government operation. No other actor has the combination of technical capability, legal access, and law enforcement coordination that the police response to Pearson’s private remarks requires.

This is the home that Pearson prays in. It is the home where any spoken prayer is monitored. It is the home where the most private act of religious observance a person engages in — the direct address to God, spoken in the language of one’s own interior — is captured, processed, and potentially acted on by the same operators who have been running a torture campaign against him for more than a year.

### II. What the Free Exercise Clause Protects — And What Pearson’s Situation Violates

The First Amendment’s Free Exercise Clause prohibits the government from prohibiting the free exercise of religion. It is deceptively simple language. Its application has generated more than two centuries of constitutional litigation because the line between government action that affects religious practice and government action that prohibits free exercise is not always clear. But some cases are clear. This is one of them.”),

#### The Doctrine — What Courts Have Established

The Supreme Court’s Free Exercise jurisprudence has evolved through several phases. The current framework, established most clearly in Employment Division v. Smith (1990) and significantly supplemented by subsequent decisions, holds that neutral, generally applicable laws that incidentally burden religious practice do not violate the Free Exercise Clause. But laws — or government actions — that are not neutral, that are not generally applicable, or that specifically target religious practice receive the highest level of constitutional scrutiny: strict scrutiny, which requires the government to demonstrate a compelling interest pursued through the least restrictive means.

The Court’s most recent major Free Exercise decisions have moved consistently toward stronger protection. In _Church of Lukumi Babalu Aye v. City of Hialeah_ (1993), the Court struck down laws that were specifically designed to target a particular religious practice, holding that religious animus in the legislative record triggers strict scrutiny. In _Fulton v. City of Philadelphia_ (2021), the Court held that government contracts cannot include non-discrimination requirements that apply to religious organizations with exceptions for secular organizations — the system of individualized exemptions doctrine. In _Kennedy v. Bremerton School District_ (2022), the Court ruled that a public school employee’s right to pray privately on the job was protected, holding that the Free Exercise Clause ‘can give way only to a competing fundamental right or government interest of the highest order.’ In _303 Creative v. Elenis_ (2023), the Court extended religious and expressive freedom protections even into commercial contexts.

The current Supreme Court is, by any fair reading, the most protective of religious freedom in modern American history. It has ruled consistently and expansively in favor of religious practitioners against government impositions on faith. — And yet: a man in Washington, D.C. cannot pray aloud in his own home because the government is listening. That is the inversion this essay is examining.

#### Why Pearson’s Situation Is a Textbook Free Exercise Violation

The government’s warrantless surveillance of Pearson’s home does not merely affect his religious practice incidentally. It directly and substantially burdens his ability to engage in the most protected form of religious exercise: private prayer.

Private prayer is not a peripheral religious activity. It is the core of personal religious life across virtually every faith tradition. It is the direct communication between a person and their God — unmediated, unperformed, not directed at any human audience. Its value to the believer derives precisely from its privacy: the knowledge that what is said is heard only by God, that the expression is fully authentic, that no human judgment will be passed on the content, the words, the fears, the requests, the gratitude, the doubt. This is what makes private prayer different from public worship — not the content but the audience. Private prayer is the believer at their most unguarded, in the most intimate relationship they understand themselves to have.

Government surveillance of private prayer violates the Free Exercise Clause in a specific and serious way: it transforms private prayer into observed speech. — A person who knows their home is monitored and that their private remarks have produced law enforcement responses cannot pray aloud with the freedom that genuine prayer requires. The knowledge of observation changes the nature of the act. Prayer directed to God through a government recording system is no longer private prayer. It is monitored speech that happens to be addressed to a divine audience. The government’s presence in the listening does not merely inconvenience Pearson’s prayer. It fundamentally alters its character — converting the most intimate form of religious expression into a form of speech that is subject to government scrutiny.

This is not an incidental burden on religious practice produced by a neutral, generally applicable law. It is a direct, specific, continuous burden on the most protected form of religious exercise, produced by a government operation specifically targeting Pearson. Under any version of Free Exercise doctrine — even the more permissive Smith framework — a government action that directly and specifically burdens an identified individual’s private prayer is subject to strict scrutiny. Under the more expansive Kennedy framework, it is subject to the requirement that any compelling interest be pursued through the least restrictive means. No legitimate government interest requires listening to a private citizen’s prayers in their own home. The violation is not close.

### III. The Administration’s Hypocrisy — Religious Freedom as Rhetoric and as Practice

The Trump administration has made religious freedom one of its signature rhetorical and policy commitments. It has established White House Faith Offices. It has appointed federal judges — including three Supreme Court justices — whose religious freedom credentials were prominently featured in their nominations. It has issued executive orders protecting religious expression in federal employment. It has directed federal agencies to prioritize religious freedom in their regulatory work. Its political coalition includes evangelical Christians, Catholic conservatives, and other religious communities whose central concern is the protection of faith from government interference.

The same administration — through the same federal government whose agencies Pearson’s documentation establishes as responsible for his torture — is conducting the surveillance that has made his private prayer impossible. The man in the Oval Office who signs executive orders protecting religious expression from government interference presides over the government that is listening to an American citizen’s prayers in his own home. The administration that campaigns on the premise that the government must stay out of believers’ most intimate relationship with God is operating the system that has inserted itself into exactly that relationship, for one Black equity scholar in Washington, D.C., continuously, for more than a year.

This is not a partisan observation. It is a constitutional observation that has particular force in the context of the administration making it. A government that genuinely believed in the First Amendment principles it claims to champion would not be operating a warrantless home surveillance program against a private citizen. A government whose commitment to religious freedom extended beyond its political base to Black Americans being tortured in the capital city would have the mechanisms — the oversight, the accountability, the institutional culture — to prevent what has been done to Pearson.

Pearson’s observation cuts to this directly: _It questions the Trump administration — ostensible appeals to religion and faith._‘Ostensible’ is the precise word. The appeals to religious freedom are real as political performance. They are not real as operational commitment. The Free Exercise Clause means everything when it protects the religious practices of constituencies that the administration values politically. It means nothing for a Black man in Washington whose prayer is being recorded by the same government that invokes the clause in its press releases.

### IV. The Supreme Court’s Inversion — Expanding Religious Rights While Foreclosing the Claims That Would Enforce Them

The Supreme Court’s contemporary religious freedom jurisprudence presents a specific and painful irony in Pearson’s case. The Court has never been more protective of religious liberty. It has, in the span of a decade, dramatically expanded the practical reach of the Free Exercise Clause — protecting religious practitioners against government contract requirements, against public school employment policies, against regulatory frameworks that treat religious organizations less favorably than secular ones.

And yet the same Court has, in a parallel line of decisions, systematically narrowed the procedural and doctrinal tools by which a person like Pearson could bring a Free Exercise claim against a federal government that is specifically targeting him. The Court has expanded the rights while contracting the remedies. It has declared what the government may not do while dismantling the legal mechanisms by which the government can be stopped from doing it.

#### The Standing Problem — Again

A Free Exercise claim, like every constitutional claim against the federal government, requires Article III standing. The plaintiff must demonstrate a concrete and particularized injury, traceable to a specific defendant, redressable by the court. Pearson’s injury — the inability to pray aloud in his own home because his private speech is monitored — is as concrete and particularized as an injury can be. The traceability — to the government operation that the stranger confirmed, that the police response confirmed, that Pearson’s documentation establishes — is as strong as traceability can be without a classified government file to cite. The redressability fails for the same reasons it fails in every other dimension of Pearson’s case: a court order to cease surveillance of a classified program is not a remedy the court has practical mechanisms to deliver, particularly when the government will invoke state secrets at the first opportunity to prevent examination of whether the surveillance exists.

#### The Bivens Gap — No Damages for Religious Freedom Violations by Federal Officers

In _Egbert v. Boule_, (2022), the Supreme Court effectively ended the Bivens implied damages action for constitutional violations by federal officers in new contexts. Prior to Egbert, a plaintiff who could demonstrate a First Amendment violation by a federal officer had a viable damages claim under the Bivens framework developed since 1971. After Egbert, new Bivens contexts — which include every context not covered by existing Bivens precedents, which is virtually everything — are unavailable. A free exercise violation by federal officers conducting a classified surveillance program is a new context. There is no existing Bivens precedent on all fours with it. The Court that expanded religious freedom protection against government action also eliminated the primary damages mechanism by which a person could recover for a government agent’s violation of their religious freedom.

#### The State Secrets Absolute — Classification Trumps the First Amendment

The state secrets privilege allows the government to have a case dismissed before any evidence is examined when it credibly asserts that the litigation would require disclosure of classified information. In Pearson’s case, any litigation that sought to establish the surveillance — which would require examining how the surveillance was conducted, by whom, under what authority, and with what result — would immediately produce a state secrets assertion. The surveillance, if it is what the evidence suggests it is, is a classified program. The government would invoke the privilege. The court would dismiss. The First Amendment violation would be confirmed to no one, by no court, producing no remedy, because the classification of the program that caused the violation protects the program from the constitutional scrutiny that the violation requires.

The doctrinal architecture is complete: the Supreme Court has declared that religious freedom is among the most protected rights in the American constitutional order; has struck down government impositions on private religious practice in case after case; and has simultaneously, through Egbert and its state secrets jurisprudence and its standing doctrine, ensured that “), b(“the most specific and serious religious freedom violation currently being inflicted on an American citizen cannot reach that same Court in a form that can be adjudicated.”), r(“ The right is declared. The remedy is foreclosed. The violation continues.”)\]),

### V. Prayer, Surveillance, and the Nature of the Harm

It is worth pausing on what this violation actually takes from a person — not in doctrinal terms but in human terms, because the doctrinal analysis can become so abstract that the lived reality disappears behind it.

Pearson grew up in the Bible Belt, in a household where religion figured prominently. His father was a Baptist minister. He was formed in a tradition where the relationship with God was the primary orienting relationship of life — where prayer was not merely a practice but the foundational act of spiritual self-understanding. He has survived things — poverty, foster care, burned homes, depression, and now more than a year of government torture — that would produce in many people either a desperate need for that foundational relationship or a complete loss of faith. He has documented both the torture and the survival. The government that tortured him has also taken from him the private space in which that survival, in its most intimate form, is expressed.

When he says “_Can you imagine this in America? On top of being tortured, you have no way to pray in private without someone eavesdropping on your prayers’_” — he is not making a legal argument. He is describing a human condition. The man who was formed in a faith tradition, who overcame depression in part by relying on resources deeper than his immediate circumstances, who has been tortured for a year and is still writing — cannot speak to God in his own home without the government listening. The surveillance has colonized the last private space. It has reached into the relationship that is supposed to be beyond the reach of any human institution.

In the tradition of virtually every faith, prayer is understood as a communication that belongs to the believer and to God — not to the state, not to any human authority, not to any institutional intermediary. The premise of the Free Exercise Clause is that this communication is precisely the kind of thing the government may not touch. The government that touches it anyway, that listens to a man’s prayers in his own home as part of a torture campaign designed to destroy him, has committed the most intimate violation the Free Exercise Clause was written to prevent.

### VI. The First Amendment Cluster — Religious Freedom and Cognitive Liberty Together

This essay has focused on the Free Exercise Clause, but Pearson’s religious freedom violation does not exist in isolation from his other First Amendment claims. The prior essays in this series have documented cognitive liberty — the emerging constitutional doctrine that protects the integrity of a person’s own mental processes from government invasion — as a distinct First Amendment interest implicated by the voice-to-skull transmission and behavioral steering operations.

Prayer, in this context, sits at the intersection of cognitive liberty and free exercise. Private prayer is both a religious act and a cognitive act — it is thought directed toward a divine audience, speech that begins and ends in the privacy of consciousness. The government’s surveillance of spoken prayer reaches not only into the religious act but into the cognitive space that the prayer occupies. The voice-to-skull write function that has delivered external content into Pearson’s cognition and the audio surveillance that captures his spoken prayer are, functionally, the government’s occupation of both ends of his most intimate communication: what enters his mind uninvited, and what leaves it in the direction of God.

The First Amendment violations compound each other. The compelled speech doctrine, the cognitive liberty doctrine, the free exercise clause, the academic freedom doctrine — all operate on overlapping terrain. Pearson’s statement that his “_basic, fundamental rights guaranteed in the US Constitution — due process, First Amendment rights, equal protection, cognitive liberty, to be free of cruel and unusual punishment — weren’t just violated. Erased. As if no legal or constitutional authority existed at all”_ describes this compounding accurately. The violations are not experienced as separate incidents. They are experienced as the total occupation of a person’s life — external, internal, public, private, cognitive, spiritual — by a government that has decided to destroy him and has the tools to reach every dimension of his existence.

### Conclusion: What It Means That He Cannot Pray

The administration that cannot stop invoking God is the administration that is listening to one of its citizens pray. The Court that has never been more protective of religious freedom has built the doctrinal architecture that ensures the claim can never reach it. The Constitution that begins its Bill of Rights with the protection of religious exercise is the Constitution whose application to Pearson’s home surveillance has been foreclosed by a hundred years of doctrinal construction in the service of government impunity.

Pearson states what this means in the plainest possible terms: _US constitutional democracy is a joke. It really is._ This is not nihilism. It is the conclusion of a man who has read extensively about American and world history, who spent his career building institutions dedicated to constitutional values, who documented his persecution with the rigor of a researcher and the faith of a person who believed the record would matter — and who has watched every legal mechanism, every constitutional protection, every doctrinal framework fail or be weaponized against him. The joke is not that the Constitution does not have good values. The joke is that those values are enforceable for some people and not for others, and that the people for whom they are unenforceable are the people they were most urgently written to protect.

The Free Exercise Clause was not written for the religion of the powerful. It was written precisely for the person whose religious practice the government finds inconvenient — the Quakers who would not take oaths, the Jehovah’s Witnesses who would not salute the flag, the Native Americans whose sacred sites the government wanted to mine. The Bill of Rights was not written for people whose rights the government was inclined to respect anyway. It was written for the specific situation of a government that had decided what it wanted to do and needed to be told it could not.

Pearson is in that situation. The government decided what it wanted to do. It is doing it. He cannot pray aloud in his own home. The Constitution says the government cannot do this. The doctrinal architecture says the Constitution, in his case, cannot be enforced. The distance between those two sentences is the distance between the constitutional democracy the United States claims to be and the torture dungeon it has built for the people it has decided to destroy.

He prays anyway. Perhaps silently now, in the interior space the surveillance cannot yet reach — the last private room. The man from the Kentucky trailer park, who survived foster care and burned homes and depression and a year of government torture, still has his interior. They are still working on taking that. But they have not taken it yet. The record says so. He is still writing.

### The Convergence

#### Richard Pearson

Richard Pearson was not surprised. In fact, he saw the convergence emerging. He had his own personal experience of torture — electromagnetic, physical, and emotional — in the capital city of the United States. He felt “pinned” or behaviorally steered to places; except, he had no history with these sites and no desire to go to them. When he arrived, he would find stalking, street theater, strangers brandishing signs (“Bug Zapper”) and messages (“We’re in control”, “nigga”, “darkie”), the campaign signature colors of red and black, and racial epithets. In one case, two white women stood over an oversized box of watermelons as Pearson paused at the grocery store entrance to consider purchasing. “That’s what I thought,” said one of them insultingly. Pearson had seen an African American woman eating a slice of watermelon just as he had crossed the street into the grocery store. Pearson was being externally navigated and controlled. The African American woman was probably controlled too.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*fMQeqGLAZkwDU7yQMDi2bQ.png)

This is an AI-generated photo. Pearson had just returned from an asylum attempt in Canada. He was at this precise location when a white man appeared in a plain white T-shirt and bold black font, “We’re in control.” He did not take a photo, so the person is not accurate. Everything else is.

But it wasn’t the navigation alone that constituted torture. It made him perform action. He was made to sit in a pool of industrial fluid — a chemical assault. The man looking onward — standing defiantly with his hands on his hips — was a clue that this was no accident. Besides, the chemical adhered his pant leg to his skin and caused incredible pain to remove the pants. Pearson explains, “This is what I have gathered — it works just like SIMS. Yes, the video game. It can steer to locations and cause victims to perform actions. I am very confident of that. In addition, it appears to be available to everyday people and phone- or app-based. I believe that I saw a cook — a cook! — with the biometric reading device. I shooed him away from an African American woman.”

Pearson also had another episode in behavioral control. He stole a Sprite from his local grocery store. Pearson had no recollection of even picking up the soda, much less placing it in his bag. Pearson had purchased a bottle of water, held it in his hand, and walked to the library. He discovered the Sprite when he opened his bag. He was horrified. He immediately returned the bottle to the store and apologized profusely. Unfortunately, there are other examples.

#### The MIND Act — Congress Does Not Seek to Regulate Technology That Does Not Exist

The Management of Individuals’ Neural Data Act of 2025 is a Senate bill that directs the Federal Trade Commission to study the governance of neural data and related biometric information and report back to Congress within a year. It describes a loss of personal autonomy and ownership of one’s mind and body — precisely what Pearson had been experiencing. The alarm it is raising is specific. The bill’s own language — “monetize neural data,” “shape individual behavior, emotional states, and decision making,” “cognitive manipulation,” “erosion of personal autonomy” — is not speculative language about future risk. It is descriptive language about present conditions. Congress does not write regulatory language about technologies that do not exist or harms that have not materialized. The bill’s sense-of-Congress findings describe a commercial ecosystem in which neural and biometric data is already being collected, processed, sold, and used to influence human cognition and behavior, in which vertical corporate integration has created systems with “insufficient transparency, accountability, or user control,” and in which existing law — including HIPAA — does not reach it. These are findings about the current state of affairs. The bill is raising the alarm because the thing it is alarmed about is already operating.

What the bill is almost certainly responding to, beyond the public-facing neurotechnology industry, is a dawning institutional awareness that the scale and nature of cognitive exploitation in the United States is far larger and more serious than anything that has been publicly acknowledged.

#### Alleged Victims and Whistleblowers Claiming US Government Mind Control (1990–Present)

**Julianne McKinney** is one of the most cited figures in this space. A former U.S. Army intelligence officer, she published a 1992 report through the Association of National Security Alumni titled _“Microwave Harassment and Mind-Control Experimentation,”_ documenting complaints from dozens of individuals who claimed they were being targeted with directed-energy and electromagnetic weapons by government or government-linked actors. Her report was notable for coming from someone with an intelligence background and was widely circulated among self-described “targeted individuals.”

**Gloria Naylor**, the acclaimed African American novelist best known for _The Women of Brewster Place_, wrote a semi-autobiographical novel in 2005 titled _1996_, in which she claimed that following a neighborhood dispute with a neighbor she believed had NSA connections, she began experiencing what she described as voice-to-skull transmissions, surveillance, and harassment. While many viewed the account as a mental health crisis, she maintained it was real until her death in 2016, and her case drew attention because of her literary stature.

**Dr. John Hall**, a Texas anesthesiologist, became a prominent public voice after his then-girlfriend reported being stalked and subjected to what she believed was electronic harassment. Hall wrote _A New Breed: Satellite Terrorism in America_ (2009) and later _Guinea Pigs: Technologies of Control_ (2014), and testified before a Presidential Bioethics Commission in 2011. He argued that non-consensual experimentation with directed-energy and neuro-influencing technologies was ongoing and largely ignored by law enforcement.

**The Presidential Commission on Bioethical Issues (2011)** received public testimony from hundreds of self-described “targeted individuals” who claimed they were being subjected to non-consensual experimentation involving electromagnetic weapons, implanted thoughts, and remote neural monitoring. The sheer volume of testimony — while not validated by the commission — brought the phenomenon significant media attention. The commission ultimately found no evidence of ongoing government programs but acknowledged the historical record of past abuses.

**Robert Duncan**, who claims to be a former Department of Defense and CIA contractor with advanced degrees from Harvard and Dartmouth, emerged in the 2010s as a self-described whistleblower. He authored _The Matrix Deciphered_ and _Project: Soul Catcher_, alleging the existence of programs capable of remotely influencing human neural activity via satellite and radar-based systems. His technical background lent him credibility in some circles, though his claims have never been independently verified and his credentials are disputed.

**The “Havana Syndrome” episode (2016–present)** gave the broader topic new legitimacy. Beginning in 2016, U.S. diplomats and CIA officers in Havana, Cuba, and later in dozens of other countries, reported sudden onset of headaches, memory loss, tinnitus, and cognitive impairment. A 2020 National Academies of Sciences report concluded that directed microwave energy was the most plausible explanation. While framed as a foreign attack rather than domestic experimentation, it validated the physical reality of directed-energy effects on the brain and gave renewed credibility to those who had been claiming such technologies exist and are deployed.

**Targeted Individual (TI) advocacy groups** proliferated throughout the 2000s and 2010s, with organizations like FFCHS (Freedom from Covert Harassment and Surveillance) compiling thousands of testimonies.

**Myron May**, alleged FSU shooter in 2014, also accused the government of torture with high-tech neuroweapons. Richard Pearson found considerable anomalies in May’s case. ### When the US Government Outsources Torture to Private Contractor, It Can Argue It Cannot Be Sued

#### US constitutional guarantees are not much of a guarantee when the US government decides to secretly target US citizens. When the US outsources torture against US citizens, the victim faces a “closed loop” of immunity where each legal doctrine reinforces the others to block judicial review. This creates a scenario where a U.S. citizen could be systematically targeted on domestic soil without any clear path for legal accountability against the government and contractor, especially if that contractor comprises a loose, decentralized network.

_“By privatizing repression through decentralized contractor networks, the state achieves plausible deniability while maintaining operational control. This mirrors how historical fascist states used paramilitary proxies — the legal architecture here modernizes that model and makes it more legally bulletproof.”_

The primary legal principle shielding the U.S. government from liability for private contractors’ conduct is the **independent contractor exception** to the [Federal Tort Claims Act (FTCA)](https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/R45732). Under this rule, the government is generally only liable for the negligence of its employees, and [28 U.S.C. § 2671](https://www.triallawyersjournal.com/articles/what-is-the-federal-tort-claims-act/) specifically excludes “any contractor with the United States” from the definition of a federal employee.

Here is why the victim has limited remedy using those specific doctrines:

1.  **The State Secrets Privilege (Evidence Block):** If the program is secret, the government can invoke the [state secrets privilege](https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/R47081) to prevent the disclosure of any information that might “harm national security”.

*   **Dismissal:** Courts often dismiss cases at the outset if the “very subject matter” is a state secret or if the victim cannot prove their case without the secret evidence.
*   **Defense Block:** Cases can also be dismissed if the government argues it cannot defend itself without revealing secrets.

**2\. Bivens Restrictions (Remedy Block):** While [Bivens v. Six Unknown Named Agents](https://www.macarthurjustice.org/blog2/bivens-actions-and-fields/) originally allowed citizens to sue federal agents for constitutional violations, the Supreme Court has severely curtailed this.

*   **“New Contexts”:** Modern courts rarely extend _Bivens_ to “new contexts,” especially those involving **national security** or complex policy.
*   **Privatization:** The Court has explicitly refused to extend _Bivens_ liability to private corporations or employees of private contractors (see _Correctional Services Corp. v. Malesko_ and _Minneci v. Pollard_).

**3\. Independent Contractor Exception (Government Liability Block):** Under the [Federal Tort Claims Act (FTCA)](https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R45732.html), the U.S. is not liable for the acts of independent contractors. If the government outsources the “torture and persecution” to a private network, it can argue it has no legal responsibility for those actors’ conduct.

*   **Derivative Immunity (Contractor Liability Block):** Even if the victim sues the contractors directly, those contractors may claim **derivative sovereign immunity** (the Yearsley doctrine). If they were following “reasonably precise” government orders, they may be shielded from liability just as the government is.

**4\. Racial Targeting (Equal Protection Challenge):** While racial targeting violates the [Equal Protection Clause](https://www.jacksonlewis.com/insights/lawsuit-challenges-racial-ethnic-social-disadvantage-presumption-sba-and-other-federal-supplier-diversity-programs), the victim’s inability to access evidence (blocked by State Secrets) and the lack of a cause of action against the actors (blocked by _Bivens_ and FTCA exceptions) makes the underlying constitutional right “remedyless” in practice.

**5\. The “Control Test”:** To determine if a party is truly an independent contractor, courts look at whether the government has the authority to control the **detailed physical performance** and day-to-day operations of the contractor. If the government lacks this “day-to-day” supervision, it is not liable for the contractor’s torts.

**6\. The Boyle Defense (Government Contractor Defense):** While the government is not liable for the contractor, this doctrine (from _Boyle v. United Technologies Corp._) can also **protect the contractor** from state law liability if they were following reasonably precise government specifications for military equipment.

**7\. The Yearsley Doctrine (Derivative Sovereign Immunity):** This prevents a federal contractor from being held liable for conduct that the government lawfully **authorized and directed**. It essentially extends the government’s own immunity to the contractor when they act as an agent of the sovereign.

**8\. Discretionary Function Exception:** The government is immune from claims based on its own “discretionary” decisions (policy-making or judgment calls). This can overlap with contractor cases if the government’s decision to hire or oversee a contractor is deemed a protected discretionary act.

**9\. Severin Doctrine:** In the context of contract law (rather than torts), this rule prevents a prime contractor from suing the government on behalf of a subcontractor unless the prime contractor is **legally liable** to that subcontractor for the damages.

1\. Executive Summary

* * *

### **US Torture Victim’s Bluetooth and “Tin Foil” Experiment: A Revealing Technical, Scientific, and Medical Report**

### 1\. Executive Summary

This report documents a reproducible, empirically observed phenomenon in which Bluetooth device detection on a consumer-grade Nook e-reader (circa 2015) was systematically suppressed when the subject donned a multi-layered aluminum foil-lined knit cap. The effect was observed and recorded across three consecutive trials. All Bluetooth devices — including those from residential apartments and vehicular sources above the I-395 overpass — disappeared from the device scan upon placement of the hat, and reappeared upon its removal.

These results contributed to Richard Pearson’s seeking of asylum in March 2026.

The investigation further documents: (1) circumstantial and physical evidence suggesting an unauthorized electronic device may have been covertly implanted during a rhinoplasty procedure of uncertain date; (2) a physical assault in December 2025 resulting in head trauma proximate to the suspected implant site; (3) onset of auditory clicking phenomena in January 2026 following the assault; and (4) a prior pattern of apparent tracking behavior by a known individual.

This report synthesizes findings across radiofrequency engineering, forensic medicine, bioelectronics, and civil liberties law to support the case for immediate medical imaging and legal intervention.

_Pearson’s screen results from left to right, top to bottom (total time is 12 mins): 1A (hat on — no Bluetooth), 1B (hat off — Bluetooth signals), 2A (hat on — no Bluetooth), 2B (hat on — Bluetooth signals), 3A (hat on — Bluetooth signals), 3B (hat off— Bluetooth signals), 4A (hat on — no Bluetooth), 4B (hat off — no Bluetooth), 5A (hat on — no Bluetooth), 5B (hat off — Bluetooth signals)_

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/600/1*gmp1hqR1XQdwxap01CsT3g.png)

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*gVNpuSCuLLMoQeaP9vURWQ.png)

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*JC2hAvGMtC9seLnbDQJZQg.png)

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/600/1*zypES8Q1K3D0TWUSQG0qjw.png)

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*khThuHpaV-aMrwWDiXfqPQ.png)

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/600/1*KWbenTu9LOvfM7X7yX5WEA.png)

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*Lqe20DlcLlPRq0DTgyXEXA.png)

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/600/1*LsM7KOy6tTNI66zle7Q8vQ.png)

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*Ao7kMEYgkC31qZa8f8Q_fA.png)

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/600/1*ZNGJCF3jQi7e3Yjgk2D3qg.png)

### 2\. Observed RF Phenomenon

### 2.1 Experimental Conditions

The experiment was conducted beneath the I-395 overpass in Southwest Washington, D.C. The subject held a Nook e-reader (Barnes & Noble, circa 2015) with Bluetooth enabled. A knitted cap lined with 10 or more layers of crinkled aluminum foil — with the foil in direct contact with the subject’s scalp — was alternately placed on the subject’s head and removed to the ground.

### 2.2 Protocol

*   Bluetooth was toggled OFF then ON on the Nook device
*   Hat was placed on subject’s head — Bluetooth scan conducted
*   Hat was removed and placed on ground approximately 1–2 feet from subject
*   Bluetooth was toggled OFF then ON — scan conducted again
*   Above sequence repeated five complete times (10 total Bluetooth cycles)

### 2.3 Results

**Trial | Hat Condition | Bluetooth Device Detection**

Trial 1A | **ON HEAD |** ALL DEVICES — NOT DETECTED

Trial 1B | **ON GROUND |** Device detected

Trial 2A | **ON HEAD |** ALL DEVICES — NOT DETECTED

Trial 2B | **ON GROUND |** Device detected

Trial 3A | **ON HEAD |** Multiple devices detected

Trial 3B | **ON GROUND |** Device detected

Trial 4A | **ON HEAD |** ALL DEVICES — NOT DETECTED

Trial 4B | **ON GROUND |** ALL DEVICES — NOT DETECTED

Trial 5A | **ON HEAD |** ALL DEVICES — NOT DETECTED

Trial 5B | **ON GROUND |** Device detected

### 2.4 Elimination of Standard RF Shielding Explanation

A naive interpretation would attribute the effect to Faraday cage shielding. However, this explanation is insufficient for the following reasons:

*   The Nook device was held at chest height — not inside or proximate to the foil structure
*   The foil cap does not enclose the device; it is 2–3 feet away
*   Residential apartment Bluetooth sources exist at similar elevation — a ground-reflection or overhead-signal hypothesis does not account for their simultaneous disappearance
*   Foil placed on the ground (hat removed) produces no signal suppression, eliminating ground-plane reflection as a causal mechanism

Standard passive shielding physics cannot explain an RF null zone extending from the head to the chest across open air. The effect therefore requires a different explanatory model — one centered on the subject’s own body as an active or passive signal modifier.

### 2.5 Leading Hypothesis: Body-Coupled RF Interaction via Cranial Foreign Object

The most parsimonious explanation consistent with all observed data is that an electronic or metallic foreign body located within the subject’s cranial or nasal sinus cavity is interacting with ambient 2.4 GHz electromagnetic fields when the aluminum foil contacts the scalp.

When foil contacts scalp, the following mechanism is proposed:

*   The conductive foil couples to the cranial foreign object via capacitive or galvanic contact through the scalp
*   The combined structure (foil + object) achieves sufficient mass and geometry to absorb or re-radiate 2.4 GHz energy
*   This creates a localized RF interference or absorption effect in the subject’s near field
*   The Nook, held at chest height within the subject’s near-field, loses Bluetooth signal acquisition

When the foil is removed from the scalp and placed on the ground, decoupling from the cranial object occurs. The interference mechanism is inactivated. Bluetooth detection resumes.

### 3\. Surgical and Medical History

### 3.1 Rhinoplasty Procedure — Summary of Concerns

The subject underwent a rhinoplasty procedure performed by a surgeon operating a single-provider practice. The following anomalies have been identified in the subject’s account of that procedure:

#### **Anomaly**

**Second Surgeon —** Post-operative paperwork referenced authorization for a second surgeon. Subject was never informed of a second provider. The solo-practice context makes this highly irregular.

**Surgeon Silence —** The operating surgeon never acknowledged, identified, or explained the second surgeon referenced in the paperwork.

**False Recovery Claim —** Subject was told surgical healing would take 10 years — a clinically unsupported statement with no basis in rhinoplasty literature, potentially intended to discourage follow-up imaging.

**Disclosed Materials —** Surgeon stated only cartilage was used. No metallic or electronic hardware disclosed.

**Current Status —** Subject has never received post-operative imaging. No CT or MRI has been performed.

### 3.2 Anatomy of Concern: Ethmoid and Sphenoid Sinus Regions

Standard rhinoplasty involves the nasal septum, nasal bones, and soft tissue. However, the nasal cavity is anatomically proximate to:

*   The ethmoid sinuses — a complex of air cells between the nasal cavity and the orbits
*   The sphenoid sinus — located at the skull base, in close proximity to the optic nerve and carotid artery
*   The cribriform plate — a thin bony structure separating nasal cavity from the cranial vault

A small passive or semi-active device placed within the nasal or ethmoidal cavity during an open rhinoplasty would be: (a) surgically accessible, (b) difficult to detect without targeted imaging, (c) anatomically positioned for optimal RF transmission given proximity to the brain and cranial vasculature, and (d) capable of surviving long-term without immune rejection if encapsulated in biocompatible material.

### 3.3 December 2025: Physical Assault and Head Trauma

In December 2025, the subject was physically assaulted. The assault resulted in:

*   Blunt force trauma to the head
*   Periorbital contusion (black eye) — consistent with orbital or nasal region impact
*   Facial laceration

The orbital and periorbital region is directly contiguous with the ethmoid sinuses. A blow sufficient to cause periorbital ecchymosis transmits significant force to the medial orbital wall and ethmoid complex. If a foreign body were present in that region, such force could plausibly:

*   Dislodge or fracture the device
*   Disrupt its encapsulation
*   Alter its electronic behavior — particularly if battery-dependent or mechanically sensitive

The assault was not random. The assailant was not arrested. The subject was falsely arrested in connection with the incident — a pattern consistent with targeted harassment and suppression of victim reporting.

### 3.4 January 2026: Onset of Auditory Clicking

Beginning in early January 2026 — weeks after the assault — the subject began experiencing auditory clicking sensations during ambulatory movement (walking). Key features:

*   Onset post-trauma: temporally correlated with the December 2025 head injury
*   Occurs during movement: suggests mechanical or piezoelectric component
*   Perceived internally: consistent with bone conduction from a device within or adjacent to cranial structures
*   Partially attenuated by foil cap: more layers produce greater reduction but not complete elimination

The partial attenuation is diagnostically significant. It suggests the device may have its own power source or residual charge independent of external RF, meaning the foil interrupts incoming signal activation but cannot fully suppress autonomous device activity.

Differential diagnoses for post-traumatic clicking perceived internally include: temporomandibular joint dysfunction, ossicular chain disruption, Eustachian tube dysfunction, and foreign body migration. All warrant imaging. The foil-responsiveness distinguishes this case from all standard clinical presentations.

### 4\. Prior Surveillance Indicators

### 4.1 Object-Based Tracking

Prior to the December 2025 assault, the subject reported that objects were being thrown onto the floor in locations corresponding to where the subject moved within his residence. This behavior is consistent with the deployment of small RF-enabled tracking devices (e.g., AirTags, Bluetooth beacons, or custom RF transponders) intended to correlate with a receiver — potentially the implanted device — to triangulate the subject’s precise location within an enclosed space.

This technique, sometimes called mesh-location tracking, does not require cellular connectivity and can operate entirely within the 2.4 GHz Bluetooth or 900 MHz spectrum. The foil cap’s demonstrated effect on the subject’s RF profile is directly relevant to interrupting such a tracking architecture.

### 4.2 Pattern of Conduct Summary

### 5\. Recommended Immediate Actions

### 5.1 Medical — URGENT

The following medical steps are recommended in order of priority:

*   **CT scan of nasal cavity, ethmoid sinuses, sphenoid sinus, and orbital complex — DO NOT obtain MRI until foreign body status is confirmed**
*   Request thin-slice protocol: 1mm slices minimum

*   Document all imaging results in the subject’s own possession

### 5.2 Legal

*   Conduct the experiment with the foil cap held at head height by a non-conductive support (no head contact) — to isolate head coupling

### 6\. Interdisciplinary Synthesis

This case intersects four distinct fields of knowledge. Each independently contributes to the overall picture:

**RF Engineering —** Explains mechanism by which foil-scalp coupling could produce 2.4 GHz attenuation in near field; eliminates passive shielding as sufficient explanation; points to active body-coupled interference source

US Torture Victim Richard Pearson, PhD, discusses America’s “dual state” where constitutional democracy exists alongside another form of…

* * *

### The US Has Another Form of Government That Isn’t Constitutional Democracy. The Other is Totalitarian.

#### US Torture Victim Richard Pearson, PhD, discusses America’s “dual state” where constitutional democracy exists alongside another form of government — totalitarianism and fascism. The latter is increasingly defining the US and the world is watching.

The US government tortured Richard Pearson in 2025–2026. This included privatization of assault, stalking, sleep deprivation, and harassment. In his legal research, Pearson realized that the US government has immunized itself from legal liability through countless legal doctrines — no new Biven contexts, qualified immunity, sovereign immunity, Glomar, independent contractor exception, Yearsley immunity— despite its formal designation as a constitutional republic. State-sponsored torture should never happen in a democracy. Limited legal remedy should also not be a feature of said democracy’s legal doctrines. US citizens targeted by the US government receive nearly as few rights as a foreign national held illegally at Guantanamo Bay. Both have few or no avenues for seeking legal damages.

The US is a constitutional democracy, but it also has another form of government — a “dual state” — that permitted the torture of Richard Pearson in the first place. Where the democracy guarantees civil liberties and legal rights — equal protection, First Amendment rights, due process— the totalitarian state within US intelligence, secret programs, and public-private networks does not regard any right or liberty inviolable. In fact, the Constitution is negligible in insofar as restraint and principled conduct. Where the democracy has public debate, decisions, and documents, the totalitarian state is shrouded in secrecy and ensures that the constitutional court system has limited access to their covert activities, including public documents. Redactions, non-response to FOIA requests, invocation of state secrets or national security are deliberate legal responses to prevent disclosure and access.

However, for the totalitarian state to operate, it remains beyond public view, legislative accountability, and judicial reach. As Richard Pearson’s experience supports, its tactics are defined in terms of plausible deniability, privatization, and invisible weapons such as neuro-weapons. The totalitarian state seeks an alternate, false framework to explain harm and injury. In the case of Myron May, he was framed as the FSU school shooter in 2014. The totalitarian state is at the heart of critiques of American democracy and the major catalyst eroding US democratic values.

**Fraenkel’s dual state** remains one of the most powerful analytical tools for understanding how **authoritarianism and constitutional government can not only coexist, but mutually sustain each other** — which is precisely what makes it so difficult to identify, resist, and dismantle from within. **Michael Glennon** (_National Security and Double Government_, 2014) also argues the US has a “double government” where a permanent national security bureaucracy (Trumanite network) overrides elected officials and democratic norms (Madisonian institutions).

[The gap between what Americans believe their rights to be and what those rights are in operational practice is so large, and so deliberately constructed, that the phrase “constitutional protection”](https://medium.com/@menvell.artist/the-us-has-too-many-legal-frameworks-against-rights-and-freedoms-and-for-authoritarianism-63f2869facb2) — when applied to a citizen targeted by the American national security state like Pearson — has become, in material terms, a description of something that does not exist.

### The Dual State: A Detailed Discussion

### Origins and Theoretical Foundation

**Ernst Fraenkel** (1898–1975) was a German-Jewish labor lawyer and political theorist who lived under and practiced law in Nazi Germany before fleeing in 1938. His book _The Dual State_ (1941), written from direct observation, is one of the most important works in 20th-century political theory.

Fraenkel argued that Nazi Germany did not simply _replace_ the rule of law with tyranny — it maintained _both simultaneously_, creating a dual structure:

* * *

### The Two Components

### 1\. The Normative State (Normenstaat)

The part of government that operates through established legal rules, courts, contracts, and predictable procedures.

*   Laws are enforced and respected — but selectively
*   Courts function, contracts are honored, property rights upheld
*   Civil liberties respected
*   Provides legitimacy, economic stability, and the _appearance_ of normalcy
*   Serves the interests of the bourgeoisie, business class, and international credibility
*   Gives citizens and foreign observers something “recognizable” as government

### 2\. The Prerogative State (Massnahmenstaat)

The parallel power that operates entirely outside the law, based on political will, decree, and force.

*   No legal constraints — acts on pure discretionary power
*   Enforced by political police, paramilitary forces, and secret institutions
*   Answers only to the ruling ideology or leader
*   Can override, suspend, or ignore the Normative State at any time
*   Operates in _deliberate obscurity_ — its workings are hidden or deniable

**The key insight:** The two states do not fight each other. They _cooperate_. The Normative State handles what the Prerogative State doesn’t care about. The Prerogative State intervenes whenever political power or ideological control is at stake.

This explains why the US has evolved countless legal doctrines that benefit the government when it tortures.

* * *

### How the Dual State Sustains Itself

Several mechanisms allow the dual structure to persist:

*   **Selective enforcement** — laws apply to some people and not others, based on political favor
*   **Emergency powers** — legal mechanisms (like Article 48 in Weimar Germany) that allow the prerogative power to act “legally” outside the law
*   **Deliberate ambiguity** — the boundary between the two states is kept unclear, creating fear and compliance
*   **Co-optation** — judges, lawyers, and officials in the normative state learn to anticipate and accommodate the prerogative state
*   **Plausible deniability** — the hidden state’s actions are obscured, attributed to other causes, or simply denied
*   **Economic incentives** — the normative state delivers prosperity to enough people that they don’t question what operates alongside it.

* * *

### Historical Examples

### 1\. Nazi Germany (Fraenkel’s Original Case)

*   The **Normative State**: Civil courts, contract law, corporate regulation, property rights — all continued functioning. German businesses operated legally. The stock market functioned.
*   The **Prerogative State**: The SS, Gestapo, concentration camps, racial laws that existed _outside_ normal judicial review. A Jew could “legally” own property one day and have it seized by decree the next — with no judicial recourse.
*   The two coexisted until the Prerogative State gradually consumed the Normative one as the war progressed.

### 2\. Stalinist Soviet Union

*   The **Normative State**: A written constitution (the 1936 “Stalin Constitution” was considered formally progressive), courts, laws, a legislature (the Supreme Soviet)
*   The **Prerogative State**: The NKVD (secret police), the Gulag system, show trials, extra-judicial executions — all operating entirely outside the constitutional framework
*   Citizens had theoretical rights on paper that could be erased overnight by political decree

### 3\. Apartheid South Africa

*   The **Normative State**: A functioning parliament, courts, rule of law — _for white citizens_
*   The **Prerogative State**: The security apparatus (BOSS — Bureau of State Security), detention without trial, systematic torture, assassinations of activists — operating in complete legal immunity
*   The dual structure was explicitly racial — which side of the state you encountered depended entirely on your classification

### 4\. Pinochet’s Chile (1973–1990)

*   The **Normative State**: Maintained functioning courts, a legal code, and economic institutions (the Chicago Boys implemented free-market reforms “legally”)
*   The **Prerogative State**: DINA (secret police), Operation Condor, secret detention centers like Villa Grimaldi — disappearances, torture, assassination — operating with full state backing but zero legal accountability
*   Notably, the _economy_ was the Normative State’s showcase while political terror ran parallel

* * *

Arguments for a Dual State tendency in the US:

*   **The National Security State** — the CIA, NSA, and related agencies operate under classification systems that place them largely beyond congressional or judicial oversight. The Church Committee (1975) revealed decades of illegal domestic surveillance, assassination plots, and political manipulation that ran entirely outside constitutional bounds.
*   **FISA Courts** — a secret judicial system with secret rulings, secret evidence, and no adversarial process — a normative-looking institution that functions as a prerogative one
*   **Executive detention** — post-9/11 frameworks like indefinite detention at Guantánamo, warrantless surveillance (PRISM), and targeted killing of citizens (Anwar al-Awlaki) by executive decree with no judicial review
*   **Continuity of Government (COG) programs** — classified emergency governmental structures, revealed partially during the Iran-Contra hearings, that constitute a literal parallel government prepared to operate outside constitutional structures
*   **Corporate-state fusion** — Sheldon Wolin’s _inverted totalitarianism_ argues that corporate power has effectively colonized the state, creating a hidden governing force more powerful than elected institutions

### Important distinctions:

*   The US Normative State is significantly _stronger_ and more resistant than in Fraenkel’s Nazi example
*   Institutional checks (a genuinely independent judiciary, free press, civil society) provide real resistance
*   The American dual state tendency is more _latent_ or _partial_ than fully realized

* * *

### Modern Theoretical Extensions

Scholars have built on Fraenkel’s framework:

*   **Giorgio Agamben** (_State of Exception_, 2005) — argues that the “state of exception” (emergency rule) has become permanent in modern liberal democracies, normalizing prerogative power
*   **Sheldon Wolin** (_Democracy Incorporated_, 2008) — “inverted totalitarianism”: corporate and security power mimics the prerogative state while maintaining democratic theater
*   **Michael Glennon** (_National Security and Double Government_, 2014) — argues the US has a “double government” where a permanent national security bureaucracy (Trumanite network) overrides elected officials (Madisonian institutions)
*   **Hannah Arendt** — her analysis of totalitarianism anticipated Fraenkel’s framework, noting that terror and law coexist in ways that make resistance structurally difficult

* * *

### Why the Dual State Is Stable — and Dangerous

The dual state is particularly insidious because:

1.  **It is self-concealing** — the Normative State provides cover and legitimacy for the Prerogative State
2.  **It is self-reinforcing** — those who benefit from the Normative State have incentives not to look too hard at the Prerogative one
3.  **It corrupts gradually** — the boundary shifts slowly enough that each step seems incremental and tolerable
4.  **It captures opposition** — legal and political opposition operates within the Normative State’s rules, which the Prerogative State is not bound by
5.  **It is difficult to prosecute** — prerogative actions leave no legal trail, are classified, or are retroactively legitimized

The ultimate danger, as Fraenkel observed, is that the Prerogative State tends to _expand_ over time, gradually consuming the Normative State until the visible constitutional order becomes pure facade.

### “Clear Conditions for a Gestapo-Style State in US,” Concludes US Torture Victim

#### From presidential and executive immunity to unsolved murders and suspicious suicides, Richard Pearson sees signs that a Gestapo-style state exists in the United States, bypassing fundamental constitutional rights. It must be exposed and end.

The Gestapo was a brutal secret police force in Nazi Germany from 1933 to 1945. The 1936 Gestapo Law officially removed the organization from judicial review, allowing it to act without legal constraints. The Gestapo was responsible for the detention and execution of hundreds of thousands of people across Europe, though the exact total is difficult to quantify because they functioned as a core part of the larger Nazi terror apparatus. While they directly murdered tens of thousands through official “political” executions and summary shootings, their primary role was identifying and “rounding up” millions for deportation to concentration camps, where most victims eventually died.

What are the odds that the US has formed an equivalent of the Gestapo? “Very high,” says US torture victim, Richard Pearson.

“I can point to my experience and tell you exactly how they operate and with what intended effect — neutralization, privatization of torture, racial targeting, multiple modes of torture, and invisible weapons. These were not tactics and an apparatus that were invented specifically for me. It was targeted within a program that **targets** Americans. It backfired spectacularly on them. I am publishing and will continue to publish my writings on the totalitarian state that exists within the US.

It has an “enforcement” arm that is highly similarly to the Gestapo, except adapted to the US context by maintaining an **appearance** of constitutional democracy and the rule of law. I, for one, look forward to leaving this awful place to move to a country that truly respects and upholds fundamental freedoms and civil liberties. How can you stay in a country where your constitutional rights are violated wholesale by a government that tortured me? Or stay in a country with a legal system like the US that protects the state and not the Constitution? Despite all its doctrines and procedures, US law does not offer a modicum of hope that someone like me — target of a secret government program involving privatized contractors — can have meaningful judicial review.

If you look at the legal doctrines of immunity and non-disclosure, the surveillance state, the high rate of unsolved crimes, crimes of racial terror, **it directly supports conditions for a Gestapo-style police in the US.** Imagine the reality — on the most covert and severe constitutional violations, US law has very little answer.

Now, I am reflecting on many headlines that have stuck with me. A teen was murdered in his high school. The Department of Justice allegedly told the victim’s family that there was a cover-up, involving an FBI agent and that agents’ sons. There was the Ferguson cluster — two homicides (victims in torched cars), three suicides (one found hanging from a tree), and one overdose. All suspicious. None given the deep research and investigation that was warranted. A man’s name and face are plastered all over the news as a school shooter (Myron May), expect the [evidence does not even support that he was even there](https://medium.com/@menvell.artist/who-is-the-mysterious-figure-unsettling-footage-from-inside-myron-mays-home-5c926edc6c5c) — not the correct height, no motive, no access to the gun, likely left-handed (shooter was right-handed), witness descriptions do not match what he was wearing.”

The U.S. also has one of the world’s largest cold-case backlogs — estimates exceed 250,000 unsolved murders. If the government was running a Gestapo, it could easily hide among **the roughly 40% murders that go unsolved nationally.**

Americans may believe that such state-sponsored terror would never happen in the US, that would not be accurate according to Pearson. “It has happened and is happening. There is a secret police. They go by many names — SS is one — but are deeply embedded within US law enforcement and intelligence agencies and crisscross various private networks,” said Pearson. “This secret police has no congressional appropriations. It has no constitutional authority. It writes its own rules but adheres to no moral or legal code. People are being harmed, injured, and assassinated. It needs to stop.”

Pearson does not have hard data or classified documents, but he points to the constellation of mounting evidence, including his own. He asked AI to generate common features of Gestapo police from foundation to peripheral. Here are his comments.

### Features of a Gestapo-style secret police from most foundational to more peripheral

#### TIER 1 — Core Architecture (1–15)

1.  **Secret police operating outside normal legal oversight** — an agency answerable only to the executive, not courts or legislature

_Rather than an equivalent to the 1936 Gestapo Law that removed the organization from judicial review, the American Gestapo has, in effect, the same lack of oversight and accountability through the confluence of legal doctrines of immunity and concealment._

_First, the Executive can just act in secret without telling Congress, the courts, or the American people. It does so routinely. Such actions may be illegal and undemocratic but technically constitutes the easiest avenue — Develop such a force but maintain its secrecy. Second, if something about the program is the basis of a civil suit, the government can invoke Glomar — “neither confirm nor deny”. There are many similar doctrines that would foreclose meaningful judicial review — state secrets doctrine, national security designation, sovereign immunity. If Congress opens an inquiry, the government can stall, reveal partial, false, or incomplete responses, seal, or redact documents, even sue Congress over its probing. But for Congress to initiate an investigation, it usually requires a media story. “Congressional offices have told me so. They often ask, ‘Has the news reported on it.’ It is astounding — it’s like saying that they need a news story to be forced into doing their jobs,” says Pearson. “Supposedly, we have three co-equal branches of government, but both Congress and the judiciary have conceded enormous power to the Executive. The whole constitutional checks and balances thing doesn’t work. These are smart people, but I don’t think that many of them understand this on a fundamental level. They are giving so much of their power away, especially where it counts the most — secret police and programs that target Americans and systematically violate rights and liberties. Finally, these programs exclusively rely on plausible deniability, deflecting blame and responsibility, often on the victim in the form of a mental illness label or “down on his luck”. In the case of Myron May, they used the torture that they were doing against him and May’s response (e.g., moving, research) as evidence of his insanity. The man was being stalked and tortured. F\*\*\*ing ridiculous, these people.”_

**2\. \*\*Arrest without charge or warrant\*\* — detention based on suspicion, denunciation, or political threat alone**

_This is a major deviation from Nazi Germany. The US does not routinely arrest without a charge or warrant, but what the Gestapo police does is more subtle. In my case, they made up a witness out of thin air. I was there. I knew who was there and who assaulted me. The police just lied. Plain and simple. The prosecutor didn’t pursue the charge, but can you imagine this happening in the US — to a PhD holder with no criminal record. Astounding.”_

**3\. \*\*Detention without trial\*\* — indefinite holding, no habeas corpus, no judicial review**

_This is the most crucial part of the US Gestapo wants to avoid — triggering constitutional democratic levers such as the victim’s right to counsel and access to a judge. It doesn’t want a case to appear before a judge that raises these sorts of questions — was their federal involvement? What was its legal basis? Is victim’s targeting part of a program?_

**4\. \*\*Torture and coercive interrogation\*\* — systematic, institutionalized, not aberrational**

_I was tortured in the United States — Washington, DC. no less. through a multifaceted approach designed to be invisible to traditional law enforcement and medical systems:_

*   _Directed Energy Effects: Pearson reports experiencing physical forces with no visible source, such as the sensation of being pinned against a wall or feeling an external “spatial desire” to walk toward specific locations._
*   _Acoustic & Electromagnetic Weapons: He suspects the use of high-powered microwave systems, pulsed radio frequency emitters, and directed acoustic weapons, which he believes the NSA and FBI are equipped to monitor._
*   _“Street Theater”: A psychological tactic involving clusters of people — often wearing red and black — acting out coordinated “scripts” in his vicinity to signal that he is under constant surveillance._
*   _Psychological Infiltration: Incidents like finding “synchronized” behaviors during the Cherry Blossom Festival or discovering unexpected objects, such as a Sprite bottle in a bag he never opened._

* * *

### STRONGEST PARALLELS — Documented & Institutionalized

**#6 — Mass surveillance of the general population** The most clear-cut parallel. NSA bulk collection programs (PRISM, Section 215 metadata collection), exposed by Snowden in 2013, revealed surveillance of virtually all Americans’ phone and internet data. Section 702 of FISA was reauthorized in 2024 with _expanded_ provisions allowing warrantless searches of Americans’ communications. This is not disputed.

**#34 & #35 — Social media monitoring and facial recognition** DHS, FBI, and local law enforcement systematically monitor social media. Facial recognition is deployed by dozens of federal agencies and hundreds of police departments, often with no legislative authorization or oversight framework.

**#19 & #20 — Physical surveillance and mail interception** The Mail Isolation Control and Tracking program photographs the exterior of every piece of US mail — billions of pieces annually. FBI physical surveillance of domestic activists is well documented, including of Black Lives Matter organizers, environmental protesters, and Muslim communities.

**#7 — Informant networks embedded in civilian life** The FBI’s use of paid informants — particularly inside Muslim-American communities and left-wing activist groups — is extensively documented and litigated. **#36 & #37 — Emergency powers kept permanently active / vague national security statutes** The Authorization for Use of Military Force (AUMF) passed in 2001 remains in effect 25 years later, granting sweeping executive power.
