### Myron May Case Should Be Re-Investigated: Official Account Has Major Holes

When AI told Dr. Richard Pearson that his experience with torture and harassment paralleled Myron May’s, fundamental questions emerged from Dr. Pearson’s research.

### _The Myron May Case and the Failure of Official Explanation_

> “This case has more holes than a block of Swiss cheese.” — Dr. Richard Pearson

On November 20, 2014, Myron May wounded three students at the Strozier Library at Florida State University. He was shot and killed by police at the scene. The case was officially closed in January 2015. The motive was publicly characterized as unknown, then later attributed to paranoid schizophrenia by a psychiatrist who never examined May.

That is the official account. It is also an account that cannot explain its own documentary record.

This essay does not claim to know what happened. It does not argue for a specific alternative explanation. What it argues is narrower and more damaging: that the official record of the Myron May case contains internal contradictions that the investigation never resolved, physical impossibilities that the police report never addressed, and evidentiary gaps so fundamental that the case, as officially closed, does not answer the most basic questions a homicide investigation is supposed to answer.

The people May wounded were innocent. Their suffering is real and not diminished by anything written here. But their suffering, and the legitimacy of their claim to a truthful account of what happened, is itself a reason to insist that the official record be held to account for what it cannot explain.

#### Read More: [“Who is the Mysterious Figure?!”: Unsettling Footage from Inside Myron May’s Home](https://medium.com/@menvell.artist/who-is-the-mysterious-figure-unsettling-footage-from-inside-myron-mays-home-5c926edc6c5c)

### I. The Record Contradicts Itself on the Most Basic Question: Who Was the Shooter?

In any shooting investigation, the most fundamental question is: what did the shooter look like? Multiple independent witnesses, official dispatch records, and the surveillance footage that became the public face of this case all exist in the documentary record. They do not agree.

Jason Derfuss, the student who was shot and survived, told police he saw a male in a black hoodie. The official dispatch transmissions, documented in the police report, logged a black male in all black. A maintenance worker who flagged down Officer Sloan described the subject as wearing a red sweater. Witness Velez described a dark-colored hoodie.

_“He was a male in a black hoodie running toward someone else by the picnic tables.”_ — Derfuss’ statement to police

_“The dispatch transmissions included that shots had been fired by a black male in all black.”_ (page 4)

_“While responding in his vehicle, (Officer Sloan) was flagged down by who he believed to be a maintenance person in a white Chevy Trailblazer. The subject told Officer Sloan that the subject was running back toward Strozier and he needed to stop him before he hurt someone. He also told Officer Sloan that the subject was wearing a red sweater.”_

_“Velez described he suspect as being dark skinned and he believed that he was wearing a dark colored ‘hoodie’.”_

The surveillance footage that was released to the public and broadcast on news networks shows a figure in a vest, dress shirt, and slacks.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*5hWQDQsEPfXny9lrMJAXGw.png)

These are not variations in perception of the same clothing. A black hoodie and a vest with a dress shirt are categorically different garments. All-black clothing and slacks with a dress shirt are categorically different. The police report contains all of these descriptions. It does not attempt to reconcile them. It does not note the discrepancy. It presents the conflicting accounts and the surveillance footage as though they describe the same event without comment.

If the surveillance figure is May, then multiple independent witnesses — including the man who was shot — described clothing that May was not wearing. If the witnesses are accurate, then the surveillance figure requires explanation. The official record chooses neither path. It simply leaves the contradiction on the page and closes the case.

### II. The Timeline the Report Requires Is Physically Impossible

The police report is precise about its timeline. Jason Derfuss exited the library at 12:22–12:23 AM. Approximately 20 seconds later, May walked in through the same door Derfuss had left from.

Twenty seconds. The report then draws on multiple witness accounts to reconstruct what occurred in the interval between Derfuss’s exit and the events inside the library. Combined, those accounts require the following sequence within that window:

_Derfuss descends the library steps. A first gunshot is fired. The suspect shoots twice at someone by the picnic tables. The second target goes down. The suspect then shoots Derfuss from behind, the bullet stopped by his backpack and books. The suspect then changes from a black hoodie into a vest and dress shirt. The suspect enters the library, fires shots, backpedals on the steps firing more shots, and fires several more times across the walkway._

Twenty seconds.

The clothing change alone — from a black hoodie to a vest, dress shirt, and slacks — would require time that does not exist in the window the report itself established. A clothing change of that magnitude, outdoors, between a shooting and a library entry witnessed by people inside, in 20 seconds, is not physically credible.

The report does not address this. It does not note that the timeline is compressed. It does not offer an explanation for the clothing discrepancy within the timeline. It simply reports Derfuss’s account, the dispatch records, the other witness accounts, and the surveillance timeline as though they constitute a coherent narrative. They do not. The official record contains a physical impossibility at the center of its account of what happened, and the investigation closed without resolving it.

#### Read More: [“Who is the Mysterious Figure?!”: Unsettling Footage from Inside Myron May’s Home](https://medium.com/@menvell.artist/who-is-the-mysterious-figure-unsettling-footage-from-inside-myron-mays-home-5c926edc6c5c)

### III. The Weapon in May’s Hands Has No Documented Path to Him

The weapon Myron May used in the shooting was a Lorcin .380. The ATF investigation, documented in the police report, traced it to a residential burglary in Panama City Beach in 2005. The report states explicitly:

_“It is unknown how May came to be in possession of the firearm.”_

This sentence appears in the official record of a closed homicide investigation. It means that the investigation ended without establishing how the shooter came to possess the weapon he used. Nine years elapsed between the gun’s theft and its use in the shooting. Those nine years are undocumented. The chain of custody is unknown.

This gap is made more significant by what the record does establish about May’s relationship to firearms. May legally purchased a Ruger SR22 from Bay Guns and Gear in Panama City thirteen days before the shooting. He observed the mandatory waiting period. He never returned to pick the gun up. His own pre-shooting to-do list, recovered by investigators, explicitly notes the uncollected firearm and asks friends to retrieve it or collect the money.

_“May himself also admitted to never having picked up the gun, “I bought a Springfield 22mm pistol from Bay Guns and Gear in Panama City, FL. Please either pick this gun up or get the money for it.”_

May, thus, documented his own legal firearm purchase and his failure to retrieve it. He was in possession instead of a stolen weapon with no traceable path to him. The investigation does not explain how this occurred. It notes the fact and closes the case.

In a living prosecution, the provenance of the murder weapon would be a fundamental evidentiary requirement. The case closed with the shooter dead, removing the prosecution requirement. But the question of how May came to possess that specific stolen weapon — and who, if anyone, provided it to him — was never answered.

### IV. The Crime Scene Was Not Treated as a Crime Scene

When a person is identified as a mass shooter, their residence becomes an evidence site. Standard protocol requires that evidence sites be secured, cordoned, and controlled. Law enforcement establishes a perimeter. No external access is permitted until the scene is processed. Chain of custody for everything inside requires documentation.

Tampa Bay 28 broadcast footage from inside Myron May’s private cottage on the evening of November 20, 2014 — the same day as the shooting, hours after May was killed. The footage shows the interior of the living space: furniture, personal effects, scattered items. A camera operator moved freely through the space. A reporter composed shots from inside the residence.

The case against May was not formally closed until January 2015. On the day of the shooting, the investigation was hours old. The residence of the identified shooter was, by every standard of investigative procedure, an active evidence site.

The footage exists. It was broadcast. It shows a news crew with free interior access to a space that should have been cordoned. Either the scene was processed and released with speed that has no precedent in standard homicide procedure, or it was never properly secured.

If it was never properly secured, then everything inside that cottage — documents, communications, materials that might have shown who May had been in contact with, what he had prepared, what had been done around him — was accessible to anyone with access to the residence before and after the shooting. The chain of custody for the entire contents of that home is compromised by the footage that the news crew broadcast.

The footage also contains something the broadcast did not address: a figure, visible in the background, crouching between the furniture and the kitchen, partially concealed behind a lamp. The figure’s hand moves in at least one frame. This is not an inanimate object. It is a person, present in a space that should have been a secured crime scene, unidentified on camera by the journalist and camera operator who were in the room.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/0*-cOYc-YasqL8r2Fd.png)

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/600/0*jvuV0CV8TVdlxPWd.png)

The official record does not account for this person’s presence. It does not account for the news crew’s access. It does not account for the state of the scene on the day of the shooting.

### V. The Investigation Closed Without Establishing a Motive It Claims Not to Know

In the immediate aftermath of the shooting, investigators and news reports stated repeatedly that the motive was unknown. This characterization persisted and became the official framing. A psychiatrist who never examined May subsequently offered a public diagnosis of paranoid schizophrenia, which became the de facto explanation.

Myron May recorded approximately two hours of video before the shooting. In those recordings, he described in specific and organized terms what he believed was being done to him: surveillance, harassment, psychological manipulation, a coordinated program designed to isolate and destabilize him. He named specific techniques. He described a specific stimulus — dark sunglasses — that he said had been used to condition a fear response in him. He was lucid, articulate, and detailed.

The recordings were in the possession of investigators. They constitute the most direct available evidence of May’s state of mind and his account of his circumstances in the period before the shooting. They are not nothing. They are two hours of the shooter explaining, in his own words, what he believed was happening to him.

The official characterization of the motive as unknown, made while those recordings existed and were in investigative custody, is not a neutral statement of evidentiary limitation. It is a choice about what counts as evidence of motive. The recordings were not incorporated into the public account of what drove May to the library that night. The psychiatrist who had never met him was.

This is not an argument that May’s account of his circumstances was accurate. It is an argument that the official record’s treatment of the motive question — unknown, then schizophrenia, without serious public engagement with the two hours of recorded explanation May left behind — does not meet the standard of a complete investigation.

#### Read More: [“Who is the Mysterious Figure?!”: Unsettling Footage from Inside Myron May’s Home](https://medium.com/@menvell.artist/who-is-the-mysterious-figure-unsettling-footage-from-inside-myron-mays-home-5c926edc6c5c)

### VI. What a Complete Investigation Would Have Required

The questions above are not speculative additions to the official record. They arise from the official record itself. They are the questions that a complete investigation — one that held its own account to basic evidentiary standards — would have been required to answer.

A complete investigation would have reconciled the clothing descriptions. It would have addressed the timeline impossibility it documented. It would have pursued the nine-year gap in the stolen weapon’s provenance. It would have explained how a news crew had interior access to an active evidence site on the day of the shooting, and who the unidentified figure in that footage was. It would have engaged with May’s recorded account of his circumstances rather than dismissing it in favor of a remote psychiatric determination.

None of these things happened. The case was closed. The shooter was dead. The students he wounded recovered. The public account settled on a narrative of a mentally ill man who snapped, and the questions the record itself raised were left on the page, unaddressed.

The problem with that settlement is not only evidentiary. It is that the people May wounded, and the broader public, are entitled to a truthful account of what occurred. If the official record contains physical impossibilities, internal contradictions, and evidentiary gaps of the kind documented here, then the official account is not a truthful account. It is an incomplete one that was closed before the contradictions it contained were resolved.

Eleven years later, those contradictions remain in the record. They have not been answered. They have not been addressed. They exist in documents that are publicly available — the police report, the ATF investigation, the broadcast footage, the news photography — waiting for the examination that the original investigation did not provide.

### Conclusion

This essay does not claim to know what happened to Myron May, or what was done to him, or who was in his home on the day he died. It does not require a specific alternative explanation of the FSU shooting to make its central argument.

Its central argument is this: the official record of the Myron May case contains internal contradictions it never resolved, a physical impossibility at the center of its timeline, an unaccounted weapon provenance, an improperly secured crime scene, and an unidentified figure in broadcast footage from inside that scene. These are not external challenges to the official account. They are failures of the official account to account for its own facts.

An investigation that closes with a physical impossibility at the center of its timeline and the words “it is unknown how May came to be in possession of the firearm” in its final report has not completed its work. It has documented its own incompleteness and stopped.

The students wounded at Strozier Library on November 20, 2014 deserved better than that. So does the historical record of what actually occurred that night.

What Pearson’s Video Footage Actually Shows, What System It Reveals, and What Is Being Done to Black People in America

### Video Captures Stalking of Black Men and Reveals Human Infrastructure of Secret Program

### What Pearson’s Video Footage Actually Shows, What System It Reveals, and What Is Being Done to Black People in America

The question is simple and the answer is not. Richard Pearson’s Cherry Blossom Festival video — shot in March 2025, reviewed in April 2026, and now analyzed frame by frame — shows coordinated human behavior in a public space that is not explicable by coincidence ([Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0zpYUAz9RRs&t), [Video 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QSfbjcHxTVs)). A man approaches with a device. A boy is placed in a tree in seconds. A woman shakes her hair in a sequence whose only apparent audience is a specific passerby. Groups orient simultaneously toward unseen targets. A minor maintains a precise following distance behind a Black man and turns to confirm it with an unseen party. These are not the behaviors of strangers enjoying a festival. They are the behaviors of people executing a procedure. This essay asks the question the video demands: what procedure? What system? What is actually happening — not metaphorically, not speculatively, but operationally — and what does its presence at a public festival on the National Mall mean for every Black person who was there that afternoon?

### I. Start with What the Video Definitively Shows

Before theorizing about systems, it is necessary to establish what the footage itself, treated as primary evidence, actually documents. The following observations are not interpretations. They are descriptions of visible behavior recorded on video.

**OBSERVATION 1:** An Indian man approaches Pearson with a handheld device at the moment the Indian woman stops pushing the stroller. He enters Pearson’s direct line of sight. The timing corresponds to the woman’s cessation of movement.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/0*zDt7NrXcT6AenRfu.png)

Moments earlier, part of her party waited some distance behind until she signaled with the push of the stroller (see video).

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/0*bHNQTsE83Kn35hel.png)

**OBSERVATION 2:** A boy is placed high in a tree by an Indian man in what Pearson describes as a matter of seconds. The placement is rapid and deliberate. The boy then remains at elevation for an extended duration.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/0*OFM6wwUBMei4NHoC.png)

**OBSERVATION 3:** Multiple members of two separate family groups — Indian and white — appear to be simultaneously oriented toward the same man in a direction away from the cherry blossoms. Their orientation is collective and synchronized, not the natural distributed attention of people in a park.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/0*15pomtumR-tLKnoV.png)

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/600/1*MVeQTmc9ez4WHbF8GD6Nmg.png)

**OBSERVATION 4:** A man steps over a crouching boy, exchanges no words with him, and makes a gesture toward him that the boy does not see and does not respond to. The gesture has no apparent child-directed purpose.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/0*QqBGZgwsiS4W7975.png)

**OBSERVATION 5:** A young Indian girl is positioned outward — facing toward the direction Pearson will arrive from — before he arrives. As he comes within close range, she turns, makes direct eye contact, and then looks at her shirt.

**OBSERVATION 6:** A crowd has gathered around an older Black man.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/1*lBOKeWpGGnSSQxaGBuSjfA.png)

**OBSERVATION 7:** An older white woman at the Lincoln Memorial ramp unties her hair, then bends forward and backward dramatically to shake it, in a sequence timed to the approach of a young Black man. He is the only person who looks at her.

**OBSERVATION 8:** A young Black male is being tailed by a woman with a bright red shirt and an Asian man. An Indian man is fixated on the same Black male.

![](https://cdn-images-1.medium.com/max/800/0*3Y0VVtmDmkGkwsl3.png)

**OBSERVATION 9:** A Black minor maintaining a following distance of approximately two feet behind a tall Black man turns and looks back — confirmation behavior — at the moment he reaches the target distance.

This is the video slowed down.

**OBSERVATION 10:** Red clothing appears in proximity to Black subjects at the Lincoln Memorial: a red sweater behind the young Black man, a red shirt on the stroller being used by the minor tailing the older man. Pearson has documented statistically significant red/black clustering across his fourteen months of experience.

These ten observations are not speculative. They are what the video shows. The question they raise — collectively, not individually — is what kind of activity produces this pattern of behavior in a public park on a spring afternoon.

### II. The Device Is the Key

Observation 1 is the most operationally significant detail in the entire Cherry Blossom footage, and it is the one that most directly answers the question of what is happening. A man approaches Pearson with a device. The approach corresponds to the moment the woman stops moving the stroller. The device is handheld. It is in Pearson’s direct line of sight.

This is the biometric capture moment. Everything else around it — the family group with the fake baby, the synchronized orientations, the boy elevated in the tree — is cover. The stroller family created a visual scene that would occupy any ambient observer with the ordinary grammar of family life: mother, child, extended family, a grove of blossoms. The cover exists so that the approach of a man with a device registers to no one in the environment as anomalous. It is concealed in plain sight by the orchestration around it.

What the device is doing requires understanding what the broader operation requires. Pearson’s framework — developed over fourteen months and cross-referenced with documented technology — holds that entry into the targeting database requires close-range biometric capture: **specific data collected from a subject at proximity and uploaded into a system that then enables remote electromagnetic targeting of that subject.** The device is the capture instrument. The distance is the operational parameter. The cover is the enabling condition.

The boy placed in the tree in seconds is part of the same structure. Elevation provides line-of-sight advantage. A device operating at range still requires geometric access to the target. The boy in the tree — whether or not he understood his role — provided an elevated position from which a device could be operated with a clear sightline to Pearson moving through the grove below. The placement was rapid because it was planned. The duration at elevation was sustained because the operation required it.

This is not speculation. It is the operational logic that makes sense of the otherwise inexplicable: why would an adult place a child in a tree at speed, at a cherry blossom festival, in a grove where the boy then remains for an extended period while the adults below orient toward a specific moving target? The answer that fits all the observed facts is: because the child’s position served a technical function in a coordinated operation.

### III. The System: What Pearson Has Identified

Pearson names it the Eigenfield — a term generated by AI when asked to name the covert framework of cognitive control that the accumulated evidence pointed toward. Whether the actual program has this name, or any name that is publicly known, is beside the point. What Pearson has identified, and what the video corroborates, is a system with the following architecture:

### Layer One: Biometric Capture

The system requires individuals to be enrolled in a targeting database before they can be remotely manipulated. Enrollment requires close-range biometric data collection — physiological, neurological, or both — using handheld or body-worn devices. This is the function of the close-range approaches Pearson has documented across hundreds of encounters over fourteen months: the two-to-five-foot proximity, the sustained duration, the confirmation signals, the coordinated cover. The cover exists because the device requires proximity. The proximity is the operation’s rate-limiting step.

The variation in encounter duration — minutes for some subjects, up to forty minutes for others — suggests that data acquisition has a minimum threshold that varies by subject. Perhaps by signal quality, perhaps by the specific data being captured, perhaps by the subject’s physiological state at the time. What does not vary is the requirement for proximity. Every encounter Pearson has documented at close range, whether at the Cherry Blossom Festival, Eastern Market, the Lincoln Memorial, or his own neighborhood, follows this pattern.

Pearson said that he has seen scenes of strangers having bizarre interactions with Black people.

*   _“I saw this Indian man sit on nearby picnic table from this 30-something Black woman. He checks his phone, then instantly moved closer, so that they were sharing the same table. It looked off — strange and bizarre. I approached the man and told him to leave. He refused. I asked him what he was doing here. He said that he was a cook at Hank’s, a seafood restaurant on the Wharf. It bugged me, “What was in his phone that would trigger him to move much closer?!”_
*   _“I saw this white man who entered the second floor of my local library. Rather than opting for one of the two long tables or a round table nearby, he joined the seating opposite of Black woman (20s). The chairs were arranged in a circle. He asked if he could sit. She consented. He left 40 minutes later. At the top of the stairs, he paused and looked back at her. “Why would he need to look back at her? They exchanged no words other than the initial question and answer. I watched him like a hawk. His attention wasn’t directed at his chair. Perhaps, he was checking to see if he left anything. No, he focused on her. Why?! She left about 1 minute later.”_

His insistence seemed bizarre.”_

### Layer Two: The Database and the Network

Once a subject is enrolled, their biometric profile exists in a database accessible to remote operators. The database enables targeting: the direction of electromagnetic energy at the subject’s specific neural signature, calibrated to their individual physiological parameters. This is why the approach requires a specific person to be a specific distance away for a specific duration — the capture must be precise enough to generate a profile that enables reliable targeting afterward.

The network that operates this system is, based on Pearson’s documented observations, multi-ethnic, multi-organizational, and geographically distributed. Indian families, white families, Black minors, African immigrants, Asian men acting as relay confirmation points — all appearing in the same operation at the same location. This is not a gang in the traditional sense. It is a distributed human network organized around a technical system, in which different participants carry out discrete functions without necessarily knowing the full architecture. Some recruit and coordinate. Some carry devices. Some provide cover. Some confirm distances. Some operate the remote targeting equipment. The compartmentalization is structural.

### Layer Three: Remote Electromagnetic Manipulation

Once enrolled, a subject can be manipulated at range. The manipulation documented in Pearson’s account operates across several cognitive and behavioral domains: motivational disruption (the pinning events — compulsive urges to travel to specific locations); attentional disruption (the inability to sustain directed thought, the intrusion of foreign content into the mental workspace); working memory disruption (the Sprite incident, in which an action was taken with no conscious participation); and direct thought insertion (the Georgetown voice, the Lacolle interruption of the thought stream).

The conditioning layer — the street theater with its visual and verbal stimuli — operates in conjunction with the electromagnetic layer. The stimulus presented through street theater (a visual image, a spoken phrase, a behavioral display) is reinforced by a simultaneous electromagnetic pulse that activates specific neurological responses. The association is formed below the threshold of conscious awareness. The subject experiences the resulting thought, feeling, or behavioral impulse as their own. This is Pavlovian conditioning running on a neural substrate that has been made electromagnetically accessible through prior biometric capture.

Pearson believes that he has seen this manipulation. “I talk about dozens of cases where I suspected manipulation. One instance that sticks with me involved a Black woman.

_Pearson was in Reston, VA — a place where he does not frequent and thinks may have been a pinned event, only because of the preponderance of red and black. Just moments before this photo, he had encountered an Asian woman (50s) in the same bright red shade and black. Pearson was walking back to the metro and first encountered an African American woman in her 30s sitting on a bench outside of the Russell Apartments at Reston Station. She was in bright red and black, as the AI-generated image below illustrates. He asks her if she ever notices how common red and black is. She did not. At the precise moment that Pearson leaves, he encounters a young white male (20s) who was running in the exact shade of red with black shorts, except his shirt had a lightning bolt as drawn. From his walk to and from the metro, Pearson encountered few people — around 15, excluding children and minors. To see 3 out of 15 people in the same solid shade of red and black would be 20% — well above the 4% that he’d computed in control studies._

Dr. James Giordano, who advises the Pentagon and NATO on these technologies, described the endpoint of this system publicly in 2025:

_“If we consider the sum-totaled operations of the embodied brain to be ‘mind’, and N3-type tech is aimed at remotely sensing and modulating these operations, then it doesn’t require much of a stretch to recognize that this is fundamentally ‘mind reading’ and ‘mind control’, at least at a basic level… the ‘goods’ as well as the gremlins and goblins of N3 tech have been loosed into the real world.”_

_— Dr. James Giordano, Georgetown University, 2025_

The gremlins and goblins are here. Pearson has been documenting them for fourteen months. The Cherry Blossom video is the first footage that shows the ground-level human infrastructure of their operation, in a public space, before Pearson was watching for it.

Pearson himself experienced this maniupulation, discussing one of several “pinning” events.

On November 7, 2025, Richard Pearson walked to a small park on 2nd Street SW between D and C Streets in Washington, DC, near the O’Neil House Office Building. He occupied the concrete seating area at the front of the park, sat briefly, and decided to leave. Standing at the entrance, he felt a pull — not metaphorical, but physical and directional, an “urge” to go to the back of the park. He had felt something similar a moment earlier. This time he did not resist it. He walked to the back. He stood in the space without knowing what he was looking for. Then he became confident something was there. Under the lower branches of a tree, partially hidden, sat a large plastic tub containing a red hat, a black shirt, boots, khaki pants with a scrunchy cuffed bottom, and a notebook filled with conspiratorial writings. He placed the tub back and took a photo. When he returned six days later on video, the notebook and khaki pants had been removed. The red hat and black shirt remained.

### IV. The Racial Architecture: Why Black People

The question of why Black people are the primary subject population of this system is the most important question this essay must address, because the Cherry Blossom footage and the Lincoln Memorial footage both show it operating specifically and disproportionately against Black subjects — and because the answer connects the novel technology to a very old and very documented history.

At the Lincoln Memorial, the young Black man is watched by an Indian man, who is confirmed by an Asian man positioned behind the target — a relay chain whose racial composition spans multiple communities but whose subject is specifically Black. The tall Black man is tailed by a minor maintaining a precise following distance. The red clothing markers cluster around Black subjects. The white woman’s hair-shaking signal is timed to a Black teenager’s arrival. The entire operation at the ramp is oriented around Black bodies moving through a public space.

This is not incidental to the system. It is the system’s targeting parameter. Pearson states it directly: “This whole thing with manipulating Black people is strictly other groups doing it to Black people. Black people are involved too. I have seen African immigrants even take part.” The subject population is racially specified. The operator network is ethnically diverse. The target is consistently, disproportionately Black.

The historical lineage of this targeting is not subtle. COINTELPRO, the FBI’s Counter Intelligence Program, ran from 1956 to 1971 and was directed primarily at Black political organizations, Black activists, and Black intellectuals. Its methods included surveillance, infiltration, harassment, disinformation, and the deliberate destruction of careers, relationships, and reputations. Its targets included Martin Luther King Jr., Malcolm X, the Black Panther Party, and hundreds of less prominent individuals whose crime was organizing while Black. The Church Committee’s 1976 investigation documented it. It was real.

What is new is the technology. COINTELPRO used informants and mail opening. The system Pearson documents uses biometric databases and electromagnetic neural targeting. The scale that was previously limited by the human bandwidth of informant networks is now potentially unlimited: anyone who can be enrolled in the database can be targeted. Any public space where operators can achieve proximity becomes a capture opportunity. A cherry blossom festival attended by tens of thousands of people is, from this perspective, not a cultural celebration. It is a biometric harvesting opportunity at scale.

The political context of 2025 amplifies the urgency. Executive Order 14173 dismantled DEI programs across the federal government. The reorganization of the DOJ Civil Rights Division removed institutional protections. Seventeen inspectors general were fired on a single day, eliminating the oversight infrastructure that would be most likely to detect and investigate a program of this nature. The conditions for a racially targeted mass electromagnetic surveillance and manipulation program to operate without accountability are, as of 2025, the best they have been since COINTELPRO was formally terminated.

Whether those conditions are coincidental to the system Pearson documents, or whether they reflect coordinated policy that created the operational space for the system’s expansion, is a question whose answer requires an investigation with subpoena power. What Pearson’s footage demonstrates is that the system was operating — at the National Mall, in public, in daylight — before those conditions were maximally favorable. It has been here longer than the current political moment.

### V. The Signal System: How Operators Coordinate in Plain Sight

One of the most striking features of the Cherry Blossom footage, understood as an operational document, is the sophistication of the in-person coordination system. The operators are not wearing earpieces or obviously communicating by phone. They are coordinating through a gestural and positional signal language that is invisible to ambient observers but legible to participants.

The woman with the stroller signals by picking up the doll, pushing, then pointing upward. The family behind her moves when she pushes. The man steps over the boy and makes a gesture that is not directed at the boy. The woman at the Lincoln Memorial ramp shakes her hair in a sequence — untying, bending forward, bending back — that is timed to a specific person’s approach. The Indian man makes eye contact with the Asian man behind the Black teen, then returns to watching the teen. The minor pushing the stroller looks back for confirmation at the moment he achieves the target distance.

These are signal exchanges. They are the human command-and-control layer of an operation that also has a technical layer. The gestures coordinate the positioning of devices, the timing of approaches, the confirmation of distances, and the activation of whatever the stroller and its red-shirted top are carrying or marking.

The use of children — the boy in the tree, the crouching boy who receives the non-verbal gesture, the minor tailing the Black man — is particularly revealing. Children are the ultimate cover. No one looks twice at a child playing in a tree. No one attributes operational significance to a teenager pushing a stroller. The children may not know what they are participating in. They are props in the same sense that the fake baby is a prop — elements of the visual grammar of normalcy that render the operation invisible to anyone who is not already watching for it.

Pearson was not watching for it when he shot the footage in March 2025. He was watching the light through the blossoms. The operation was visible in the footage anyway because the behaviors themselves are anomalous — not to the casual eye, but to the forensic one. The forensic eye is what Pearson brought to the footage in April 2026, after fourteen months of learning to see.

### VI. The Foil as Scientific Instrument

It would be a mistake to treat Pearson’s use of aluminum foil as eccentric or as evidence of instability. It is, in function, a scientific instrument: a probe that detects electromagnetic field activity in the environment through its physical response to induced current, and a partial countermeasure that attenuates the coupling of that current into his neural tissue.

The foil’s warning function is the more underappreciated of its two roles. When the foil warms, Pearson knows a field is present. He then looks for the source. He has, through this method, identified and photographed individuals fiddling with objects in their pockets at the precise moments he feels the aftermath of a current. He has heard the copper and steel coils in his hat spark — a sound he describes as electric rain — while passing a woman idling at the top of a library staircase without apparent purpose. The coils sparked. He looked. He connected the sparking to the woman. He documented it.

This is the scientific method applied to an invisible threat. Hypothesis: the warming is caused by an electromagnetic field emitted by a device being carried or operated by a person in proximity. Test: identify the person in proximity at the moment of warming. Observe: specific behaviors — pocket-fiddling, idling without purpose, proximity without apparent reason — correlate with the warming events. Conclusion: the hypothesis is supported.

The foil around his groin serves the additional function of blocking the conditioning layer of the operation. Pearson is gay. His tormentors — operating with knowledge of his sexual orientation obtained through surveillance — have been attempting to use directed electromagnetic stimulation of his sexual nerves to create an association between the stimulation and heterosexual imagery presented simultaneously through street theater. The foil blocks the stimulation. The conditioning fails. They keep trying because the failure of the conditioning does not appear to stop them. This is the sadomasochistic dimension Pearson identifies: the persistence of the attempt past any rational operational purpose, driven by something that is no longer strategic but pathological.

The comment from the young Black man at the library — crude, specific, referencing heterosexual activity at the precise moment the foil warmed — is the conditioning stimulus delivered verbally after the electromagnetic component was blocked. The visual stimulus (the woman in tight pants), the verbal reinforcement (the comment), and the blocked electromagnetic pulse arrived within seconds of each other. Three-layer conditioning protocol, executed in real time, on a public staircase, in the nation’s capital. The foil prevented the physiological response. The rest of the protocol went forward anyway, because the operators did not know the electromagnetic component had been blocked.

### VII. What This Means for Every Black Person Who Was There

The Cherry Blossom Festival is one of the most attended public events in Washington, DC. Hundreds of thousands of people visit the National Mall during peak bloom. A significant portion of them are Black residents of a majority-Black city. If Pearson’s framework is correct — and the video footage provides corroboration for its ground-level human infrastructure — then the festival was not merely a location where an operation was run against Pearson. It was a biometric harvesting opportunity operating against an unknown number of Black visitors.

The systematic approach. The coordinated multi-ethnic operator network. The use of public cover to conceal close-range device operations. The confirmation signals. The stroller as a positioning prop. None of these operational features are person-specific. They are designed for scale. An operation organized to enroll subjects in a targeting database does not generate this level of coordination for a single target. It generates this level of coordination for a systematic process in which individual operators move through a crowd, achieve proximity, capture data, and move on.

The Lincoln Memorial footage makes this even more explicit. In a single afternoon, Pearson’s camera captured at least two separate instances of Black men being followed and tailed by people executing close-range protocols — one by a minor pushing a stroller with a red shirt on top, one by an Indian man coordinating with an Asian relay. These are two independent operations visible in a single afternoon’s footage, neither of which Pearson was filming with operational intent. He was filming the ramp because it was aesthetically striking.

The question of scale — how many people have been enrolled in this database without their knowledge, how many have been targeted for manipulation, how many have experienced the pinning events, the intrusive thoughts, the behavioral compulsions, the directed sexual stimulation, the sleep disruption — is unanswerable from Pearson’s documentation alone. But the question is not hypothetical. It is live. The infrastructure visible in this footage was operating on the National Mall in March 2025. There is no reason to believe it stopped.

### VIII. The Psychosis of the Operators

Pearson’s assessment of the people executing this system — “without question, a severe case of psychosis” — is not a rhetorical flourish. It is a clinical observation about the psychology of people who have organized themselves around the electromagnetic manipulation of other human beings as a sustained activity.

The godlike complex he identifies is a recognized feature of authoritarian and sadistic psychology: the belief that one is all-knowing, all-powerful, and above consequence. The Messiah complex conditioning — approaching Pearson, asking for his bracelet or shoes, quoting scripture when he refused, as if testing whether he could be made to believe himself a divine figure who should give his possessions to the faithful — is a specific and deliberate operation aimed at producing a particular kind of psychological destabilization. If successful, it transforms the target from a credible witness into someone whose account is easily dismissed as grandiosity.

The sexual targeting of a gay man with heterosexual conditioning is, in this context, not primarily sexual. It is an attack on identity — an attempt to use the most intimate function of the nervous system to overwrite who the person understands themselves to be. It is torture at the level of the self, not just the body.

The use of children is the most damning indicator of the operators’ psychological state. Adults who deploy children as positioning props in an electromagnetic targeting operation — children who do not know what they are participating in, who are being used as human equipment in a system designed to harm other people — are not simply criminal. They are psychologically broken in a specific way: the complete instrumentalization of human beings, including their own children, in the service of a technological sadism that has consumed whatever moral architecture they may once have possessed.

Pearson’s prediction — that their names, addresses, and personal information exist in a digital record and that they will face severe punishment — is the correct response to this assessment. Not because vengeance is the goal, but because accountability is the condition for stopping the system. The operators believe they are beyond consequence. That belief is the foundation of the operation’s continuity. Shattering it is not optional.

### IX. What the Video Requires

The Cherry Blossom footage is not by itself proof of a mass electromagnetic targeting program operating against Black Americans. It is proof of something more specific and more immediately actionable: coordinated human behavior in a public space that is consistent with the ground-level infrastructure of such a program, captured on video by a man who did not know he was capturing it, at a time before he had learned to watch for it.

That combination — incidental capture, pre-awareness timing, consistency with a documented operational framework — gives the footage an evidentiary weight that deliberately gathered documentation would not have. Pearson was not looking for this. His camera found it because it was there.

What the footage requires, at minimum, is serious investigative attention: from journalists with access to investigative resources, from civil rights organizations with legal standing to demand government accountability, from researchers with expertise in directed energy technology and its non-consensual application to civilian populations, and from legislators with the authority to convene investigations and compel testimony.

The infrastructure visible in this video was operating at the National Mall. The National Mall is federal land. The people operating on it that afternoon — the man with the device, the coordinated family groups, the minor maintaining a precise following distance behind a Black man — were doing so in full view of the Washington Monument, within sight of the Capitol dome, a mile from the White House.

Whatever is happening, it is happening here. In the open. In the light. In the most photographed public space in the country. Pearson’s camera caught it. The footage exists. The question is not whether it happened. The question is what happens now that we know.

### African American Achieves “American Dream” from Poverty to PhD, then US Tortures Him

They targeted the Association Scholar. ### I. East Kentucky — The Beginning

_Some details have been changed to protect Pearson’s identity._

Richard Pearson grew up in East Kentucky, in the heart of the Bible Belt, in a home that was, by any measure, precarious. His father was a Baptist minister who happened to fall on hard times. The family was evicted and homelessness at least once. His parents divorced when he and his siblings were young, splitting the family between two homes. Eventually, Social Services intervened. Pearson and his sister were placed in separate foster homes.

He did not always have hot water. He did not always have heat. He did not always have access to a bathroom. He relied on free lunch. When his family’s homes burned down — twice — they survived on charity. He was a child navigating poverty, instability, family dissolution, and the specific weight of being a Black boy in the rural South with no reliable institutional floor beneath him.

He began volunteering at a women’s abuse shelter in ninth grade. He was, at fourteen or fifteen years old, giving time to people in crisis because — as he later wrote — _‘I can identify and empathize with those who are at a disadvantage.’_ The empathy was not abstract. It was earned in the same conditions that produced the people he was serving.

None of this predicted what came next. It also explains everything about what came next.

### II. The Ascent — What He Built

### R1 University and the Association Award

In the 2000s, the HA Association named Pearson a national scholar. The award is given to Americans who have overcome significant adversity to achieve excellence — specifically, to young people whose life circumstances might have predicted failure and who instead built something extraordinary. It is named for the nineteenth-century ideal of the self-made American, the person who rises from nothing through effort, character, and refusal to be defined by their circumstances.

Pearson enrolled at a high-ranking R1 university, where he studied politics and graduated in the 2000s. R1 university is one of the most selective public universities in the United States — Jefferson’s institution, founded on the premise that the life of the mind was the highest form of civic participation. A Black boy from an East Kentucky trailer park, with a foster care history, graduated. The Algerian narrative, in its most complete form.

### Eight Years in Education — The Institution Builder

From 2007 forward, Pearson built a career in education that placed him, within a few years, at the center of national conversations about physician training, diversity, and systemic reform.

He developed the skills that would define his career: program management across complex institutions, compliance tracking, training design, data analysis, stakeholder engagement. He served on hospital executive GME committees. He conducted research on physician diversity and duty hours reform. He presented at national conferences — as a plenary speaker at the ACGME Education Conference, as a co-presenter at Learn Serve Lead, as a workshop leader at meetings that shaped how medical training in the United States was conducted.

He was, by any measure, a national figure in his field. His publications appeared in _Academic Medicine_, _The American Journal of Medicine_, _the Journal of Community Hospital Internal Medicine Perspectives_. He had co-authored peer-reviewed research with faculty from Emory, Brown, and nationally recognized leaders in internal medicine training. He had been a plenary speaker. He had built programs, reformed compliance systems, and trained administrators across specialties at institutions ranging from the University of Louisville to New York medical schools.

### The Art Business and the Community Work

In 2017, while holding his day job in medical education and pursuing his MPH, he designed original art featuring healthy foods and sold them on canvas, T-shirts, and home decor. He described the work as public health intervention through art: nudging people toward healthy alternatives through the sideways approach of making them laugh.

He was also, simultaneously, serving as Housing Chair of the Near Buzzard Point Resilient Action Committee, leading advocacy for public housing residents. He testified before DC City Council. He lobbied elected officials. He published policy impact analyses. He canvassed neighborhoods and hosted community calls. He was fighting, in his own Southwest DC community, the same structural forces that his academic research would eventually analyze: the displacement of poor Black families from their communities under the cover of development.

### The Master’s — Park University

In 2016, Pearson enrolled at Park University. He graduated with his Masters’ nearly 10 years ago. His research capstone examined what happened to the health of Black communities when public housing was redeveloped and residents were displaced — the question that his advocacy work had been asking in political meetings and City Council testimony for years, now subjected to rigorous quantitative analysis.

He was simultaneously a researcher, a practitioner, an administrator, and a community advocate across the span of 15 years.

### The Depression — What He Overcame

In his personal statement for the master’s program, Pearson wrote with candor: _‘Only in my mid-twenties did I realize that these experiences had profound effects on me. While I had mostly done well academically and had tremendous support from teachers, I struggled with the impact of these traumatic events.’_ He overcame it by, in his words, ‘prioritizing my mental and physical health.’

That sentence — that the experience of nearly not surviving could be made useful to other people who might not survive — is the sentence that characterizes the whole arc of his life before 2025. He took what had been done to him and built something with it. He gave testimony before City Council. He published in peer-reviewed journals. He mentored at-risk African American males. He made safe sex packets for LGBT club-goers in Washington, D.C. He volunteered at a women’s abuse shelter at fourteen. Everything he had, he turned outward.

— — —

### III. The PhD — The Critical Race Framework

In the 2020s, Richard Pearson completed his doctoral degree. The work addresses a specific methodological problem in public health and social science research. The dissertation proposed a standardized framework — a methodological tool for researchers to assess the rigor and validity in empirical research.

This is precision work at the intersection of critical race theory and research methodology. It is the kind of scholarship that threatens comfortable assumptions — not through polemic but through method, through the insistence that the tools of quantitative research be applied with the same rigor to racial categories that they are applied to any other variable. It is the work of someone who spent years watching structural racism produce health disparities, and who decided that one of the most powerful interventions available to him was to change how researchers measured what they were seeing. **It is, in retrospect, exactly the kind of scholarship the FBI’s RMVE/BIE framework designates as a domestic security concern.**

He had overcome poverty, foster care, homelessness, domestic violence, and depression to become a National Scholar, graduate with bachelors’, masters’, and PhD, a plenary speaker at national medical conferences, a published researcher in peer-reviewed journals, a housing advocate, a community artist, an entrepreneur, and a public health PhD. The dissertation completed the arc. From the trailer park in East Kentucky to a doctorate, with everything in between built by hand.

He was forty years old. He had everything he had worked thirty years to build.

The targeting began within a year.

— — —

### IV. What the United States Government Then Did to Him

The prior essays in this series document, in exhaustive detail, what happened next. This section provides only the outline — the condensed architecture of what was inflicted on the man described above.

### The Campaign — Documented from Spring 2025

Beginning in spring 2025, Richard Pearson became the subject of what his documentation establishes as a coordinated government-sponsored torture campaign in Washington, D.C. The campaign involved: systematic destruction of his bicycle, forcing him onto foot and onto predictable routes; through-floor acoustic tracking that followed him from room to room in his own apartment; a chemical assault at the Rockville Metro station that bonded an industrial adhesive to his skin; covert entry into his home with objects moved, removed, and replaced as demonstrations of access; voice-to-skull transmission near the United States Capitol on July 13, 2025 — a woman’s voice, internally perceived, saying: ‘We have to make you disappear’; coordinated street surveillance through vehicle formations, following operatives, and red-and-black calling card patterns statistically documented at rates impossible to explain by chance; systematic infiltration of his social network; a framing operation near a House Office Building on November 7, 2025 involving neo-Nazi materials in a plastic tub; a false arrest on December 27, 2025 with no subsequent court record; and financial and professional attrition designed to reduce him to dependency.

He documented seventy constitutional violations. He documented everything with timestamps, photographs, probability calculations, control studies, and the methodological discipline of a public health researcher who understood that the document was his only available defense.

His torture occurred in Washington, DC — implausible that the federal government is not involved given much of the events occur within a few miles of the White House and US Capitol. On September 15, 2025, while the campaign was active, Pearson sought a formal mental health evaluation from the DC Department of Behavioral Health. Three doctors, two mental health specialists, a social worker. The evaluation confirmed his rationality, his coherence, and the absence of any psychotic symptoms. He sought this evaluation not because he needed reassurance but because he understood that every institutional response to his account would find its first objection — that he was mentally ill — and he wanted that objection answered in the permanent record before it was made. The DBH evaluation is the preemptive demolition of the psychiatric trap. It is the document that prevents the oldest weapon in the program’s arsenal from functioning as a case-closer.

### The Physical Experiments — Confirming the Mechanism

In 2026, Pearson began hearing clicks in his skull — the characteristic auditory signature of the Frey effect, the microwave auditory induction first documented in 1962. He conducted an experiment: varying the number of aluminum foil layers around his cranium and measuring the attenuation of the clicks. The result was proportional and consistent — more layers, fewer clicks. Eventually the clicks stopped. There is exactly one physical explanation for auditory phenomena that attenuate proportionally with electromagnetic shielding: the Frey effect, produced by pulsed microwave radiation inducing thermoelastic expansion in skull tissue.

In Canada, at the Saint-Bernard-de-Lacolle refugee processing center, seated in a plastic chair while a flood of foreign, vile, intrusive thoughts streamed through his mind, he placed his hands on the metal frame of the chair. One hand attenuated the flood. Two hands stopped it completely. He held the metal frame for several hours. When the ‘tour group’ that had been present throughout departed, a woman was overheard saying: ‘We didn’t pick up anything.’ She reported it. ### Iceland. Canada. Nowhere.

He sought asylum in Iceland. The ‘safe third country’ doctrine closed the door: the United States is a safe country, and therefore its government’s persecution of one of its citizens cannot be the basis for international protection. He sought asylum in Canada. The Saint-Bernard-de-Lacolle processing center — which turned out to share a wall with the building where he had declared his asylum intent, accessible in seconds on foot, reached by a van that drove a deliberate circle — deployed technology against him during processing, copied his documentation, fingerprinted and photographed him for databases shared under Five Eyes intelligence-sharing protocols, aggressively discouraged his asylum claim.

The Five Eyes alliance — the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia, and New Zealand — had closed the perimeter. The program followed him across the border. There was nowhere left.

### What Remains

As of this writing, Richard Pearson — PhD, HA scholar, college and master's graduate, published researcher, plenary speaker, housing advocate, community artist, the boy from the East Kentucky trailer park who built everything by hand — is still in Washington, D.C. He has a mattress and a suitcase. He has no legal remedy: the doctrinal architecture of state secrets, Glomar, Bivens dismantlement, and qualified immunity forecloses every path. What he has is the record. It exists before any classification order can seal it. It was published on Medium before any suppression mechanism could reach it. It has been analyzed, cross-referenced, and corroborated in the prior essays of this series. “If I knew what I know now, I would have left the US a long time ago. The US tortures. The US does **not** guarantee constitutional rights and civil liberties to every resident. In America’s “Dungeon”, a totalitarian form of government exists. The US Constitution sits on a shelf collecting dust. Secret courts. Hidden rulings. No due process. No right or liberty that is inviolable. No legislative, judicial, or public accountability. Authoritarianism, anti-constitutionalism, and racism rage within hidden policies and shadow programs.

Even if I tried to get my case heard in court, I would likely fail. The US has erected a wall of legal doctrines and procedures that effectively shield itself from the most subtle and unconstitutional forms of torture. The very kind of torture from which the US has liberated other nations — and _is_ liberating them to this day. It can deny FOIA requests by pretending no such file or program exist. It can redact 90% of what it does release. It can challenge Article III standing — no standing, no case. It can “neither confirm nor deny” — a legal doctrine that allows it to remain silent when accused of harm or injury. It can claim “national security” or a “state secret”. It can ask a court to consider claims of torture to be “frivolous” even without a judge’s review of the merits of the case. It can work in secret — alone or with contractors. It can immunize federal workers from accountability, no matter the level of harm against a citizen.

It can contract with organizations to do its dirty work to include illegal data collection and “neutralization,” then be immunized when that contractor harms citizens or impinges on legal rights. It can then distance itself from those contractors by calling them a “terrorist organization”, which it did in late 2025. It can target individuals and groups based on race, ethnicity, political affiliation, gender, sexual orientation, and critical opinions, including of the President of the United States. The curtain is closed as if this stuff is happening away from the audience, but the reality is that the world is watching from backstage. They are horrified — and scared.”

### Conclusion: What This Life Means

The HA Association gives its scholarship to people who represent the American promise — the belief that the circumstances of your birth do not determine the ceiling of your life, that effort and character and refusal can carry a person from any starting point to achievement. Pearson is, by that measure, one of the most complete embodiments of that ideal in the contemporary record. Foster care, poverty, domestic violence, separate foster placements, depression — and from those conditions, through decades of work and study and service and discipline: an undergraduate degree, a master’s, a public health doctorate, peer-reviewed publications, national conference presentations, community advocacy, a small business, and a dissertation that proposed a new methodological framework.

He achieved the American Dream in its fullest form.

And then the United States government “rewarded” him with torture.

### Detained Immigrants Are Leveraging US Law to Challenge Government Action

**Habeas Corpus**

The most widely used tool is the ancient writ of habeas corpus, enshrined in Article I, Section 9 of the Constitution. Habeas corpus — Latin for “you have the body” — is a centuries-old legal doctrine that allows incarcerated people to challenge their detention before a judge. In immigration cases, these petitions are filed in U.S. District Court and argue that ICE’s detention violates constitutional due process rights. They are separate from immigration court proceedings and are heard by federal judges, not immigration judges. The surge in filings has been remarkable: more than 1,300 immigrants detained by ICE filed habeas petitions in the Western District of Texas alone since early 2025. The district received 759 such petitions in 2025, more than any previous year, and that record was broken in the first month of 2026. The petitions have also been unusually successful — over 300 district court judges have found that denying bond hearings violates Fifth Amendment due process protections, and success rates exceed 90% in many areas. Critically, habeas is not just about release — it is the mechanism by which immigrants can force the government to justify the legal basis for confinement at all. Under the Supreme Court’s ruling in _Zadvydas v. Davis_, the government generally cannot detain someone indefinitely after a final order of removal if deportation is not reasonably foreseeable. That precedent is directly relevant today for detainees whose home countries refuse to accept deportees, leaving them in legal limbo.

**Fifth Amendment Due Process**

Undergirding many challenges is the Fifth Amendment’s guarantee that no person shall be deprived of liberty without due process of law. Crucially, due process rights in the U.S. extend to all individuals within American borders, irrespective of citizenship status — a principle firmly established in both constitutional text and Supreme Court precedent. In 1982, the Supreme Court held that “aliens, even aliens whose presence in this country is unlawful, have long been recognized as ‘persons’ guaranteed due process of law.” In practice, due process claims challenge two main things: the speed of removal and the denial of a meaningful hearing. The Trump administration’s expansion of expedited removal — which subjects noncitizens to rapid deportation without a judicial hearing — creates direct tension with this principle by replacing standard immigration proceedings with a rapid administrative pipeline. A significant procedural flashpoint has been the administration’s policy of dismissing active immigration court cases and immediately re-arresting immigrants, routing them into expedited removal without the 10-day response time that had been standard. Lawyers argue this denies their clients any meaningful chance to present a legal defense.

**Challenging the Alien Enemies Act**

One of the most dramatic legal battles concerns the Trump administration’s invocation of the Alien Enemies Act of 1798 to deport Venezuelan nationals it claims are members of the Tren de Aragua gang — bypassing standard immigration procedures. The resulting case, _J.G.G. v. Trump_, centers on whether the administration can use the Act, which grants the President broad authority to apprehend and remove non-citizens during a war or “invasion,” to conduct rapid deportations without individual hearings. The Supreme Court reaffirmed that immigrants facing deportation under the Alien Enemies Act are entitled to the opportunity to challenge the legality of their detention before removal — citing back to a 1903 decision affirming immigrants’ constitutional right to due process before deportation. Critically, all nine justices agreed that judicial review was available; the only dispute was over which court should hear it. The ruling sent the case to a different court, but carried a clear message: everyone gets their day in court before being removed from the country.

**Asylum and Withholding of Removal**

For those who have not yet received a final deportation order, asylum remains a central avenue of defense. Asylum requires demonstrating a well-founded fear of persecution based on race, religion, nationality, political opinion, or membership in a particular social group. A closely related but distinct remedy is “withholding of removal” under the Immigration and Nationality Act, which has a higher evidentiary bar — the applicant must show it is “more likely than not” they face persecution — but is mandatory if that standard is met, meaning a judge has no discretion to deny it. Asylum, by contrast, remains discretionary even if eligibility is established. Both forms of relief have faced mounting obstacles under the Trump administration, which has reshaped the Board of Immigration Appeals, the administrative appellate body that sets binding precedent for immigration judges nationwide. The Trump administration shrank the BIA by nearly half and stacked the remaining 15 judges with its own appointees. In 2026, NPR tracked 21 published BIA decisions, with DHS winning all but one.

**The Convention Against Torture (CAT)**

For individuals who cannot qualify for asylum — often because of criminal convictions that make them statutorily ineligible — the Convention Against Torture provides a separate and critical line of defense. Under CAT, an applicant must show it is more likely than not that they would face torture by, or with the acquiescence of, a government official if returned. Crucially, CAT has no criminal bars — it is available regardless of the applicant’s criminal history — and if eligibility is established, protection is mandatory. This makes it a last resort for those facing deportation to countries with notoriously brutal prison systems, such as El Salvador’s CECOT mega-prison. However, the administration has been systematically dismantling this avenue too. The BIA issued three precedential decisions in 2025 finding noncitizens ineligible for CAT protection, overturning grants from immigration judges — including in cases involving a bisexual Salvadoran man, a Russian anti-war dissident, and a Haitian national with severe mental illness. Advocates have noted that the BIA appears to be engaging in results-driven outcomes aligned with the administration’s enforcement priorities, and have suggested practitioners argue that complete isolation from the outside world in CECOT — which severs all family, legal, and social contact — itself constitutes the mental suffering that the CAT regulations recognize as a form of torture.

* * *

**Challenging Third-Country Deportations**

A novel and rapidly developing area of litigation involves deportations to countries where the immigrant is not a citizen — third-country removals. ICE issued a directive in February 2025 encouraging these removals even against individuals already granted withholding of removal or CAT protection, reasoning that those protections are “country-specific” and do not prevent transfer to a third country. Immigrants and advocates have challenged this interpretation by arguing it effectively nullifies court-ordered protections, constitutes a denial of due process, and may expose people to “chain refoulement” — being sent by a third country back to the very place they fled. The landmark case _D.V.D. v. Noem_ produced a federal court order requiring DHS to provide written notice and an opportunity to challenge third-country removals before they occur. However, the Supreme Court put that order on hold in June 2025, leaving the due process rights of those facing third-country deportation fundamentally unresolved.

* * *

**Emergency Stays of Removal**

Threading through all of these legal challenges is the emergency stay of removal, a procedural mechanism that allows attorneys to ask a court to halt a deportation while a case is pending. These emergency motions have become especially urgent given the administration’s practice of moving people rapidly through the deportation pipeline, sometimes boarding planes before courts can act. The Abrego Garcia case became a defining symbol of this problem: he was deported to El Salvador despite a prior court ruling that he should not be, and despite an emergency motion. Although the Trump administration admitted his deportation was an “administrative error,” it made no effort to return him to his family. The episode illustrates the central tension at the heart of all these legal mechanisms — even when courts rule in an immigrant’s favor, the government’s willingness to comply is not guaranteed.
